chapters.title: Chapter 251 | Master Michael
paragraphs: Stargate City was far more complicated than it appeared on the surface.

To ordinary citizens, it was simply an enormous city filled with heroes, awakened individuals, wealthy businessmen, academies, guilds, and countless opportunities. They saw the glittering towers, the bustling streets, the heroes who patrolled the skies. They saw the surface.
But those who truly understood Stargate City knew that its real power rested in the hands of a select few.
Nine families.

They were known collectively as the Nine Great Families of Stargate City. Each possessed enormous wealth, influence, businesses, territories, awakened experts, and generations of accumulated resources. Some controlled important industries. Others had connections reaching into politics, academies, military institutions, and hero organizations.
Even a single one of the Nine Great Families could make ordinary organizations tremble. Together, they practically dominated Stargate City.
Yet even the Nine Great Families weren’t at the top.
There was one organization whose influence overshadowed them all.
The Hero Association.

If the Nine Great Families were nine enormous pillars supporting Stargate City, then the Hero Association was the roof hanging above all of them. Its influence wasn’t limited to Stargate City. It wasn’t even limited to the country.

Branches of the Hero Association existed across the continent, and its influence extended even farther, with branches operating on other continents throughout the world. Countless powerful heroes were registered under it. Resources, techniques, intelligence networks, training facilities, ancient inheritances—the organization had accumulated them for generations.
More importantly, the Hero Association possessed overwhelming strength. Within Stargate City alone, its power was enough to rival the Nine Great Families combined.
That was why, regardless of how arrogant the great families became, none of them openly challenged the authority of the Hero Association.
But where there was order, there would always be those who rejected it.

The Hero Association wasn’t the only extraordinary organization in existence. Far from it. Numerous factions existed beyond its control. Some operated openly. Others remained hidden. And some had been forced underground precisely because the Hero Association was too powerful for them to reveal themselves carelessly.
Among those hidden forces were organizations whose names alone were enough to make experienced heroes uncomfortable.
The Villain Association was one of them.

Unlike ordinary criminals who committed crimes for money, survival, or revenge, those recognized as true villains were frequently awakened individuals who had completely rejected the laws governing society. Some killed. Some experimented on humans. Some destroyed entire communities. Others pursued power regardless of the price.
And among the numerous villain organizations associated with the darker side of the awakened world, there was one name that carried a particularly bloody reputation.
The Golden Snake Syndicate.

They were considered one of the three most dangerous villain factions in the entire country. Not necessarily because they possessed the greatest number of awakened experts. Nor because they controlled the most territory. It was because of what they could supposedly do.
Extract talents.
The Golden Snake Syndicate was rumored to possess a forbidden method capable of forcibly extracting an awakened talent from another person. To them, an awakened individual wasn’t simply an enemy.
They were a resource.
A harvest.

The extracted talent could supposedly be used to strengthen an existing talent or, under certain circumstances, be transferred to someone else. Whether every rumor was true remained uncertain. But enough heroes had disappeared over the years for people within the awakened world to fear the possibility.

It was also precisely why the Golden Snake Syndicate attracted so many villains. Power was everything to people like them. And if power could be stolen? There would always be someone willing to steal it.

Human lives meant little to the Syndicate. Enemies were resources. Captives were resources. Sometimes, even their own members were nothing more than resources waiting to be consumed by someone more valuable.
That ruthlessness had earned them enemies everywhere. Especially within the Hero Association. Yet somehow, despite numerous attempts to destroy them, the Golden Snake Syndicate continued to survive.
Of course, the world wasn’t divided simply between heroes and villains.

There were other factions. Organizations that didn’t care about justice. Organizations that didn’t worship destruction. Neutral powers. Merchant organizations. Ancient clans. Mercenary groups. Research societies. Hidden sects.

They obeyed neither the Hero Association nor the Villain Association. They served their own interests. And within Stargate City, some of these organizations had existed quietly for generations. Their influence remained buried beneath the city’s glittering surface.
Waiting.
Watching.
Growing.
Somewhere within Stargate City stood an enormous mansion.

Its towering walls surrounded a vast estate filled with carefully maintained gardens, stone pathways, fountains, and several luxurious buildings. Everything about the estate radiated wealth. Yet beneath that beauty existed something considerably darker.

Deep within the mansion was a private chamber inaccessible to ordinary servants. The chamber was enormous. There were no windows. Dark stone covered the walls, while strange crimson patterns had been carved across the floor.
At the center stood a massive circular pool.
But there was no water inside it.
The liquid was crimson. Thick. Dark. And carrying the unmistakable metallic scent of blood.
At the center of that bloody pool sat a young man.

His upper body was exposed, revealing a muscular physique. Long crimson-red hair flowed behind him, several strands floating across the surface of the liquid. His eyes remained closed. His breathing was almost nonexistent.
Cultivating.

The blood surrounding him slowly rotated. At first, the movement was almost imperceptible. Then it became faster. A vortex gradually formed around his body. Tiny wisps of crimson energy began rising from the surface. One after another, they entered the young man’s body through his skin.
Every time another wisp disappeared into him, the level of liquid within the pool decreased slightly.

Three beautiful female attendants stood around the edge of the pool, silently maintaining the strange cultivation ritual. They carried containers filled with the same crimson liquid. Whenever the level of the pool dropped too far, they poured more inside.
Splash!
Fresh blood entered the pool. The young man’s breathing deepened. Another wave of crimson mist rose around him. The temperature inside the chamber seemed to increase.
Then...
Knock.
The sound came from the door.
The three attendants instantly stopped. Their expressions changed.
Boom!

Killing intent erupted from them simultaneously. The atmosphere inside the chamber became suffocating. Their previous appearance as quiet attendants vanished completely. They weren’t ordinary servants. Each one was dangerous.
The young man’s eyes opened.
Crimson pupils appeared beneath his eyelids.
"Enough."
One word. That was all it took.
The killing intent disappeared immediately. The three attendants lowered their heads.
The young man raised one hand. One attendant immediately walked toward a nearby hanger and retrieved a long black robe.

The young man rose from the pool. Strangely, the crimson liquid slid away from his body before it could cling to his skin. By the time he stepped onto the stone floor, there wasn’t a single drop remaining on him.
The attendants approached. One held the robe open while the others helped place it around his shoulders. The dark fabric covered him. They secured it neatly.
Throughout the entire process, the young man said nothing.
He walked toward a sofa positioned beside the pool and sat down. Only after settling comfortably did he finally look toward the door.
"Come in."
Click.
The door opened.
A young man entered. The moment he stepped into the chamber, he lowered his head respectfully.
If Dexter had been standing there, he would have recognized him immediately.
Wayne.
The very same Wayne who had approached Violette when she and Dexter were eating together at the restaurant.
But Wayne’s attitude now was completely different from the confident manner he had displayed that day. Here, there was no arrogance. No casual smile. He didn’t even raise his head without permission.

The red-haired young man leaned back against the sofa. One of the attendants moved behind him and began massaging his shoulders. He didn’t acknowledge her. His crimson eyes remained fixed entirely on Wayne.
Several uncomfortable seconds passed.
Then he finally spoke.
"You asked to see me."
Wayne swallowed. "Yes."
The young man’s fingers tapped gently against the armrest. Once. Twice. Three times.
"Then speak."
Wayne finally raised his head. There was a strange seriousness in his expression.
"It’s about Violette."
The tapping stopped.
For the first time, genuine interest appeared in the red-haired young man’s crimson eyes.
"Violette?"
"Yes."
Wayne hesitated.
" the man who was with her."
Silence.
The crimson pool behind them continued rotating slowly. The young man’s expression didn’t change. But the blood within the pool suddenly stopped moving. Completely.
Wayne noticed and his body stiffened.
The red-haired young man leaned forward. His crimson eyes narrowed.
"Speak Up..."

chapters.title: Chapter 252 | Let’s Go Girls
paragraphs: Wayne lowered his head slightly before beginning his report.
"Our spy sent another dispatch today."

Michael remained seated on the sofa, his crimson eyes resting calmly on Wayne. The blood pool behind him had resumed its slow rotation, crimson wisps rising from the surface like steam from a heated spring.
"The old man still hasn’t given Violette the key," Wayne continued. "Which means she still doesn’t possess complete authority. Officially, she hasn’t become the leader yet."
Michael said nothing.

His fingers rested against the arm of the sofa while the three attendants remained completely silent around him. They had returned to their positions after the earlier outburst, their heads bowed, their presence barely noticeable.
Wayne continued. "According to our sources, the old man’s condition is worsening. He’s growing weaker by the day. Everyone expected him to retire and transfer authority to Violette long ago."
Michael’s eyes narrowed slightly. "But he hasn’t."
"No."
"Why?"
"That is precisely what we’re trying to understand."

Wayne straightened slightly. "The authority transfer ceremony should have begun already. Violette is the obvious successor, and from everything we’ve gathered, the old man originally intended to hand everything over to her."
Michael tapped one finger against the armrest. Tap. Tap. Tap.
"Yet he still possesses the key."
"Yes."
The chamber fell silent.
Behind them, the enormous pool of blood continued rotating slowly, crimson wisps occasionally rising from its surface. The metallic scent of it hung in the air, thick and cloying.
Michael glanced toward it but said nothing.
Wayne understood that as permission to continue.
"There is something else."
Michael looked back at him.
"Our sources reported that Violette and the old man recently had a falling-out."
The tapping stopped.
Michael’s expression finally changed. "A falling-out?"
"Yes. We haven’t discovered exactly what caused it, but considering the timing, we believe it may be related to the key and the authority transfer ceremony."
Michael leaned back.
That certainly made things more interesting.
Violette had spent years preparing to inherit that position. For the old man to suddenly delay the transfer now... Something must have happened.
"There was also a name mentioned during their disagreement," Wayne added.
Michael’s gaze sharpened. "What name?"
Wayne hesitated. "Dexter."
The atmosphere changed.
Michael slowly turned his head. His crimson eyes locked onto Wayne with an intensity that made the air itself feel heavier.
"Which Dexter?"
Wayne suddenly felt uncomfortable. He had expected Michael to react to Violette’s name. But not like this.
"Dexter Ashford."
BOOM!
An invisible pressure erupted throughout the chamber.

The sofa beneath Michael cracked. The three attendants were instantly forced to their knees, their previous composure vanishing beneath the overwhelming pressure. Wayne’s expression changed dramatically. His own knee slammed against the floor.
Boom!
His entire body trembled.
Even the blood inside the enormous pool began churning violently.
Michael slowly rose. His long crimson hair shifted behind him despite there being no wind inside the chamber.
"Dexter..."
The name escaped his mouth almost like a curse.
Wayne remained kneeling. He didn’t dare interrupt.
Michael’s hand slowly curled into a fist.
Crack!
The air around his fingers distorted.
His expression, which had remained calm throughout the entire report, had become frighteningly cold.
"Not only did you take her from me..."
His fist tightened further.
"...now you’re involved in this matter too?"
The pressure intensified.
Wayne gritted his teeth. He could barely breathe. Yet what frightened him wasn’t the pressure itself. It was Michael’s reaction.
He had known there was history between Michael and Dexter. But this? This was hatred. Deep hatred.
Michael closed his eyes.
Several seconds passed.
Then the terrifying pressure disappeared as suddenly as it had arrived.
Wayne gasped quietly. The attendants remained kneeling. Michael opened his eyes again. His expression had returned to normal. Almost.
"Continue watching Violette."
Wayne immediately lowered his head. "Yes."
"And Dexter?"
Wayne waited.
Michael’s crimson eyes seemed to become several shades darker.
"Find out why his name was mentioned."
"Yes."
"I want to know what connection he has to the key, the old man, and the authority transfer."
Wayne nodded. "Understood."
Michael turned toward the blood pool.
"And Wayne?"
Wayne froze. "Yes?"
Michael glanced at him over his shoulder. "Don’t let Dexter know we’re watching him."
Wayne lowered his head. "I won’t."
Michael said nothing else.
Wayne understood. The meeting was over. He stood, bowed once, and left the chamber.
Click.
The door closed behind him.
Michael remained standing silently.
Dexter Ashford.
After all this time, that name had appeared before him again.
His eyes slowly narrowed. "Dexter..."
Morning arrived.
And while forces hidden throughout Stargate City were beginning to move around his name, Dexter knew absolutely nothing about it.
He was busy cooking.

Two large sets of meals occupied the kitchen. The first consisted of Grade One meals. Dexter had deliberately prepared plenty of them because of what Tessa had told him the previous night. The neighborhood festival was essentially a massive picnic, and exchanging food was part of the tradition.

Naturally, Dexter couldn’t bring his best meals and hand them out indiscriminately. Not because he was stingy. Grade Five meals were simply far too valuable. Giving them away at an ordinary neighborhood festival would attract more attention than he wanted.
So the Grade One meals were perfect. Good enough to impress people. Low enough in grade not to cause absolute chaos.
The second set of meals was completely different. Grade Five. Those were exclusively for his wives.
Dexter smiled as he finished the final dish. "Done."
He turned off the heat and began washing his hands. Then he felt someone behind him. He didn’t turn around.
"Good morning, Lyra."
Silence.
To anyone watching, it would’ve appeared as though Dexter had greeted an empty kitchen.
Then a sweet, melodious voice sounded directly inside his mind. "Good morning, Dexter."
Dexter smiled. Lyra stood quietly behind him.
"I slept well," her voice continued inside his head. "How about you?"
"Pretty well."
Dexter dried his hands. He remembered waking up with Selene wrapped around him and decided that perhaps pretty well was an understatement.
He turned toward Lyra. "How are the others?"
Lyra blinked. "They’re almost ready."
"Almost?"
"They’re still dressing."
Dexter glanced toward the hallway. Lyra smiled. "I’ll tell them to hurry."
"Thanks."
Lyra nodded brightly. Then, before leaving, her eyes wandered toward the food. Dexter noticed.
"Lyra."
Her hand stopped. She looked at him innocently.
Dexter looked at the small snack already in her hand. Then back at her. Lyra silently took another bite.
Dexter sighed. "At least leave enough for the festival."
A beautiful smile spread across her face. Then she turned and hurried toward the girls’ room.
Dexter shook his head. He couldn’t even be angry.

With the cooking finished, he packed everything into two separate coolers. One contained the Grade One meals meant for sharing. The other contained the Grade Five meals reserved for himself and the girls.
He carried both outside. His Type 6 vehicle was already waiting. Dexter opened it and carefully secured the coolers inside.
"That’s everything."
Or at least he hoped so. After double-checking the vehicle, Dexter returned to the house. He pushed open the front door.
Then stopped. Completely.
Three women were waiting in the living room. Lyra. Selene. Mira.
For several seconds, Dexter genuinely forgot why he had come back inside.
They were wearing the dresses he had bought for them weeks ago. The same dresses they rejected was what they were wearing right now.

Lyra stood slightly to the left. Her dark hair flowed beautifully around her shoulders, contrasting with the elegant dark gown she wore. The dress carried a quiet elegance that suited her perfectly, making her already delicate appearance even more striking.

Then there was Mira. Even sitting in her wheelchair, her presence was impossible to ignore. Her gown possessed a deep color somewhere between crimson and dark orange. Under different angles of light, it seemed to shift between the two. Dexter wasn’t entirely sure what color he should call it. But he knew one thing. It suited her. Perfectly. The fiery shade complemented her hair and gave her a fierce elegance.

Then Dexter noticed something else. The necklace. His eyes paused. Mira was wearing the necklace he had given her. For some reason, seeing that affected him even more than the dress. She had accepted it. And she had chosen to wear it today.

Finally, Dexter’s eyes moved toward Selene. Her gown was pure white. Combined with her silver-white hair, she appeared almost otherworldly. A delicate necklace rested around her neck, accompanied by matching earrings.
The three women were completely different from one another. Lyra possessed a quiet, mysterious beauty. Mira was fiery and commanding. Selene carried an icy elegance.
Yet standing together... Dexter had only one thought.
Beautiful. Far too beautiful.
His brain temporarily stopped supplying useful words.
The girls noticed.
Lyra’s cheeks slowly became pink. Selene looked away, a faint blush appearing across her face. Even Mira seemed slightly uncomfortable beneath the intensity of his stare.
Still, none of them said anything. Neither did Dexter.
Several seconds passed. Then more.
Eventually, Mira couldn’t take it anymore. "Have you seen enough?"
Her voice finally dragged Dexter back to reality. He blinked. Then looked at her.
Without even thinking, he answered honestly. "No."
Silence.
Lyra covered her mouth. A tiny laugh escaped her. Selene also failed to completely suppress her smile.
Mira stared at Dexter. Her eyes narrowed.
Dexter blinked again. Then realized what he had just said.
"Oh."
Mira’s glare intensified.
Dexter cleared his throat. "I mean..."
He looked at the three of them again. No. Actually, he had meant exactly what he said. His lips curved upward.
"You three look beautiful."
Lyra’s blush deepened. Selene lowered her eyes. Mira looked away.
"Obviously."
Dexter chuckled. Of course that would be Mira’s answer.

Still, he couldn’t stop looking at them. Not simply because they looked beautiful. The dresses meant something to him. When he had first given them the clothes and jewelry, he hadn’t been sure how they felt about the gifts. Now they were wearing them willingly.
It was a small thing. Perhaps ridiculously small. Yet to Dexter, it felt like proof that the invisible distance between them was slowly disappearing.
He didn’t mention it. There was no reason to ruin the moment.
Instead, Dexter pulled out his phone. 10:30 a.m.
His eyes widened slightly. "Right."
He slipped the phone back into his pocket.
Mira raised an eyebrow. "What?"
"We should probably leave before Tessa starts accusing me of deliberately hiding food from her."
Lyra tilted her head. Selene looked confused. Mira simply stared at him.
Dexter laughed. "Long story."
He walked toward the door and opened it before turning toward the three women.
"All right, girls."
Dexter smiled. "Let’s get moving."
And one after another, the four of them finally stepped out of the house for the festival.

A delicate necklace rested around her neck, accompanied by matching earrings.
The three women were completely different from one another.
Lyra possessed a quiet, mysterious beauty.
His brain temporarily stopped supplying useful words.
Selene looked away, a faint blush appearing across her face.
Even Mira seemed slightly uncomfortable beneath the intensity of his stare.
Still, none of them said anything.
Eventually, Mira couldn’t take it anymore.
Her voice finally dragged Dexter back to reality.
Without even thinking, he answered honestly.
Selene also failed to completely suppress her smile.
Then realized what he had just said.
He looked at the three of them again.
Actually, he had meant exactly what he said.
Of course that would be Mira’s answer.
Still, he couldn’t stop looking at them.
Not simply because they looked beautiful.
The dresses meant something to him.
When he had first given them the clothes and jewelry, he hadn’t been sure how they felt about the gifts.
Now they were wearing them willingly.
Yet to Dexter, it felt like proof that the invisible distance between them was slowly disappearing.
There was no reason to ruin the moment.
Instead, Dexter pulled out his phone.
He slipped the phone back into his pocket.
"We should probably leave before Tessa starts accusing me of deliberately hiding food from her."
He walked toward the door and opened it before turning toward the three women.
And one after another, the four of them finally stepped out of the house for the festival.

chapters.title: Chapter 253 | You’re My Sun
paragraphs: Dexter opened the front door and stepped aside.
Lyra was the first to walk out, followed closely by Selene. Dexter waited until both women were safely outside before moving behind Mira’s wheelchair and pushing her carefully over the threshold.
Before closing the door, he stopped and looked back into the house.
"Serum, snacks, tea..." he murmured, mentally checking everything one final time.
He had prepared more carefully than he wanted to admit.

Selene’s ice-suppressing serum was packed safely in case her condition suddenly flared up. For Lyra, he had brought several snacks because her appetite remained terrifying enough to bankrupt a restaurant if left unchecked. He had also brewed a special tea for Mira, though there was enough for all three women.
Dexter didn’t want to take any chances.
This would be the first proper outing the four of them had taken together since their marriage.
Fortunately, medicine and food weren’t the only precautions he’d taken.
His gaze briefly passed over the necklaces resting around their necks.
Each looked like an expensive piece of jewelry, but their real value had nothing to do with appearance.
Mira’s necklace contained a powerful defensive formation. The moment its wearer encountered a sufficiently dangerous attack, the necklace would automatically generate a protective barrier around her.

Lyra’s necklace was considerably more aggressive. Instead of simply protecting its wearer, it could retaliate. If Lyra’s life came under genuine threat, the artifact could release an attack carrying the power of a Peak Ultra Realm expert.
As for Selene’s...
Dexter considered hers the strangest of the three. If Selene encountered a lethal threat, the necklace could activate an emergency teleportation formation and transport her away from the danger.
Dexter finally closed the door.
’That should be enough.’
He didn’t actually expect anything to happen today. This was a neighborhood picnic, not a dungeon expedition. Still, caution had never killed anyone.
Besides, the necklaces weren’t their only protection.
There was him.

His cultivation was still within the Superhuman Realm, but judging him solely by cultivation level had become increasingly misleading. His combat strength had already surpassed what someone at his realm should possess, and when his talents, bloodline, techniques, and combat abilities were included...
His true combat power could already contend with someone in the Ultra Realm.
Unless someone particularly troublesome appeared, he could protect them.
He locked the gate.
Dexter opened the SUV rear passenger doors, allowing Lyra and Selene to enter first.
Dexter then returned to Mira.
"I’m going to carry you."
Mira looked up at him before giving a small nod.
Dexter bent down and carefully lifted her from the wheelchair. He fastened the supporting harness around her.
Only after checking each fastening twice did he straighten.
Dexter walked around to the driver’s side and climbed in.
"All right, here we go."
The drive took barely five minutes.
The neighborhood was strangely quiet along the way. It seems almost everyone was heading toward the same place.
The neighborhood festival. Or, more accurately, the neighborhood picnic.
When Dexter approached the public garden where the event was being held, the reason for the empty streets became obvious.
The parking lot was packed. Vehicles filled row after row, from ordinary family cars to expensive mana-powered vehicles.
"Quite a turnout," Dexter muttered.
He found an empty space near the edge and parked. After stepping out, he opened the rear door.
Lyra climbed down first and she immediately looked around with obvious curiosit.
Selene followed more cautiously as Dexter naturally reached for her arm and guided her away from the vehicle.
Dexter then went around to Mira. He unfolded her wheelchair beside the passenger door, locked it into position, then carefully transferred her into it.
Then they started toward the garden.
Mira was directly ahead of Dexter as he pushed her wheelchair. Lyra walked on his left. Selene stayed on his right, close enough that Dexter could reach her immediately if necessary.
For several seconds, everything seemed perfectly normal.
Then Dexter noticed the staring.
A woman unloading a basket from her vehicle stopped halfway through the motion. A man beside another car whispered something to his wife. Two teenagers openly turned around.
Dexter’s enhanced hearing caught fragments from different directions.
"Isn’t that..."
"That’s the Ashford..."
"Those must be his wives."
"Wait, Dexter Ashford?"
Dexter’s eyebrow twitched.
’Wonderful.’
Apparently, marrying three women from three powerful families was enough to transform someone’s private life into neighborhood entertainment.
Then a tiny voice cut through the whispers.
"Hi, Dexter!"
Dexter stopped. He turned toward the voice.
A little boy, probably around five years old, stood beside a nearby vehicle, enthusiastically waving at him. His smile was wide, gap-toothed.
Dexter blinked.
The child grinned wider. "Hello, Dexter!"
Before Dexter could recover from the absurdity of a five-year-old knowing him by name, another little boy popped out from beside the first. They looked almost identical.
Twins.
The second child immediately began waving too. "Hi, Dexter!"
Dexter blinked. "...Hi?"
He awkwardly raised his hand and waved back. Both children immediately brightened as though Dexter had just personally acknowledged two lifelong fans.
Their mother looked stunned.
Their father, who had been unloading containers from the trunk, immediately straightened.
Then, almost simultaneously, they grabbed their respective children.
"Sorry!"
"So sorry!"
One twin was lifted under the arms. The other was scooped against his father’s chest.
"But I wanted to ask him about his three wi—
The mother’s hand immediately covered the boy’s mouth.
Dexter nearly stumbled.
Lyra’s shoulders trembled. She was laughing. Silently, but definitely laughing.
Even Mira’s lips curled upward.
Dexter looked between them. "Very funny."
Mira finally spoke. "You know, if children that young already know your name, their parents must have been gossiping about you quite extensively."
Dexter glanced back at the rapidly retreating family. He sighed.
"What can I do? Their mouths belong to them."
Mira raised an eyebrow.
Dexter shrugged. "Besides, maybe I enjoy being the center of attention. You m?"
Mira’s lips curved slightly.
"Never."
The sarcasm was so dry Dexter almost laughed.
They continued toward the garden. The closer they came, the louder everything became.
Children laughed somewhere ahead. Music drifted through the trees.
Yet gradually, Dexter noticed something.
Lyra had slowed. Her dark eyes weren’t looking toward the festival anymore.
They were looking upward.
At the sky.
Dexter followed her gaze. The morning sky stretched endlessly overhead, painted a brilliant blue with thin clouds drifting lazily beneath the sun.
Lyra simply stared.
Then her voice appeared inside their minds. It was soft and melodious.
’It’s been a long time since I’ve seen the sky.’
Dexter’s expression changed slightly.
Lyra continued staring upward. ’It’s beautiful.’
He looked at Lyra and smiled. "Wait until sunset."
Lyra turned toward him. A small smile appeared on her lips.
Beside them, Selene also tilted her face toward the sky. Unlike Lyra, however, there was no beautiful blue world waiting above her. There hadn’t been for years.
But she could feel it.
The sunlight touched her pale skin. The breeze brushed strands of silver-white hair across her cheek.
Selene raised her face slightly higher.
"It’s been a long time since I’ve felt the warmth of the sun."
Dexter looked toward her. For several seconds, Selene quietly enjoyed it.
Then she glanced at Dexter.
"Now that I think about it... I don’t think I missed it that much."
Dexter stared at her, stunned.

chapters.title: Chapter 254 | The Attraction
paragraphs: The festival grounds were nothing like Dexter had imagined.

When Tessa had described it as a neighborhood festival mixed with a picnic, Dexter had pictured something simple. Music. Dancing. Perhaps a few stalls selling food and drinks. Children running around playing games. Something old-fashioned and peaceful.
The reality waiting for them beyond the entrance was completely different.
Dexter stopped pushing Mira’s wheelchair for a moment.
"Well..."
His eyes moved across the enormous garden.
"I definitely wasn’t expecting this."

The garden itself was massive, stretching almost as far as a football field. Green grass covered most of the open space. Colorful banners hung between lampposts, and the distant sound of music mixed with laughter and conversation.
But the first thing that caught everyone’s attention was the structure at the very center.
A waterfall.

It rose almost ten meters into the air, surrounded by an elaborate circular pool and strange architectural structures that concealed most of the machinery operating it. Yet its most fascinating feature was the illusion it created.
The water appeared to be flowing upward.

Thousands of glittering droplets seemed to rise from the pool toward the sky instead of falling toward the earth. Under the sunlight, those droplets sparkled brilliantly, occasionally creating tiny fragments of rainbows that danced across the mist.
Lyra stopped walking. Her dark eyes widened, reflecting the shimmering water.
Even Mira stared.
Selene couldn’t see the spectacle, but she could hear the tremendous rush of water in the distance.
Dexter continued forward.
The waterfall was only the beginning.
Beyond the enormous picnic field were numerous attractions. A roller coaster rose above one side of the garden, its tracks twisting between several artificial hills.

Farther away stood a horror house decorated to resemble a ruined castle. Fog machines pumped mist around its entrance, and costumed figures lurked near the doorway, waiting to scare unsuspecting visitors.
There were shooting ranges and game booths. Candy stores and small restaurants were present. Children’s rides and prize stalls completed the scene.
There was even a large artificial lake with small boats drifting across it, their occupants laughing as they paddled in circles.
Families were everywhere.

Some had spread colorful mats across the grass and were eating together beneath large umbrellas. Others were walking between attractions carrying snacks and drinks. Children raced across the grass while their parents shouted after them. Groups of adults sat together laughing. Several families were already lining up for the roller coaster.
Dexter stared.
"So this is what Tessa calls a picnic?"
Mira’s lips curled. "Apparently."
"I feel deceived."
Lyra’s voice appeared inside their minds. ’It looks fun.’
Mira nodded. "It does."
Dexter looked toward her. Mira was studying the attractions with considerably more interest than he had expected. Her eyes moved from the roller coaster to the shooting range to the horror house.
"All right."
He pushed Mira farther into the festival.
"First, we establish our territory."
Mira glanced upward. "Our territory?"
"Picnic territory."
"That’s not a thing."
"It is now."

They entered through the main gate without difficulty. There were no tickets or guards demanding identification. The entire event appeared to have been arranged specifically for residents of the neighborhood and their guests.
Dexter searched for somewhere suitable. Many of the best spots near the waterfall had already been occupied.

Eventually, he noticed a large open patch of grass beneath the partial shade of an enormous tree. It was far enough from the busiest attractions that they wouldn’t constantly have people walking around them, yet close enough to the center of the festival to enjoy everything.
"Here."
Dexter stopped. "This should work."
The three women seemed satisfied.
"Give me a second."
Dexter flipped his hand.
Three folded picnic mats appeared.
He unfolded the first mat.
"Fwoop!"
It spread neatly across the grass. Then another. And another. He arranged the three large mats beside one another until they formed one comfortable picnic area.
"There."
Dexter stepped back proudly.

Lyra immediately sat down, folding her legs beneath her. Selene carefully lowered herself onto the mat beside her, using Lyra’s hand for guidance. The two of them settled in comfortably, their shoulders almost touching.
Dexter then turned toward Mira. She was still in her wheelchair.
"Do you want to stay in the chair?"
Mira glanced at the mats.
Dexter continued, "Or would you rather sit with us?"
Mira considered it but then spoke.
"Put me on the mat."
Dexter raised an eyebrow. "You’re sure?"
"I already came all the way here."
A small smile appeared on her face. "I might as well get the full experience."
Dexter smiled. "Fair enough."
He locked the wheelchair. Then he bent down.
Her right arm.
Unlike the rest of her body, which remained badly affected by her injuries, the arm had already recovered enough function for her to move it voluntarily.
Dexter slid one arm behind Mira’s back and the other beneath her legs.
"Ready?"
"Just pick me up."
"Bossy."
"Dexter."
"Picking you up."
He lifted her effortlessly. Mira’s arm moved around his shoulder for stability. Neither of them noticed several conversations nearby becoming considerably quieter.
Dexter carried Mira onto the mat. He was careful when lowering her, making certain her legs remained properly positioned rather than twisting awkwardly beneath her.
"There."

Mira adjusted herself using her recovered right arm. Dexter placed a cushion nearby, but before he could help her further, Mira used her arm to support herself. She shifted slightly. Then, with visible effort, she propped her head against her right hand. Her crimson hair spilled around her shoulders, catching the sunlight like threads of fire.
Dexter looked at her.
Mira noticed. "What?"
"Nothing."
"You’re staring again."
"I’m allowed to look at my wife."
Mira’s eyes narrowed. "You’ve become increasingly shameless."
"I’ve been practicing."
"Clearly."
Lyra silently laughed beside them, her shoulders shaking with suppressed giggles.
Dexter smiled and began arranging their things. What none of them could completely ignore, however, were the people around them.
The whispers had followed them from the parking lot.
Dexter Ashford was hardly an anonymous figure.
The discarded firstborn of the Ashford family. The bastard son who had spent years as little more than a servant. The man who had suddenly married three once-famous women from powerful families.
People wanted to see him. More importantly, they wanted to see his wives.
Dexter’s enhanced hearing caught whispers from several nearby picnic groups.
"That’s really him."
"Dexter Ashford?"
"Those are the three?"
"I heard they moved into this neighborhood recently."
"That’s Mira Calloway..."
"The silver-haired one must be Selene Frost."
"What about the dark-haired woman?"
"Lyra Vance."
Dexter heard everything but simply ignored it. If he reacted every time someone whispered his name, he’d spend the entire festival turning his head like a confused owl.
He opened one of the bags instead.
"Anyone hungry?"
Lyra’s head immediately turned.
Dexter stared at her. Lyra stared back.
"Why did I even ask?"
Her voice entered his mind. ’Because you’re considerate.’
"No. Because apparently I haven’t learned my lesson."
Lyra smiled sweetly.
Mira snorted.
Selene’s lips curved slightly.
Dexter was about to retrieve something when Mira suddenly spoke.
"They’re still staring."
"I know."
"It doesn’t bother you?"
Dexter glanced around. Several people immediately pretended they hadn’t been looking. One man became extremely interested in his drink. A woman suddenly found the grass fascinating.
Dexter shrugged. "Let them stare."
He sat down. "They’ll get bored eventually."
Mira studied him for a second. Then her expression softened. "Perhaps."
Dexter suddenly said. "This food is for later. Remember, we’re supposed to exchange meals with everyone."
Lyra’s gaze immediately drifted toward the cooler.
Dexter noticed. "Don’t even think about it."
Lyra blinked her eyes innocently.
Dexter narrowed his eyes. He want going to fall for it.
"But," Dexter continued, "we don’t have to sit here starving until then. There are candy stores, ice cream shops, snack stalls and probably a dozen other things around here."
That got Lyra’s attention. Her dark eyes immediately brightened.
’Candy.’
Her melodious voice appeared inside their minds.
’I want candy.’
Dexter laughed. "Of course you do."
Lyra smiled brightly.
"Candy it is. Anything else?"
Lyra thought for approximately two seconds. Dexter could practically see the calculations happening behind her eyes. He quickly turned away before she could produce a shopping list.
"What about you two?"

chapters.title: Chapter 255 | The Twins
paragraphs: Lyra thought passed two seconds and Dexter could practically see the calculations happening behind her eyes. He quickly turned away before she could produce a shopping list.
"What about you two?"
Selene hesitated.
Dexter noticed immediately. "You don’t know what you want?"
Selene shook her head. "I haven’t been to somewhere like this in a long time."
Dexter’s expression softened. "Then I’ll pick something for you."
Selene tilted her head toward him. "Something good?"
"Have a little faith in me."
"I’ll try."
Dexter placed a hand against his chest. "That sounded unnecessarily cruel."
A faint smile appeared on Selene’s face.
Dexter turned toward Mira. "And you?"
Mira didn’t answer immediately. Her gaze wandered toward the stalls in the distance. Then she said simply, "Ice cream."
Dexter blinked. That wasn’t what he’d expected from her.
"Ice cream?"
Mira looked at him. "Is there a problem?"
"No. I suppose it’s appropriate. With your fiery temper, you’d need something to cool you down."
Dexter suppressed a smile.
Mira immediately glared at him.
Immediately, Lyra’s voice invaded his mind. ’I want ice cream too.’
Dexter turned. "You just asked for candy."
Lyra nodded. ’And ice cream.’
"Candy and ice cream?"
Another nod.
Dexter stared at her. Lyra stared back.
He surrendered. "Fine."
Lyra’s face lit up.
"But not too much."
Her smile faded slightly.
"Don’t look at me like that. We’re still eating later."
Dexter stood and brushed the grass from his clothes.
"I’ll go get everything."
He had only taken two steps when he stopped.
Something occurred to him and he turned around.
Mira seeing this raised an eyebrow.l as though asking ’What now?’
Dexter glared at her. "I didn’t even say anything."
"You were about to."
Mira’s lips twitched.
Dexter ignored her. "Actually, why don’t you three come with me?"
Lyra immediately perked up and Selene looked interested too.
But Mira’s reaction was the most amusing. For just a second, her crimson eyes lit up but then she apparently realized Dexter was looking at her and her expression instantly became indifferent.
"If you want."
Dexter smiled. "You’re terrible at pretending you don’t want to go."
Mira slowly looked back at him and showed her cute fist.
"See? That’s much more natural."
"Dexter."
He laughed. "All right. We’re all going.
He walked toward Mira. "Let’s see whether this place is actually as fun as it looks."
Dexter carefully lifted her from the mat and returned her to the wheelchair, making sure she was positioned comfortably before securing her.
Lyra already stood up with excitement in her eyes and Selene stood beside her.
Dexter moved behind Mira’s wheelchair.
"First stop, ice cream and candy."
He started pushing. "But after that..."
His gaze traveled toward the attractions. "What do you girls want to try first?"
Three answers came almost simultaneously.
"Roller coaster," Mira said.
"Laser tag," Selene answered.
’Haunted house,’ Lyra’s voice sounded inside their minds.
Dexter blinked his eyes and immediately stopped walking.
The three women paused as they looked at one another and for a second, nobody spoke.
Suddenly Mira smiled Selene chuckled and lyra silently laughed.
Dexter looked between them. "Three women. Three completely different answers."
"Then choose one," Mira said.
"Absolutely not. I’m not walking into that trap."
Mira raised an eyebrow. "What trap?"
"If I choose one of you, the other two will remember it forever."
Selene actually laughed. "You’re learning."
"Marriage has sharpened my survival instincts."
Dexter shook his head. "I have a better idea. Before we do any of those three, I’ll choose the first activity."
Mira looked back at him suspiciously. "What activity?"
"That’s a surprise."
"I don’t like surprises."
"That’s unfortunate."
Dexter pushed her forward. "But first, snacks."
They soon reached the candy and ice cream shop.
Unsurprisingly, it was busy.
The store itself was brightly decorated, with colorful displays filling its windows. Through the glass, Dexter could see rows upon rows of sweets, chocolates, pastries, frozen desserts and much more.
Lyra’s eyes lit up like she just saw Santa.
Dexter looked at her and her eyes were enormous.
He sighed. "We’re going to be here for a while, aren’t we?"
Lyra nodded enthusiastically.
"Wonderful."
There was already a queue, so Dexter guided the group toward the back.
Several people noticed them. Dexter expected the same whispering that had followed them earlier.
There were a few glances and a few curious looks. But surprisingly, that was all. Once the initial curiosity faded, everyone returned to enjoying themselves.

A group nearby laughed loudly over drinks. Two women were arguing playfully about which ice cream flavor was better. Several children pressed their faces against the shop window while their parents tried unsuccessfully to pull them away. Music drifted faintly across the garden.
Dexter relaxed.
"Much better."
Mira heard him. "What is?"
"People aren’t staring anymore."
"Disappointed?"
Dexter looked down at her. "Extremely. My fame lasted twenty minutes."
"Tragic.
"I’ll recover."
Two families stood between them and the counter.
Then Dexter noticed someone familiar.
Or rather, two very small someones.
The twins from the parking lot. Their parents were standing two places ahead. The father was speaking to his wife while the twins were playing.
"Stop."
"You stop."
"You pushed me!"
"No, you pushed me!"
Their mother turned around. "Both of you behave."
Instant innocence. The twins immediately stood straight.
Their mother turned away.
Three seconds had barely passed when the war resumed.
Dexter watched with growing amusement.
Mira noticed where he was looking. "Your admirers."
"Please don’t call them that."
One twin dodged his brother’s hand and stumbled sideways out of the queue. He caught himself before falling. Then he looked up.
His eyes landed directly on Dexter.
The boy froze and Dexter too froze.
Recognition exploded across the child’s face as he spoke.
"Dexter!"
Instantly, half the queue turned.
Dexter closed his eyes. "So much for my fame dying."
The second twin heard his brother and immediately spun around and his face lit up too.
"It’s Dexter!"
Their parents went completely still and, very slowly, their mother turned around. Her eyes landed on Dexter. She sighed in exhaustion.
The first twin was already running toward him. "Dexter!"
His brother followed. "Dexter!"
Their father reached out too late. "Wait!"
Both children raced past the people in line and stopped directly in front of Dexter. They looked up at him with enormous, excited eyes.
Dexter stared down at them and forced a smile.
"...Hello again."
Both boys immediately grinned.
Lyra was already silently laughing and Mira looked far too entertained. Even Selene had picked up on what was happening from the voices around her.
The first twin opened his mouth.
Their mother hurried toward them. "I’m so sorry!"
She reached for her son but the boy ducked.
"I just want to ask him something!"
"No, you don’t."
"Yes, I do!"
His brother nodded furiously. "We both do!"
Dexter suddenly had a very bad feeling.
Their mother looked like she wanted the earth to swallow her.
Lyra eyes glittered with amusement.
"Well, Dexter, your fans have returned."
Dexter sighed. "I preferred the staring."

chapters.title: Chapter 256 | How Did You Do It!?
paragraphs: The parents stared at Dexter with matching embarrassed smiles.
"We’re really sorry," the mother said.
"Yes," the father quickly added. "They’ve been talking about you since they saw you earlier."
Dexter glanced down at the two boys. They were staring up at him with such excitement that he couldn’t bring himself to be annoyed.
He shrugged. "It’s fine. Really."
The parents visibly relaxed.
Dexter crouched slightly so he wasn’t towering over the children. "So, how old are you two?"
Both boys immediately raised their right hand and indicated four with their fingers.
"Four and a half!" they shouted together.
"Four and a half," Dexter repeated solemnly. "That’s a very serious age."
The twins nodded as though he had spoken an undeniable truth.
Dexter couldn’t resist reaching out and ruffling their hair. "You two are adorable. What are your names?"
The first boy proudly slapped a tiny hand against his chest. "I’m Peter!"
The second immediately copied him. "And I’m Paul!"
"Peter and Paul?"
Dexter nodded approvingly. "Nice names."
The twins grinned.
"All right, Peter and Paul. You were desperate to ask me something earlier." Dexter folded his arms. "What is it?"
The twins’ eyes lit up.
"How do we become like you?"
Dexter blinked. "Like me?"
Both nodded furiously.
Dexter glanced at their parents. Their father’s expression suddenly became suspiciously uncomfortable.
Dexter looked back at the children. "You’ll have to explain that one."
Peter and Paul exchanged a glance. Then both looked past Dexter.
Toward Mira, Lyra and Selene.
The moment the three women noticed, the twins immediately looked away, suddenly shy.
Dexter’s eyebrow rose.
Peter leaned closer. In what he apparently believed was a whisper, he said loudly enough for practically everyone nearby to hear, "My dad only married my mom."
Dexter’s lips twitched as a bad feeling settled in place.
The father closed his eyes.
Paul continued his brother’s explanation. "But you have..."
He raised one tiny finger. "One..."
Another finger. "Two..."
Then a third. "Three wives!"
A few people in the queue immediately began coughing suspiciously.
Mira turned her face away, but Dexter could already see the smile she was trying to hide.
Peter nodded seriously. "We asked Papa why he didn’t marry two more wives."
Dexter slowly looked toward their father. The man suddenly became extremely interested in the candy-store sign.
Paul continued. "And Papa said you’re very special."
Peter nodded. "And Papa said he doesn’t have a choice."
Smack!
The mother hit her husband on the arm.
The man jumped. "What?"
She glared at him. "You told them that?"
"I didn’t say it like that!"
"Yes, you did," Peter said.
"Yes, exactly like that," Paul confirmed.
The father’s face collapsed. "Traitors.
Dexter bit the inside of his cheek and stopped himself from lagging.
Behind him, Mira had already lost the battle as a soft chuckle escaped her. Selene followed. Then Lyra’s laughter sounded inside Dexter’s mind.
’His face...’
Dexter cleared his throat. "So that’s what you wanted to ask me?"
"No!"
Peter stepped closer. "We have another question."
Dexter suddenly didn’t want to hear it. Unfortunately, there was no stopping them.
Peter announced proudly, "There are three girls in my class that I like."
Paul nodded. "Me too!"
The twins looked at each other. Then Peter continued. "So we decided we’ll be like you."
Dexter’s smile disappeared.
Paul threw both arms outward. "We’ll marry all the girls in our class!"
The twins looked extremely pleased with their plan.
Their mother covered her face and their father looked ready to disappear into the candy display.
Mira’s shoulders were trembling. Selene wasn’t doing much better. Lyra had completely stopped trying to hide her amusement.
Dexter stared at Peter and Paul.
Before he could answer, Peter’s excitement disappeared. "But they said no."
Paul nodded sadly. "They don’t want to marry us."
The twins looked up at Dexter. Their expressions became deadly serious.
"So how did you do it?"
Dexter froze as he looked back at the three girls but they were each entertained.
"I’m glad my suffering amuses you."
"Very much," Mira replied.
Dexter sighed and returned his attention to the twins. This might genuinely be the strangest conversation he’d had all week. And considering his life, that was impressive.
He crouched until he was closer to their height.
"Listen, Peter. Paul."
The twins leaned forward attentively.
"That’s not how it works."
Their smiles vanished.
"You can’t just decide you’re going to marry every girl you like."
"Why?" Peter asked.
"Because those girls get to choose too."
That seemed to require considerable processing.

Dexter continued. "When you’re older, you’ll understand it better. Some people fall in love with one person. Some people’s lives turn out differently. But having more people isn’t what makes someone special."
The twins listened with surprising seriousness.
"What matters is finding someone who likes you for who you are, and who you genuinely care about too."
Paul frowned. "But you have three."
There it was.
Dexter glanced behind him. Mira was watching. So were Selene and Lyra. Their expressions had softened, the amusement giving way to something quieter.
His expression softened. "My situation is unusual."
"Very unusual?" Peter asked.
"Extremely."
The boys exchanged fascinated looks.
Dexter smiled. "Your dad found someone he loves."
He pointed toward their mother. "And judging from the way your mom keeps hitting him every time he says something stupid, I’d say he’s got his hands full already."
The father instantly burst out laughing.
His wife immediately glared at him.
He stopped.
Dexter almost lost his composure.
"So," Dexter continued, "don’t worry about marrying three girls. You’re four and a half. You’ve got more important things to do."
"Like what?" Paul asked.
Dexter thought about it. "Eat candy."
The twins’ eyes widened.
"Play games."
Their smiles returned.
"Have fun."
They nodded enthusiastically.
"And stop worrying about marriage until you’re much, much older."
Peter and Paul looked at one another. A silent conference seemed to occur.
Finally, Peter nodded. "Okay."
Paul nodded too. "Okay."
Dexter smiled. "Good."
Peter suddenly raised his hand. "But when I’m older..."
"Nop."
Dexter shook his head.
"But I didn’t ask yet!"
"I know where this is going."
Mira laughed again.
Fortunately for Dexter, the twins’ parents had finally reached the counter. Their order was ready. The mother quickly collected the ice cream while their father paid.
Then they returned for their children.
"All right, you two. That’s enough interrogation."
"No!"
Peter tried to escape. His father scooped him up.
Paul immediately attempted to run around his mother. She caught him just as easily.
Paul looked devastated.
Their mother gave Dexter another apologetic smile. "I’m really sorry about all that."
Dexter waved dismissively. "Don’t worry. They’re funny."
"That’s one word for it," their father muttered.
His wife glared at him. He immediately smiled.
The man looked toward Dexter. "Well, we’re neighbors. I’m sure we’ll see each other again."
Dexter nodded. "Probably."
The father opened his mouth. "Maybe sometime we could..."
His wife slapped his arm. "Come on."
"What did I do now?"
"Walk."
"I’m walking!"
She dragged him away while he carried Peter. Paul waved furiously from his mother’s arms.
"Bye, Dexter!"
Peter joined him. "Bye!"
Dexter raised his hand. "Bye, Peter. Bye, Paul."
The twins continued waving until their parents disappeared into the crowd.
Dexter stared after them. Then he shook his head and chuckled. "What a dilemma."
Mira’s voice came from behind him. "So..."
Dexter immediately became suspicious. He slowly turned around.
Mira wore an expression that promised trouble. Selene was smiling. Lyra looked positively delighted.
Mira rested her cheek against her recovered hand. "Tell us, Dexter."
Her crimson eyes glittered. "How exactly did you do it?"
Dexter’s face went blank and the three women burst into laughter.
Dexter sighed. Perhaps the haunted house would be safer.

chapters.title: Chapter 257 | Sugar Rush
paragraphs: It was finally Dexter and the girls turn as they reached the front of the ice cream shop.
The moment Lyra saw the enormous menu hanging above the counter, her eyes widened with excitement.
Dexter followed her gaze.
There were dozens of flavors. Some were normal flavor that Dexter was quite familiar with like vanilla, chocolate, strawberry, caramel.
Then their were other ones that Dexter didn’t know about like Frostberry Swirl, Crimson Dragonfruit and several others Dexter had never heard of.
Dexter sighed. "This is going to take forever."
Lyra didn’t even look at him.
Mira chuckled from her wheelchair. "You’re the one who brought her here."
"Yes. I’m beginning to recognize my mistake."
Lyra finally turned as her melodious voice appeared directly inside his mind. ’I heard that.’
Dexter raised an eyebrow. "Technically, you didn’t."
Lyra narrowed her eyes and she pouted with glistening eyes.
Dexter grinned softly but spoke. ’Alright. Sorry.’
He then stepped toward the counter. "All right, what flavor?"
He looked toward Mira first.
Mira studied the menu. "Strawberry."
Dexter blinked. "Just strawberry?"
She looked at him. "Is there something wrong with strawberry?"
"No."
"Then strawberry."
Dexter smiled slightly. He’d expected something more dramatic from the former Crimson Valkyrie. Crimson Dragonfruit, perhaps. Blazing Mango. Something that sounded as aggressive as she was.
Instead, strawberry.
Mira narrowed her eyes. "Why are you smiling?"
"No reason."
"You’re thinking something."
"Strawberry it is."
"Dexter."
He had already turned away. "Selene?"
Selene tilted her head as she asked.
"What flavors are there?"
Dexter began reading some of them. "Vanilla, chocolate, strawberry, mint, caramel, honeycomb, Frostberry, Moonlight Vanilla, Blue Star Mint..."
"Blue Star Mint."
Dexter stopped. "That was fast."
"I like mint."
"Blue Star Mint for Selene."
He turned toward Lyra. "And for the bottomless pit?"
Lyra glared at him. Then looked at the menu again.
Her gaze moved from one flavor to another. And another. And another.
Dexter waited for almost 2 minutes before hs spoke.
"Lyra."
But there was nothing as her eyes continued moving.
Dexter folded his arms. "Still waiting for you Lyra..."
Finally, her voice entered his mind. ’Starlight Chocolate.’
"Alright."
Dexter turned toward the employee. "One strawberry, one Blue Star Mint, and one Starlight Chocolate."
Lyra immediately touched his arm as she stared at him with her puppy eyes.
Lyra pointed toward the Starlight Chocolate. Then raised two fingers.
"You haven’t even eaten lunch yet Lyra."
She continued holding up two fingers.
Dexter narrowed his eyes. Lyra narrowed hers.
A silent battle began.
Mira watched them and Selene waited. Even the employee behind the counter awkwardly looked between the two.
Eventually Dexter sighed. "Two scoops."
Lyra smiled.
"You’re impossible."
Her smile became sweeter.
Dexter paid for everything. A few minutes later, each woman had her ice cream.

Mira received a cup because Dexter didn’t want her struggling with a cone while her mobility was still limited. Her recovered right arm had improved tremendously, but he wasn’t interested in making things unnecessarily difficult for her.
Selene chose a cone. Lyra chose the largest cone available.
Of course she did.
Dexter looked at her double scoop. Then at the single scoops belonging to Mira and Selene. "You’re going to ruin your appetite."
She smiled sweetly at him as she started eating.
Dexter shook his head. "Hopeless."
They moved away from the counter.
Mira looked toward him. "Aren’t you getting one?"
Dexter shook his head. "I’m fine."
Mira looked at her strawberry ice cream and then back at him. "You dragged us here and you’re not eating?"
"Of course im eating. I’ll steal some of yours."
Mira’s eyes narrowed. "Try it."
Dexter laughed. "Fine. I’ll behave."
He moved behind her wheelchair and began pushing again.
They hadn’t gone more than ten meters before Lyra suddenly stopped.
Dexter nearly walked into her. "What now?"
Lyra pointed.
A candy store.
Dexter stared at it. Then at her. Then at the ice cream she was still eating. "You already have ice cream."
Lyra nodded.
"And you want candy."
Another nod.
Dexter sighed. "Why did I ask?"
Mira smiled. "You’ve made a terrible mistake."
"I made three terrible mistakes."
Mira’s smile instantly vanished.
Dexter immediately corrected himself. "Marrying you wasn’t the mistake. Offering unlimited festival snacks was."
Mira snorted. "Nice recovery."
"I’ve become talented."

They entered the candy shop. The inside was a riot of color. Transparent containers covered the walls, filled with sweets of every possible shape and color. There were chocolate bars infused with tiny amounts of mana, crystal candies, fruit chews, marshmallows, hard candy, sour strips, caramel cubes and enormous spirals of rainbow-colored sugar.
Near the front was a machine spinning fluffy clouds of cotton candy.
Mira’s attention immediately shifted toward it.
Dexter noticed. He leaned slightly over the wheelchair. "Cotton candy?"
Mira looked away. "I didn’t say anything."
"You didn’t need to."
Mira looked at I’m with a strange gaze but she eventually didn’t argue back.
Dexter ordered Mira a large pink cotton candy.
Dexter turned toward Selene. "What about you?"
Selene listened as he described the options. Eventually she chose small crystalline fruit drops that dissolved slowly on the tongue.
Selene tried one and her eyebrows rose.
"Good?"
She nodded. "I like it."
"Then we’ll take a bag."
Dexter turned and he realized that Lyra had actually disappeared.
His eyes widened. "Where did she—"
He found her three steps away, staring at an enormous display of chocolate-coated caramel candies.
Dexter chuckled. "Fine. Pick one bag."
Lyra immediately grabbed the largest one.
"That’s not what I meant."
She hugged it against herself.
"Lyra."
She turned away and Selene chuckled at the display.
Dexter sughed and surrendered.
A few minutes later, they emerged from the shop carrying far more sugar than any responsible group of adults should have possessed.
They continued deeper into the festival.
The atmosphere became increasingly lively the farther they walked. The roller coaster thundered overhead somewhere in the distance.
For most people, it was simply noise.
For Selene, however, it was something else entirely.
Dexter noticed how confidently she was walking. Usually, when they were outside, Selene stayed close to either him or Lyra. Today she wasn’t.
She still walked beside him, but there was less hesitation in her steps. Her head moved slightly whenever someone approached. When a child ran across their path, Selene shifted half a step backward.
Of course she could do this due to her new talent but then Dexter saw that her eyes were actually opened and her pupils were moving as though she could see what was happening.
His expression changed slightly as he continued pushing Mira for several seconds before asking quietly,
"Selene."
"Hm?"
"Are you okay?"
Selene became silent.

Lyra pointed toward the Starlight Chocolate.
"You haven’t even eaten lunch yet Lyra."
She continued holding up two fingers.
Mira watched them and Selene waited.
Even the employee behind the counter awkwardly looked between the two.
A few minutes later, each woman had her ice cream.
Mira received a cup because Dexter didn’t want her struggling with a cone while her mobility was still limited.
Her recovered right arm had improved tremendously, but he wasn’t interested in making things unnecessarily difficult for her.
Lyra chose the largest cone available.
Dexter looked at her double scoop.
Then at the single scoops belonging to Mira and Selene.
She smiled sweetly at him as she started eating.
They moved away from the counter.
Mira looked at her strawberry ice cream and then back at him.
"You dragged us here and you’re not eating?"
He moved behind her wheelchair and began pushing again.
They hadn’t gone more than ten meters before Lyra suddenly stopped.
Then at the ice cream she was still eating.
The inside was a riot of color.
Transparent containers covered the walls, filled with sweets of every possible shape and color.
There were chocolate bars infused with tiny amounts of mana, crystal candies, fruit chews, marshmallows, hard candy, sour strips, caramel cubes and enormous spirals of rainbow-colored sugar.
Near the front was a machine spinning fluffy clouds of cotton candy.
Mira’s attention immediately shifted toward it.
He leaned slightly over the wheelchair.
Mira looked at I’m with a strange gaze but she eventually didn’t argue back.
Dexter ordered Mira a large pink cotton candy.
Selene listened as he described the options.
Eventually she chose small crystalline fruit drops that dissolved slowly on the tongue.
Selene tried one and her eyebrows rose.
Dexter turned and he realized that Lyra had actually disappeared.
He found her three steps away, staring at an enormous display of chocolate-coated caramel candies.
Lyra immediately grabbed the largest one.
She turned away and Selene chuckled at the display.
A few minutes later, they emerged from the shop carrying far more sugar than any responsible group of adults should have possessed.
They continued deeper into the festival.
The atmosphere became increasingly lively the farther they walked.
The roller coaster thundered overhead somewhere in the distance.
For most people, it was simply noise.
For Selene, however, it was something else entirely.
Dexter noticed how confidently she was walking.
Usually, when they were outside, Selene stayed close to either him or Lyra.
She still walked beside him, but there was less hesitation in her steps.
Her head moved slightly whenever someone approached.
When a child ran across their path, Selene shifted half a step backward.
Of course she could do this due to her new talent but then Dexter saw that her eyes were actually opened and her pupils were moving as though she could see what was happening.
His expression changed slightly as he continued pushing Mira for several seconds before asking quietly,

chapters.title: Chapter 258 | The First Attempt At Seduction
paragraphs: Mira glanced toward Selene.
Selene hesitated before she spoke. "I don’t want to be too hopeful or say anything but..."
She suddenly raised her head and stared into directly into Dexter’s eyes. "My eye sight has gotten a bit better."
Dexter’s eyes brightened. "How much better?"
"I think..." She raised her hand toward the sunlight. "I can see colors."
Dexter froze, Mira’s eyes widened and even Lyra finally looked away from her ice cream.
Selene’s pale eyes stared forward. They were still slightly unfocused and pale, still early damaged. But they weren’t quite as empty as they had once been.
Dexter had noticed the difference before. He simply hadn’t wanted to assume.
"You can see?"
"Not properly." Selene shook her head quickly. "Don’t misunderstand. Everything is still extremely blurry. Most things are darkness or vague patches."
Her voice became quieter. "But sometimes..." She turned her face toward the sky. "There’s blue."
Dexter’s smile slowly widened.
Selene lowered her gaze toward the grass. "And green."
Then she turned toward Mira. "Red."
Mira stared at her. "My hair?"
"I think so."
A rare softness entered Mira’s expression. "Yes."
Selene smiled. "It’s very bright."
Dexter laughed. "That’s really nice!"
Selene turned toward him.
Dexter couldn’t hide his excitement. "Very soon, you all will be healed up."
Selene’s expression softened as she looked downward shyly. "I hope so."
Dexter shook his head. "No."
Selene looked back.
Dexter smiled confidently. "I know so."
Something in his tone silenced her. He said it as though their recovery had already been decided and the world simply hadn’t caught up yet.
Selene’s cheeks warmed slightly. She lowered her head.
Dexter smiled. He knew what was happening. The medicine was working.
Everything was finally beginning to produce visible results.
He looked down at Mira. When they’d first married, she couldn’t voluntarily move anything below her neck. Now her right arm had recovered enough that she could use it independently.
Then Selene. The woman who had been completely blind could now faintly distinguish colors.
Which left...
Dexter slowly turned. Lyra.
She was walking beside them. Her entire attention had returned to the Starlight Chocolate ice cream.
Lick. Lick. Lick.
Dexter stared.
Lyra eventually sensed his gaze and she paused as her tongue had barely left the ice cream when her violet eyes shifted toward him.
She blinked. ’What?’
Dexter nearly laughed. She hadn’t been paying attention at all.
"Have you noticed any improvement?"
Lyra tilted her head.
"Your ears or vocal cords. Anything?"
Understanding appeared in Lyra’s eyes and she nodded.
Dexter’s expression immediately became serious. "When?"
Lyra’s mental voice reached him. ’A few days ago.’
Dexter stopped walking again. "A few days ago?!"
Lyra blinked. ’Yes.’
"And you didn’t tell me?"
She shrugged.
Dexter stared incredulously.
Mira chuckled.
"What improvement?" Dexter asked.
Lyra thought. ’I can hear a little.’
His expression changed. "How much?"
’Not much.’
She glanced toward the roller coaster. A train thundered along the distant tracks.
’Loud noises. Sometimes.’
Dexter watched her carefully.
’Everything sounds strange. Distant. Like I’m underwater.’
"But you can hear it."
Lyra nodded.
Dexter grinned. "What about your voice?"
Lyra expression turned a bit sad as she shook her head. ’Nothing.’
’My vocal cords haven’t recovered enough. I still can’t make any sound.’
Dexter’s smile didn’t diminish. "That’s still an improvement."
Lyra nodded.
Dexter’s determination hardened. "In the next few days, it’ll get even better."
Lyra smiled and immediately returned to her ice cream.
Dexter stared at her incredulously as she licked her chocolate scoop. "That’s it?"
"Food over emotional moment?"
Another lick.
Dexter sighed. "Of course."
Dexter pushed Mira while Selene and Lyra walked beside them.
A few minutes later, Dexter happened to glance downward.
Mira was eating her strawberry ice cream with her recovered hand. But something immediately caught his attention.
There was a streak of strawberry ice cream on her upper lip but Mira didn’t notice.
Dexter stopped the wheelchair and Mira looked up. "What happened?"
"Wait."
"For what?"
Dexter moved around the wheelchair and stood in front of her.
Mira raised an eyebrow but didn’t say anything.
"Stay still."
Her eyes narrowed suspiciously. "Why?
Dexter leaned closer.
Mira glanced at him suspiciously as she stiffened slightly.
He raised his hand and before she could ask another question, his thumb brushed gently across her sexy and Lucious lips.
Mira instantly froze.
Dexter wiped away the small streak of strawberry ice cream, his thumb remained there for half a second before he pulled away.
Mira stared at him.
Dexter looked at the ice cream on his thumb. And then gazed deeply into Mira’s eyes and then placed his thumb in his mouth slowly licking the strawberry ice cream away.
Mira’s eyes widened as she stared at Dexter’s finger and then his lips and then his eyes.
Her heart suddenly skipped and then pounded hard as her face flushed red.
"Thump. Thump. Thump."
Dexter’s enhanced hearing caught every beat as he smirked. "There."
Mira stared. "You..."
Dexter had already walked back behind her. He grabbed the wheelchair handles. "All clean."
"Dexter!"
"What?"
Mira stopped. What exactly was she supposed to say?
Behind them, Selene wore an expression of surprise. Lyra had completely stopped eating. Her eyes moved from Mira to Dexter. Then back to Mira.
Dexter pretended nothing had happened. "Let’s keep moving."
He pushed the wheelchair forward.
For several seconds, none of the women spoke.
Dexter’s smile grew as he saw Mira’s ears were still red.
’Just three days should be enough.’
Dexter smirked at his thought.
Several minutes later, they passed one of the game areas. Dexter’s attention initially went toward a shooting booth. Then he noticed Mira looking elsewhere.

Her gaze had settled on a row of claw machines. Inside were stuffed animals of different sizes. Cats. Dragons. Bears. Rabbits. Several strange monster plushies. And at the back of one machine sat five enormous white teddy bear.
Mira’s eyes lingered and Dexter noticed as he spoke. "Want one?"
Mira immediately looked away. "No."
Dexter smiled. "That wasn’t convincing."
"I wasn’t looking at anything."
"Of course."
Dexter turned the wheelchair.
Mira frowned. "What are you doing?"
"Getting you a teddy bear."
"I don’t need a teddy bear."
"Great. Then I’ll get one for myself, Selene and Lyra."
Lyra immediately smiled and Selene followed.
Fortunately, there was nobody waiting. A young attendant sat behind the counter.
"How much?"
"2 Dollars per attempt."
Dexter paid. Before beginning, he noticed glowing symbols around the machine.
"A suppression formation?"

chapters.title: Chapter 259 | First Try
paragraphs: "A formation?"
The attendant nodded. "Prevents people from using cultivation abilities or talents to manipulate the claw. Otherwise every Hero would just cheat."
Dexter smiled. "Fair."
Inside the marked playing zone, direct talents couldn’t interfere with the machine. This was purely about coordination.
Dexter cracked his fingers. "Watch and learn."
Mira immediately looked amused. "That confidence usually comes before disaster."
Dexter ignored her. He grabbed the controls.
The claw moved. Left. Forward.
He positioned it above a brown teddy bear. "Easy."
He pressed the button. The claw descended. Grabbed the bear. Lifted.
Dexter smiled triumphantly.
Then the bear slipped.
Plop.
Mira laughed.
Dexter stared blankly through the glass and then said shamelessly. "The machine is probably defective."
The attendant glanced at Dexter and coughed. "It isn’t."
Dexter ignored him and paid again then attempted it a second time.
He missed again.
"My hand slipped."
The third time, the claw caught a rabbit by one ear.
Dexter licked his lips as he gently moved the control.
"Juuuuuust a little more."
Then it slipped.
By now Mira and Selene were openly laughing and Lyra’s mental laughter rang through Dexter’s head.
’You’re terrible at this.’
Dexter turned back and glared at her. "You try."
’Gladly.’
"I’m not finished yet."
By the fifth attempt, the claw actually descended as he grabbed and lifted it.
This time, a small black teddy bear dropped into the collection slot.
Dexter raised both hands. "Hahaha! In your face!"
Selene looked at the tiny bear then at Dexter. "That’s your great victory?"
Dexter smiled smugly as he poked the teddy bear. "It’s not about the size but about technique."
"Dexter!"
Mira glared at him and Selene face flushed slightly but Lyra seemed invested in her ice cream as Dexter smirked.
Dexter chuckled as spoke. "Selene, you try."
Selene glanced at him. "You’re trying to bully me."
Dexter raised an eyebrow and said innocently. "If you can’t beat me, you can say so."
Selene glared at Dexter. "Hmph."
She stepped toward the controls and placed her hands on them the claw motor hummed as Selene listened carefully.
The claw descended and she missed the first time.
Second attempt, she adjusted based on the sounds. The claw dropped and she actually grabbed a blue bear and actually lifted it.
Dexter’s mouth opened as the bear dropped into the chute.
Selene reached down and retrieved it and it was even nearly twice the size of Dexter’s!
Mira burst out laughing.
Dexter stared at his tiny bear. Then at Selene’s.
"Beginner’s luck."
Selene smiled sweetly. "Of course."
Lyra stepped forward. ’Me.’
Dexter sighed. "You too?"
She nodded eagerly.
"Fine."
He paid.
Lyra attacked the machine with frightening determination and it wasn’t until her 8th attempt before she actually managed to get something.
By her 10th time, she actually managed to get two more plushies and hugged them proudly.
Dexter looked down at his single tiny bear. "I think the machine is sexist."
Lyra chuckled.
Then everyone looked toward Mira.
Mira noticed and she immediately shook her head. "No."
Dexter raised an eyebrow. "No?"
"This is childish."
Dexter smiled and leaned toward her. "Just say you can’t do it."
Mira’s eyes sharpened. "I said it’s childish."
"There’s nothing wrong with admitting you’re scared of losing."
"Scared?"
"Terrified."
Mira’s crimson eyes narrowed.
Dexter smiled. "Don’t worry. We’ll understand."
Mira extended her recovered right hand. "Move."
Dexter stepped aside immediately. "That’s the spirit."
Mira moved in front of the stuff and a faint spectral hand manifested beside her.

The game formation prevented talents from directly interfering with the claw or prizes themselves, but Mira could still use the spectral construct as an extension to operate the external controls, provided she wasn’t manipulating anything inside the machine.
She moved the claw and suddenly it grabbed a teddy bear and moved it. "Plop!"
Silence.
Mira looked at Dexter’s stunned face.
A slow, victorious smile spread across her face. "First try."
Dexter stared at the bear. It was smaller than his. But that suddenly seemed irrelevant.
Mira picked it up with her recovered right hand. "See?"
Dexter narrowed his eyes.
"The bear is tiny."
Selene and Lyra covered their mouth and laughed.
Dexter stared at the three women. "So that’s how it is?"
Mira hugged the little crimson bear against herself. "Accept defeat gracefully.
Dexter slowly smiled. "Defeat?"
Something about that smile made Mira suspicious. "Dexter."
He turned toward the attendant.
The attendant looked back.
Dexter pointed toward the enormous human-sized teddy bear displayed behind the counter. "How much for that?"
The attendant blinked. "It’s not technically for sale."
Dexter took out one hundred dollars. "Now?"
The attendant shook his head.
Dexter increased it to five hundred.
The attendant hesitated.
Mira stared at him. "Dexter, don’t you dare."
Dexter placed one thousand dollars on the counter.
The attendant’s eyes widened. He immediately grabbed the massive teddy bear. "Congratulations, sir!"
Mira’s mouth dropped open. Selene blinked. Lyra stared.
Dexter accepted the enormous bear. It was almost as tall as he was.
He turned toward his wives with the most shameless smile imaginable. "See?"
He hugged the giant bear. "I won."
Silence.
Mira’s eye twitched. Selene’s mouth opened. Lyra stared at him as though he’d committed a crime.
Then all three reacted.
"That’s cheating!" Mira snapped.
Selene nodded firmly. "Definitely cheating."
Lyra’s voice blasted through Dexter’s mind. ’Cheater!’
Dexter laughed. "Only the result matters."
Mira glared. "You bought it!"
"And who possesses the largest teddy bear?"
"That’s not the game!"
"The process is irrelevant. History only remembers winners."
Selene turned away from him. Lyra folded her arms and pouted. Mira looked genuinely offended on behalf of claw-machine players everywhere.
Dexter raised the teddy bear and continued laughing.
Then he noticed something. Lyra’s pout deepened. Selene still refused to look at him. Even Mira had crossed her recovered arm over herself as much as she comfortably could.
Dexter’s laughter slowly stopped. "...Seriously?"
No response.
Dexter looked at the attendant. The attendant was desperately trying not to laugh.
Dexter sighed. "Fine."
He reached into his pocket. "How much for the other two giant bears?"
The attendant’s professionalism immediately returned.
Dexter paid another two thousand dollars. The man’s smile became radiant enough to illuminate the festival.
"Excellent choice, sir."
