chapters.title: Chapter 260 | The Scary Manor
paragraphs: Three massive bears were presented. One was white, another blue, and the third orange.
He grabbed the white bear first. "Lyra."
She looked at him.
He held it toward her. "This is yours."
Her pout disappeared instantly. Her eyes lit up. ’Mine?’
"Yes."
Lyra practically attacked the bear. She wrapped both arms around it. It was almost so large that half her body disappeared behind it.
Her delighted mental voice immediately reached Dexter. ’I love it!’
Dexter laughed. "Traitor. Five seconds ago you were angry."
Lyra ignored him. She buried her face into the bear.
Dexter took the blue one. "Selene."
Selene slowly turned. He placed her hands against the soft fur. Her fingers moved across it.
"It’s huge."
"Almost your size."
Selene examined its form before embracing it. A gentle smile emerged on her face. "Thank you."
Dexter’s expression softened. "You’re welcome."
Finally, the crimson bear. Dexter turned toward Mira.
She deliberately looked away. "I don’t want it."
"Certainly."
"I mean it."
"Absolutely."
Dexter placed the bear where she could see it.
Mira’s crimson eyes gave her away at once, shifting toward the bear, then away, then back again.
Dexter remained silent.
Mira kept staring; the bear wore a small black bow around its neck and had embroidered golden eyes.
Mira’s resistance lasted seven seconds before she spoke. "Fine."
Mira smiled. "I’ll forgive you."
Dexter raised an eyebrow. "You’re forgiving me?"
"You cheated."
"I bought you a giant bear."
"Compensation for your crime."
Dexter laughed. "Whatever helps you sleep."
He carefully positioned the teddy bear with her, ensuring it didn’t interfere with her comfort or wheelchair.
Mira’s recovered arm slowly curled around it.
Dexter observed the situation. He kept silent, yet his smile persisted.
The former Crimson Valkyrie, once an elite Hero feared throughout the dungeons, is now embracing an enormous crimson teddy bear.
If he’d possessed a camera...
Mira’s eyes suddenly narrowed. "Don’t.
Dexter froze. "Don’t what?"
"Whatever you’re thinking."
"I wasn’t thinking anything."
"Liar."
"I’m beginning to think you read minds."
Dexter looked at her suspiciously.
The four left the claw-machine stall looking ridiculous.

Lyra carried an enormous white teddy bear along with three smaller plushies. Selene had her blue bear. Mira had the crimson one positioned with her wheelchair. Dexter carried his pathetic little black teddy bear.
He looked at it. The bear stared back.
"At least you and I understand each other."
Mira chuckled. "You could have simply bought yourself another large one."
"No."
Dexter held the tiny bear higher. "I earned this."
Selene smiled. "After five attempts."
"Nobody asked you."
Lyra’s voice entered his mind. ’Mine only took three.’
"You took ten attempts!"
’I got three bears.’
"That’s not the point."
Mira added, "Mine took one."
Dexter stopped pushing. "Would everyone like to stop attacking me?"
"No," Mira answered.
Selene smiled. Lyra shook her head.
Dexter sighed. Marriage was dangerous.
He resumed walking. Despite his complaints, he couldn’t stop smiling.
The three women were different today. Not completely. Their scars hadn’t disappeared and their illnesses weren’t magically gone.
But they had changed compared to the past few months.
They looked... really happy.
Dexter slowed slightly.

When he’d first met them, happiness had seemed almost foreign to all three. Mira had been bitter and exhausted. Selene had been trapped in pain and darkness. Lyra had hidden almost everything behind an unreadable expression.
Yet today...
Dexter’s gaze moved between them. He felt something warm settle inside his chest.
Maybe healing wasn’t only about repairing meridians. Maybe it wasn’t only medicine, cultivation, bloodlines, talents and expensive ingredients.
Maybe sometimes healing being outside beneath the sun after spending too long believing there was nothing outside worth seeing.
Dexter smiled.
Then Mira spoke. "Where are we going now?"
He snapped from his thoughts. "Right."
He looked ahead. They had three original options: roller coaster, laser tag, and haunted house.
Dexter remembered Lyra’s enthusiasm earlier. A grin slowly appeared. "Haunted house."
Selene stopped, Mira raised an eyebrow and Lyra’s eyes lit up.
’Yes!’
Dexter pointed toward the enormous dark building ahead. It had been designed to resemble a ruined mansion.
Black towers rose above twisted artificial trees. Thick mist crawled across the ground around its entrance. Broken windows flickered with dim red light, while occasionally a shadow moved behind them.
A sign hung above the entrance.
NIGHTMARE MANOR
Below it: ENTER IF YOU DARE.
Dexter stared at it.
A woman’s scream suddenly erupted from inside and then an absolutely terrifying laughter.
Mira looked toward him. "Still confident?"
Dexter scoffed. "It’s fake."
Another scream came from the building.
And then a mechanical growl as sounds of chains dragging and something scraping against a wall. Then what sounded suspiciously like a child’s laughter.
Dexter’s smile became slightly stiff.
Mira noticed immediately. "Scared?"
"Me?"
Dexter straightened. "Never."
Selene tilted her head. "Your heartbeat changed."
Dexter looked at her. "Whose side are you on?"
Selene smiled. "The truth’s."
Lyra’s mental laughter echoed.
Dexter shook his head. "Fine."
He pushed Mira toward Nightmare Manor. "Let’s see who’s laughing when we come back out."
Lyra eagerly followed. Selene hugged her blue teddy bear and walked beside them.
Mira looked toward the looming haunted mansion. For a brief moment, Dexter saw something in her expression that resembled excitement.
His smiled as they approached the entrance together. Four people who, only months earlier, they had barely known how to exist in the same house. Now the were closer than they should have been.
Dexter looked at his wives. "One rule."
Mira glanced back. "What?"
"If anyone gets scared..." He grinned. "You can hold onto me."
Mira rolled her eyes. Selene smiled.
Lyra’s voice immediately entered his head. ’What if you’re the one who gets scared?’
Dexter smirked as he pointed toward himself proudly. "Like you always said, I’m not an ordinary person."
Mira’s smile became dangerous. "That wasn’t the question."
Dexter cleared his throat. "Let’s just go inside."
Mira and Lyra chuckled as they followed Dexter into the manor.
If his plan works, then they would clutch until him tightly anytime they were scared. As for him getting scared, Dexter didn’t think it would happen.
He already knew it’s fake in the first place.

He grabbed the white bear first.
She wrapped both arms around it.

Her delighted mental voice immediately reached Dexter. ’I love it!’

Mira’s resistance lasted seven seconds before she spoke.

The former Crimson Valkyrie, once an elite Hero feared throughout the dungeons, is now embracing an enormous crimson teddy bear.

The four left the claw-machine stall looking ridiculous.
Lyra carried an enormous white teddy bear along with three smaller plushies.

"At least you and I understand each other."

Despite his complaints, he couldn’t stop smiling.
The three women were different today.

They had three original options: roller coaster, laser tag, and haunted house.

Below it: ENTER IF YOU DARE.

chapters.title: Chapter 261 | I’m Not Scared!
paragraphs: The entrance to Nightmare Manor swallowed the sunlight almost immediately.
One moment, Dexter was standing beneath the bright afternoon sky with music, laughter, and the roar of the festival surrounding him. The next, darkness wrapped around the four of them.
The temperature dropped. A cold artificial breeze drifted across Dexter’s face.
Behind them, the entrance doors slammed shut.
"BANG!"
Dexter stopped pushing Mira’s wheelchair. Selene stopped beside him. Lyra froze on his left.
Mira slowly looked over her shoulder. "Scared already?"
Dexter scoffed. "That?" He pointed backward. "Cheap trick."
A low whisper suddenly came from somewhere directly beside his ear.
"Get... out..."
Dexter’s head snapped around. Nothing.
Mira’s lips twitched.
Dexter cleared his throat. "Still cheap."
Lyra’s melodious voice entered his mind. ’Your shoulders jumped.’
"They did not."
’They did.’
"Must have been the floor."
Mira chuckled. "The floor frightened you?"
"I didn’t say that."
Selene’s smile appeared in the darkness. "You should stop talking before you make it worse."
Dexter stared at his three wives. "We’ve been inside for twenty seconds and you three are bullying me."
"The wives should bully the husband to sometimes." Mira replied calmly.
Dexter shook his head and resumed pushing her.

They had been required to leave their enormous teddy bears with an attendant at the entrance, something Lyra had been very reluctant to do. She had eventually surrendered hers only after receiving a numbered token and making the attendant promise twice that nobody would touch it.
Now they had nothing but the candy they’d brought inside. And each other.
The corridor ahead was barely illuminated.
Flickering candles hung along the walls, though Dexter suspected the flames weren’t real.
Ancient-looking paintings covered the faded wallpaper. Several depicted stern men and women dressed in clothing from centuries earlier.
Every few seconds, lightning flashed outside artificial windows. Thunder followed.
"BOOM!"
Dexter glanced around. He had to admit it. The place was impressive. The sounds were especially convincing.

With his enhanced hearing, however, Dexter could distinguish the mechanisms hidden behind the walls. Gears. Motors. Speakers. Pressure plates. He could even hear several employees breathing in concealed spaces.
Dexter smiled. ’This is going to be easy.’
He pushed Mira forward confidently.
A portrait beside him suddenly screamed.
"AAAAAAAH!"
Dexter jumped.
Mira burst out laughing. Lyra grabbed her stomach. Even Selene laughed.
Dexter glared at the portrait. The previously serious-looking painted woman now had black eyes and a mouth stretched impossibly wide.
"That’s cheating."
Mira looked back. "How?"
"I was analyzing the architecture."
"Of course.
"I was."
Selene tilted her head. "You screamed a little."
Dexter stopped and glared at her. "Men don’t scream, I absolutely did not scream."
"You made a sound."
"What sound?"
Selene imitated him. "Uh!"
Mira laughed harder.
Dexter stared at Selene. "I liked you better when you couldn’t tell where I was."
Selene smiled sweetly. "I can hear your heartbeat."
"Stop listening to my heartbeat."
"I can’t exactly turn my ears off."
Dexter muttered something under his breath and continued.
Lyra tapped his shoulder. He turned. ’Uh!’ She imitated his startled expression.
Dexter’s eyes narrowed. "Keep laughing." Lyra smiled. "I’m remembering this."
She gave him an innocent look.
Dexter pointed at her. "Especially you."
They continued deeper.

Despite all the teasing, Dexter was paying careful attention to the three women. Especially Selene. The haunted house was almost completely dark. Yet strangely, she seemed to be navigating it better than the bright festival grounds outside.
Air moved through corridors. Mira’s wheelchair rolled across wooden floors. Lyra’s dress brushed against her legs. Dexter’s breathing remained steady beside her.
To Selene, each sound returned information. Distance. Shape. Direction. Space. The world existed around her without needing light.
She avoided the corner of a decorative table without touching it.
Dexter noticed. His smile returned. The medicine really was working.
They entered a larger room. A sign above the doorway read: THE DINING HALL.
An enormous banquet table occupied the center. Twelve mannequins sat around it. Every mannequin wore old-fashioned clothing. Their heads were bowed.
Mira looked around. "I don’t like this."
Dexter grinned proudly. "Scared alredy ?"
"No."
"You sound scared."
"I’m stating an observation."
"That’s exactly what a scared person would say."
Mira gave him a cold look.
Dexter’s grin widened. Finally.
They moved farther into the room. Nothing happened. Ten meters. Still nothing.
Dexter began becoming suspicious. "That’s strange."
Selene turned her head. "What?"
"They’ve been too quiet."
Mira immediately frowned. "Why would you say that?"
Dexter looked around. "I mean, obviously something is going to—"
Every mannequin’s head suddenly snapped upward.
"CLACK!"
Lyra jumped backward. Selene flinched. Mira’s eyes widened.
Dexter grinned. "Got you."
Mira glared at him. "You jumped earlier."
"Ancient history.
The mannequins slowly turned their heads toward them. One. Then another. Then another. Until twelve pale faces were staring directly at the group.
A child’s voice whispered through the room. "Would you..."
The lights flickered. "...like..."
The mannequins’ mouths opened. "...to stay for dinner?"
Lyra moved closer to Dexter. He noticed. "Oh?"
Lyra immediately stopped.
Dexter smiled. "Someone’s scared."
’No.’
Lyra glared at him.
Dexter laughed. Then something grabbed his ankle. "WHAT THE—"
He nearly kicked downward before his brain caught up. A skeletal hand had emerged beneath the table.
Dexter stared at it. The hand released him and disappeared.
Silence.
Mira slowly looked at Dexter. Selene turned toward his voice. Lyra’s eyes widened.
Dexter straightened. "No."
Mira’s smile appeared. "No what?"
"Whatever you’re about to say."
"I haven’t said anything."
"You don’t need to."
Mira smiled innocently. "Interesting."
Dexter resumed pushing her. "Moving on."

The next section was considerably darker. A narrow corridor twisted between artificial stone walls. Red emergency lights glowed along the floor. The sound of dripping water echoed from somewhere ahead.
Drip. Drip. Drip.
Then came the dragging.
"Scrrrrrape."
Pause.
"Scrrrrrape."
Dexter frowned as he heard something heavy was being pulled across the floor.
Selene moved closer. "That’s ahead."
"About thirty meters," Dexter replied.
"Twenty-seven."
Dexter looked at her. Selene smiled. "Approximately."
Mira glanced between them. "You two are competing now?"
"No," Dexter said.
"Yes," Selene said simultaneously.
Dexter stared at her and Selene’s smile widened.

They rounded the corner to find a figure at the end of the hallway. Dexter assumed it was a man, given the sheer size. A bloodstained butcher’s apron covered his body, while a sack covered his face. One hand gripped a massive cleaver, and the other dragged a metal chain.
Mira eent silent, lyra stared and Selene whispered, "What’s there?"
Dexter looked at the figure. "Just a very ugly man."
The figure tilted its head. Then charged.
Mira’s eyes widened. "Dexter!"

chapters.title: Chapter 262 | Meeting Tessa Again
paragraphs: Dexter didn’t move. The butcher sprinted toward them like a bullet.
Lyra grabbed Dexter’s arm as the butcher raised the cleaver wns slashed at then with full force.
"CLANG!"
It struck the wall beside Dexter.
Lyra squeezed his arm tightly and Mira’s right hand clenched against the wheelchair as she leaned backwards towards him. Even Selene flinched from the sound as she moved closer to him.
The butcher leaned toward Dexter. Through the holes in his mask, Dexter could see the employee’s eyes.
Dexter smiled. "Good costume."
The butcher paused. Then slowly pointed toward the next corridor.
Dexter nodded. "Thank you."
He pushed Mira past. The butcher remained motionless.
Once they were safely around the corner, Mira looked backward. "You knew?"
"Yup, I paid him." Dexter smirked.
Selene immediately tilted her chin toward Dexter. "Cheating."
Dexter stopped. "What?"
Mira turned backwards and glared at him. "Cheater."
Lyra nodded. ’Cheater.’
Dexter looked betrayed. "You three are enjoying this far too much."
Mira harrumped. "You cheated at the claw machine and you’re cheating here too."
"I did not cheat."
Mira rolled her eyes.
They eventually reached a room labeled THE MIRROR MAZE.
Dexter stared at the entrance. "No."
Mira immediately became interested. "What’s wrong?"
"Nothing."
"Then let’s enter."
Dexter narrowed his eyes. "You said that too quickly."
Mira smiled. "Push."
They entered.
Mirrors surrounded them everywhere. The lighting was dim enough that reflections seemed to appear and disappear depending on where they moved.
Dexter immediately hated it. His hearing wasn’t as useful because sound bounced everywhere.
Selene, strangely, seemed delighted. "This is fascinating."
Dexter looked at her. "You’re enjoying the mirror maze?"
"I can’t see the mirrors."
Dexter paused. "...That’s unfair."
Selene covered her mouth and giggled.
She moved carefully beside them. Her fingers didn’t even touch the walls. Instead, she clicked her tongue softly.
Tick.
The sound bounced and Selene turned. "This way."
Dexter blinked. "Are you serious?"
She walked forward and Dexter followed.
Ten seconds later they hit a dead end.
Mira laughed.
Dexter folded his arms. Selene frowned. "Interesting."
"You were saying?"
"The reflections change the acoustics."
"So we’re lost."
"No."
Five minutes later, they were definitely lost.
Dexter stood at an intersection surrounded by twelve versions of himself. Mira’s wheelchair was reflected dozens of times. Lyra stared at her own reflections.
Selene stood peacefully beside them.
Dexter sighed. "Who designed this place?"
Mira answered, "Someone considerably smarter than you.
Dexter looked down. "You know, I could leave you here."
"No, you couldn’t."
"Why not?"
"You’d come back after thirty seconds."
Dexter opened his mouth and glared at her. "If you weren’t my wife, I would definitely leave you here for sure.."
Mira lips curled up. "Exactly."
Dexter snorted and continued searching.
Suddenly Lyra grabbed his sleeve. He looked over as she pointed.
One reflection wasn’t copying them.
Dexter’s smile vanished. In the mirror stood a pale woman. Long black hair covered her face. She was standing behind them.
Dexter slowly turned. Nothing.
He looked back. The woman was closer.
Lyra’s eyes widened. ’Dexter.’
"I see her."
Mira looked. "What?"
The lights suddenly went out and there was pitch darkness.
Something whispered directly behind them. "Found you."
Lyra grabbed Dexter and Mira gasped as selene jumped towards him.
Dexter’s Flame Will nearly activated instinctively before he stopped himself.
The lights returned and the pale woman was gone.
For several seconds, nobody spoke.
Then Dexter felt something. Lyra’s arms were wrapped around one of his.
He slowly looked down. Lyra followed his gaze. Then looked up at him.
Dexter smiled.
Lyra immediately released him. ’Hmph.’
"I haven’t said anything."
’Don’t.’
Dexter grinned. "Was someone scared?"
Lyra punched his shoulder.
"Ouch!"
She glared.
Dexter laughed. "Fine. Fine."
They eventually escaped the mirror maze with Selene’s help. Dexter would never admit that part.
The final section was called THE CATACOMBS.
Fake stone coffins lined the corridor. Skeletons hung from chains. Green flames flickered from wall sconces.
Dexter pushed Mira forward. Mira had become increasingly relaxed. The first few scares had startled her. Now she seemed to be anticipating them.
"That coffin will open," she said.
Dexter looked. "How do you know?"
"It’s obvious."
They passed. Nothing happened.
Mira frowned.
Dexter smiled.
Then the coffin behind them exploded open.
"BANG!"
Mira jumped.
Dexter laughed. "I thought it was obvious?"
"Shut up."
A skeleton dropped from the ceiling. Dexter ducked. Lyra stepped sideways. Selene didn’t react.
Dexter stared at her. "How did you know?"
"I heard the cable.
Dexter pointed accusingly. "Cheater."
Selene smiled. "Strategic awareness."
Mira burst out laughing. "She’s learning from you."
"Unfortunately."
They continued.
Then a low growl came from ahead. Three pairs of glowing red eyes appeared in the darkness.
Dexter stopped. The growling grew louder. Something moved.
Lyra stepped closer. Mira stared ahead. Selene tilted her head.
"Mechanical."
Dexter nodded. "Definitely."
Three enormous wolf-like creatures suddenly leapt from hidden compartments.
Mira screamed. Lyra grabbed Dexter again. Dexter flinched. Selene merely blinked.
The wolves stopped on concealed rails before reaching them.
Dexter looked at Selene. She looked toward him. "That wasn’t scary."
Mira glared. "You can’t see them!"
Selene’s expression became thoughtful. "That’s probably helping."
Dexter laughed so hard he had to stop pushing the wheelchair. Even Mira eventually began laughing.
For several moments, the four of them simply stood there laughing in the artificial darkness.
And Dexter realized something. This was the loudest he’d ever heard them together. Not screaming. Not arguing. Not crying out from pain.
Laughing.
Mira was laughing without bitterness. Selene was laughing without exhaustion. Lyra couldn’t produce the sound yet, but Dexter could hear her laughter clearly inside his mind.
Something tightened pleasantly in his chest. He wanted more days like this. No dungeons. No families. No enemies. No systems demanding advancement.
Just them.
Eventually, a glowing sign appeared ahead. EXIT.
Dexter raised both hands. "We survived."
Mira looked up. "Your bravery was inspiring."
"Thank you."
"Especially when the painting scared you."
Dexter’s smile disappeared. "Why are we returning to that?"
Selene added, "And the skeleton hand."
"Nobody asked you."
Lyra’s voice entered his head. ’Uh!’
She imitated him again.
Dexter glared. "I regret bringing all of you."
Mira smiled. "No, you don’t."
Dexter paused, then he smiled. "No I don’t."
He pushed her toward the exit. "I don’t."
The doors opened and Sunlight flooded over them.
Dexter squinted as the sounds of the festival returned at full force.
After the artificial cold of Nightmare Manor, the afternoon warmth felt wonderful.

They collected their giant teddy bears from the attendant. Lyra immediately hugged hers. Selene ran her fingers across the blue bear as though confirming nobody had switched it. Mira’s orange bear was carefully returned to her.
Dexter looked at the ridiculous group. "I still can’t believe I’m carrying stuffed animals around."
Mira looked at his tiny black bear. "Yours is the smallest."
Dexter’s expression darkened. "Why are you obsessed with attacking my bear?"
"Because it’s funny."
Dexter was about to answer when someone called from nearby.
"Dexter?"
He stopped. That voice was familiar.
Dexter turned. A young woman was standing several meters away, holding a large picnic basket with both hands.
His eyebrows rose. "Tessa?"

chapters.title: Chapter 263 | I Will Hold Your Hand Through It All
paragraphs: "Dexter?"
He stopped as that voice sounded familiar.
Dexter turned to see a young woman was standing several meters away, holding a large picnic basket with both hands.
His eyebrows rose. "Tessa?"
Tessa smiled as she stared at him then at his wives.
"Hello Dexter."
Then she looked at the Lyra, then Selene, then at Mira and then at the enormous teddy bears they were holding and then at Dexter’s tiny bear.
Her expression became increasingly strange.
Dexter blinked his eyes and looked down at himself and then glared at Tessa. "What?"
Tessa’s lips twitched. "Nothing."
Then she suddenly burst out giggling.
Dexter sighed. "Apparently everyone has decided to bully me today."
Tessa approached them. "I wasn’t expecting to find you coming out of the haunted house. Seems like you’re enjoying your self here."
Tessa smiled as she continued. "Welcome to our neighborhood."
Dexter chuckled and nodded his head.
Tessa’s attention moved toward the three women. Her expression brightened. "You brought everyone."
Dexter nodded as he spoke. "You’ve already met them briefly, but I don’t think you’ve had a proper chance to talk."
Tessa smiled warmly. "Hello."
Mira nodded politely. "Hello, Tessa."
Selene smiled. "Hello."
Lyra couldn’t speak aloud, so she smiled and raised her hand in greeting. Tessa returned the gesture.
Then she noticed something else and her eyes widened.
"Mira..."
Mira raised an eyebrow.
Tessa pointed toward her right arm. "You’re moving it."
Mira looked down. Her recovered hand rested against the crimson teddy bear then she shrugged.
"Yes."
Tessa stared. "That’s incredible."
Dexter smiled.
Tessa lifted her picnic basket. "I was actually looking for you."
Dexter raised an eyebrow. "For me?"
"For your food."
Dexter’s face went blank.
Tessa pointed toward the main picnic field. "People have already started exchanging dishes. Granny Lucy has been asking where you are because I told her you’d be bringing something."
Dexter scratched his cheek. "We got distracted."
Tessa looked toward Nightmare Manor. "Clearly."
Tessa laughed. "When you’re done having fun, we have a spot that isn’t far from yours.
She began walking beside them. Dexter pushed Mira. Lyra and Selene followed.
For a moment, Tessa simply looked at the four of them. There was something noticeably different from the last time she’d visited Dexter’s house.

They weren’t merely standing near one another anymore. They moved naturally as a group. Dexter automatically slowed whenever Selene did. Lyra stayed close enough to help Selene when necessary. Mira occasionally tilted her head backward to speak to Dexter. And Dexter constantly checked all three without appearing to realize he was doing it.
Tessa smiled. "So?"
Dexter glanced toward her. "So what?"
"Are you enjoying the festival?"
Before Dexter could answer, Mira spoke. "It’s acceptable."
Dexter looked down at her. "Acceptable?"
Mira’s lips curled. "Fine." She hugged the crimson teddy bear slightly closer. "It’s fun."
Dexter smiled.
Selene nodded. "I like it."
Lyra’s voice entered Dexter’s mind. ’Tell her I love it.’
Dexter looked toward her. "You can tell her yourself."
Lyra stared.
Dexter pointed toward Tessa, then mimed typing. Lyra understood. She pulled out her phone and typed quickly before showing Tessa.
[I love it.]
Tessa smiled. "I’m glad."
Then her eyes moved toward Dexter. "And you?"
Dexter looked around at his wives and smiled.
"It’s been a good day."
Tessa grinned. "Good."
Then she pointed toward the picnic field. "Because your peaceful day is about to end."
Dexter frowned. "Why?"
Tessa’s smile became suspicious. "Everyone’s been waiting to taste the new neighbor’s cooking."
Dexter stared at the packed field ahead. Then at Tessa. Then toward the cooler waiting at their picnic spot.
His eyes narrowed. "How many people did you tell about my food?"
Tessa suddenly found the waterfall fascinating.
"Tessa."
Then started walking faster.
"Tessa!"
Mira laughed. Selene smiled. Lyra followed eagerly, apparently delighted by the possibility of more food.
Dexter sighed and pushed Mira to the next event.
The roller coaster looked considerably less friendly up close.

The steel tracks towered high above the surrounding trees, twisting into steep climbs, sudden drops, loops, and corkscrews that looked suspiciously designed by someone who disliked the human spine. A train screamed overhead, and the sound of riders shrieking followed it around the bend.
Dexter slowly raised his head as the train vanished, then looked at his wives. "So."
Mira stared upward with obvious interest while Lyra’s violet eyes practically sparkled. But Selene had gone very quiet, and that made Dexter pause.
"Selene?"
She tilted her head toward him. "I’m fine."
Dexter narrowed his eyes. "I didn’t ask if you were fine."
"You were going to."
"True."

Another train climbed the massive first hill, the mechanical clicking of the chain filling the air. Selene followed the sound upward, her face slowly tilting higher and higher until the train plunged and screams erupted from somewhere above them. She immediately shook her head.
"No."
Dexter blinked. "No?"
"No."
Mira looked toward her, and Lyra stopped eating the last piece of candy she’d been carrying. Selene shook her head again.
"I’ve changed my mind."
Dexter almost smiled, because this was possibly the first time he’d heard Selene sound genuinely nervous about something that wasn’t related to the fact that they sleep together.
"What happened to wanting to try everything?"
"That was before I knew how high it is."
Dexter looked up at the towering structure and chuckled. "It’s not that high."
She folded her arms. "You’re lying. I might be blind but I can still basically see."
Mira laughed, and Selene’s cheeks warmed.
Dexter blinked his eyes. "You’re scared of heights.
Selene paused and nodded her head quietly.
Dexter’s teasing expression immediately softened, because that changed things. He stepped closer. "We don’t have to go."
Selene paused, and both Mira and Lyra looked at Dexter. He shrugged. "Seriously. This is supposed to be fun. If you don’t want to ride it, we’ll pick something else."
Selene remained silent. Instead of immediately agreeing, she lowered her head.
"I...I want to."
He raised an eyebrow. "But you’re scared."
"Yes."
"And you still want to ride?"
Selene nodded slowly. "I’ve spent too long being unable to do things."
That wiped the smile from Dexter’s face, and Selene’s fingers tightened slightly around the hem of her dress. "I don’t want fear to become another reason."

For several seconds, Dexter simply looked at her. Then he smiled. "All right." He extended his hand, but when Selene couldn’t see the gesture clearly, he gently took her hand instead. Her fingers stiffened for an instant before relaxing inside his.
"I’ll hold your hand through all of it."
Selene’s expression softened. "All of it?"
"From the moment we sit down until the moment the ride stops."
"What if you get scared?"

chapters.title: Chapter 264 | It’s Beautiful
paragraphs: Dexter looked offended. "Why does everyone keep asking me that?"
Mira lips curled upwards. "The haunted house."
Dexter rolled his eyes. "That was only one time."
Lyra shook her head vigorously then held up three fingers.
Dexter glared at her. "Traitor."
Dexter turned to Selene. "Ignore them."
He gently squeezed her hand and spoke softly. "Don’t worry. I won’t let go."
Selene’s smile became shy. "Okay."
Mira watched the exchange before looking away, but he noticed.
Dexter leaned toward her. "Scared?"
Mira’s crimson eyes narrowed. "Of a roller coaster? I fought monsters for a living."
Dexter smirked.
"Yet somehow you’re avoiding the question. Don’t worry, I will hold your hand too."
Mira stared at him while Dexter smiled, and she finally pointed toward the queue. "Push."
"Yes, Your Majesty."
"Dexter."
He laughed and pushed her toward the entrance.
The queue was surprisingly long. Dexter didn’t understand humanity, but unfortunately, he was beginning to look forward to it too.
They joined the line, and Lyra immediately leaned around the people ahead as she looked excitedly at the train.
Dexter watched her with amusement.
"You’re enjoying this before we’ve even gotten on."
She nodded. ’’It looks fun.’’
"You’re strange."
Lyra’s lips curled as her voice resonated in Dexter’s mind. ’You married me.’
Dexter froze, and Mira’s head snapped around while Selene’s eyebrows rose. Lyra herself seemed to realize what she’d just said, her eyes widening slightly, but Dexter slowly smiled.
"Interesting."
Lyra looked away.
"Very interesting."
She focused intensely on the roller coaster, and Dexter chuckled. "Lyra?"
Nothing.
Mira sighed. "Leave her alone."
"Why?"
"Because your face is annoying."
Dexter looked down at her. "Jealous?"
Mira’s expression became dangerously calm. "Would you like me to test how much your skull has improved?
Dexter immediately faced forward. "Beautiful weather."
Selene laughed.
Eventually, they reached the front, which presented the first complication. Mira looked toward the roller-coaster carriage.
Dexter called for the ride attendant and explained to her.
The woman gave a reassuring smile.
"We can accommodate her," the woman explained. "The restraints are adjustable, and we’ll stop the loading platform until she’s secured."
Dexter nodded. "Good."
Mira glanced at him. "I can manage."
"I know."

That didn’t stop Dexter from moving beside her as the ride attendant locked the wheelchair in place. He bent down, and Mira’s recovered right arm moved around his shoulder as he carefully lifted her. She was becoming more accustomed to being carried by him—perhaps too accustomed, because weeks ago she would have glared at him throughout the entire process. Now she simply adjusted her arm around him and let him handle it.

Dexter carefully lowered her into the roller-coaster seat, and since her legs remained passive, he took extra care with their positioning before the attendant helped secure the specialized lower-body support.
"You comfortable?"
Mira shifted her upper body slightly. "Yes."
"Good."
He inspected the restraint himself anyway, and Mira rolled her eyes but didn’t complain again. Dexter straightened and looked at the carriage, which had four seats across.
Lyra immediately moved toward the far-left seat.
Lyra sat down, and Dexter shook his head. That left Mira beside her, then Dexter, then Selene—exactly what he’d promised.

Dexter took the center-right seat, leaving Mira on his left and Selene on his right. Selene sat carefully, but the moment she heard the restraint lowering, her entire body stiffened. The locking mechanism secured across her with a loud clack, and she swallowed.
"D-dexter..."
"I’m here."
His right hand immediately found hers, and she grabbed it hard. Dexter’s eyebrows rose, because for someone who had spent years sick, Selene possessed a surprisingly strong grip.
Mira was watching him, so Dexter extended his other hand. She stared at it. "What?"
"I promised."
"I never accepted."
"Then reject it."
Mira looked at his hand as the attendant moved down the carriage checking restraints, then slowly placed her recovered right hand into Dexter’s. He smiled.
"Say anything and I’ll let go."
"Understood."
Her fingers tightened, and Dexter’s smile widened while Mira glared at him.
Dexter said innocently. "I didn’t speak."
"Your face is irritating."
"Didn’t you call me handsome a few days ago?"
Mira snorted. "I must have been blind.
Dexter chuckled.
The attendant reached them and checked Mira’s specialized restraint first, then Dexter’s, then Selene’s, and finally Lyra’s. "Everyone comfortable?"
Dexter nodded, Lyra gave a thumbs-up, and Mira said, "Yes." Selene hesitated, but Dexter squeezed her hand, and she breathed slowly.
"Yes."
The attendant stepped away. "Enjoy your ride."
The platform gates closed, and Selene’s fingers tightened again. Dexter looked toward her. "You okay?"
"No."
He laughed softly. "At least you’re honest."

The carriage jerked, and Selene’s body trembled before it began moving. They left the station with the sunlight striking their faces, and Lyra immediately looked around excitedly while Mira leaned back.
Dexter held both women’s hands, but he let his thumb caress Selene’s hand softly to calm her nervousness.
The train reached the first incline and began climbing, the mechanical clicking of the chain filling the air.
At that moment, Selene became completely still, and Dexter could feel her hand tightening with every click as they ascended ten meters, then twenty, then thirty.

The festival gradually fell away beneath them, and Dexter looked around at the view from this height. The entire public garden was visible, with the enormous artificial waterfall glittering in the distance and families becoming tiny figures scattered across the green field.
Dexter smiled. "Selene."
"No."
He blinked. "I haven’t said anything."
"I know what you’re going to say."
"What?"
"That I should look."
Dexter glanced at her pale eyes. "Actually, yes."
"I can’t see properly."
"I know." The train continued climbing. "But you said you can see colors."
Selene hesitated, and Dexter squeezed her hand. "Don’t try to see everything." Her face slowly lifted. "Just tell me what you can see."
Selene swallowed, and for several seconds there was only the mechanical clicking of the chain beneath them. Then...
"Blue."
Dexter smiled. "The sky."
Selene’s expression changed. "There’s..." She turned her head slightly. "Green."
"That’s the garden."
Her lips parted, and something bright reflected across her slowly healing eyes. "White."
"The waterfall."

Selene became silent, and Dexter watched her. She couldn’t see the details, perhaps the festival below was nothing more than blurry patches of light and color, but she could see them. For someone who had lived in darkness, even blurred colors were a world returning piece by piece.
Selene’s grip loosened slightly. "It’s beautiful."
Dexter smiled. "Told you."

chapters.title: Chapter 265 | You Look Beautiful
paragraphs: At that moment, the clicking stopped and Selene froze, while Mira slowly looked ahead and Lyra’s eyes widened with excitement.
The front of the train had reached the peak, and for one impossible second, they hung above the world.
Selene whispered, "Why did it stop?"
Dexter looked down, at the very far down. He immediately knew what was coming and glanced at Selene.
Selene seemed to have sensed it and her grip immediately tightened. "Dexter."
"Yes?"
"What’s happening?"
Dexter blinked his eyes. "Nothing much..."
The carriage immediately tipped forward, and Selene’s face changed. "Dexter?"
Mira’s eyes widened, and Lyra grinned as gravity took them.
The train plunged with a violent whoosh, and Selene grip tightened as she closed her eyes tightly and let out a silent scream.
Mira squinted her eyes and her smile widened as she giggled happily while her hair flapped backwards through the air.
Lyra laughed and screamed happily. She couldn’t scream aloud, but her mental shriek detonated directly inside Dexter’s head.
’AAAAAAAAAAAAAA!’
"LYRA, NOT IN MY HEAD!"
The train accelerated, and wind slammed into them as Selene squeezed Dexter’s right hand with both terror while Mira’s recovered hand crushed his left. Dexter laughed through the drop.
"THIS IS AMAZING!"
"You said you’d hold me!" Selene shouted.
"I AM!"
"Hold harder!"
The train reached the bottom and immediately shot upward again.
"WHO DESIGNED THIS THING?!"
"The same psychopath who designed the haunted house!"

The train entered the first turn, and their bodies shifted while Mira and Selene both squeezed his hands. Dexter was trapped between them, laughing uncontrollably, until the loop appeared and his laughter stopped.
"Wait."
Lyra’s eyes brightened, and Dexter stared ahead. "No one mentioned a loop."
Mira shouted over the wind. "It’s a roller coaster!"

They entered the loop, and the world flipped. Sky became ground, and ground became sky. For a moment Dexter was upside down, holding both Mira and Selene while Lyra’s delighted mental laughter assaulted him, and then they came around. Dexter blinked, his hair a disaster, while Mira looked equally stunned and Selene’s face had gone pale. Lyra looked ecstatic.
Dexter glanced at her. "You are insane."
Lyra grinned.
Another drop approached, and Dexter saw it while Mira saw it and Selene heard the rails changing. "No."
Dexter laughed. "Here we go!"
"No, no, no..."
The train dropped again, and Selene silent scream increased. But halfway down, something changed as her scream became laughter.

Wind whipped her silver hair behind her, and her eyes were open. The world rushing around her was little more than streaks of color—blue, green, white, gold—and she couldn’t see the roller-coaster tracks clearly or the faces below or the individual trees. But she could see something, and for the first time in a very long while, the darkness wasn’t absolute.
Selene laughed. Not because she wasn’t scared—she was terrified—but that was precisely why she was laughing.
Dexter smiled. "Still scared?"
"YES!"
Another turn threw them sideways, and Selene laughed harder while Dexter laughed with her. Mira looked across him. "You two are insane!"
Dexter turned. "You’re smiling!"
"I am not!"
"You are!"
Mira realized he was right, because a huge smile had appeared across her face. She tried suppressing it, but another sharp turn arrived, and she inhaled deeply before she suddenly smiled again.
Dexter grinned. "Got you!
"Shut up!"

The train climbed another hill, not nearly as tall as the first, and Dexter’s hands remained occupied with Mira on the left and Selene on the right. He hadn’t released either of them once, and even when his body shifted violently against the restraints, his fingers remained firmly intertwined with theirs.

Mira noticed, and she looked down at their joined hands before looking at Dexter. His attention was currently on Selene, checking whether she was all right, and something strange flickered through Mira’s crimson eyes. Her fingers tightened around his.
Dexter immediately looked left. "You okay?"
Mira nodded. "I’m fine."
Dexter smiled. "Good."
He didn’t release her, and Mira didn’t ask him to.
The train plunged again, and this time all four were ready. Well... three. Lyra’s mental scream still exploded inside Dexter’s head.
’AAAAAAAAAA!’
Dexter winced. "WHY ARE YOU SCREAMING DIRECTLY INTO MY HEAD?!"
Lyra’s mental laughter followed.

The ride continued through twists, smaller drops, and another corkscrew. By the final stretch, Selene was no longer begging for it to stop—she was laughing. Mira had abandoned any attempt to pretend she wasn’t enjoying herself, and Lyra looked as though she’d discovered her new favorite invention. And Dexter? Dexter couldn’t remember the last time he’d laughed this much.
Eventually the train began slowing, and the station appeared ahead.
"That’s sad."
Dexter turned, because that had come from Mira. She froze while Dexter stared at her, Selene smiled, and Lyra slowly turned. Mira’s expression became blank, and Dexter’s grin grew monstrous.
"What was that?"
"Nothing."
"Did the great Crimson Valkyrie just ask the roller coaster not to stop?"
"I said nothing."
"I heard you."
"Your hearing is defective."
Dexter laughed as the carriage entered the station, and the brakes engaged with a loud clack. They stopped, and for a few seconds nobody moved. Then Selene breathed out.
"We’re alive."
Dexter looked toward her. "I told you."
She slowly turned her face toward him, and only then did she seem to realize she was still gripping his hand very tightly. Her cheeks reddened. "Sorry."
"For what?"
"Your hand."
Dexter looked down. "You didn’t break it."
"I might have tried."
"Then you’ll need to cultivate harder."
Selene smiled. "Thank you."
Dexter’s expression softened. "I know."

The restraint lifted, and Dexter finally released her before turning toward Mira. She was still holding his other hand, and Mira noticed while Dexter noticed her noticing. Neither moved for a second, and then Mira quickly released him.
"Help me back into my chair."
Dexter smiled. "Of course."
He wisely said nothing else.

The attendant brought Mira’s wheelchair beside the carriage, and Dexter carefully lifted her from the seat with one arm behind her back and the other beneath her legs. Mira wrapped her recovered arm around his shoulder.
"Comfortable?"
"Yes."
He lowered her carefully into the wheelchair and adjusted her legs onto the footrests. "There."
Mira looked up and seemed like she wanted to say something but stopped her self. "Thank you.
Dexter paused, because Mira didn’t thank him often, and his expression softened. "Anytime."

He turned to find that Lyra had just climbed from the carriage, her hair looking as though she’d fought a hurricane. Dexter stared, and Lyra stared back before touching her hair. Her eyes widened, and Dexter burst out laughing while Lyra glared at him.
’Don’t!’
"You look..."
’Dexter!’
"...beautiful."
Her eyes narrowed further.
"Extremely windswept, but beautiful."
She punched him, and Dexter laughed and dodged away.
Selene carefully stepped onto the platform, and Dexter immediately moved toward her, but he stopped when he realized she didn’t need his help.
Dexter watched as Selene reached them without assistance, her smile small but proud.

Mira looked down at her recovered hand while Lyra touched one ear, and for a brief moment, all three women seemed to understand the same thing. They were healing—not overnight, not magically, but piece by piece. Unmistakably.
Dexter moved behind Mira’s wheelchair. "All right." He looked toward the festival. "What next?"
Lyra immediately raised her hand. ’Again!’
Dexter stared. "The roller coaster?"
She nodded enthusiastically, and Mira immediately said, "Agreed."
Dexter’s eyebrows rose, and he turned toward Selene. Selene heard the silence, and her face changed.
"No."
Dexter laughed. "Two against one."
"You’re forgetting your own vote."
Dexter thought about it, looking toward the towering roller coaster and then toward Selene. "Three against one."
Selene looked betrayed. "Dexter!"
He laughed. "I’m joking."
She folded her arms. "You’re terrible."
"Yet you trusted me."
Selene’s expression softened. "I did."
Dexter smiled. "And?"
She hesitated before smiling too. "I’d do it again."

Lyra immediately raised both arms triumphantly while Mira laughed, and Dexter shook his head. "Not now. If we go again immediately, Lyra’s going to demand a third ride, then a fourth, and we’ll never escape."
Lyra pouted and looked away.
Dexter narrowed his eyes. "You were already planning that, weren’t you?"
No response.
"Lyra."
She began walking as she giggled.
"Don’t walk away from me."
She walked faster, and Dexter laughed before pushing Mira after her. Selene followed beside him.

The four moved away from the roller coaster together, with Mira resting comfortably in her wheelchair and Selene walking with more confidence than before. Lyra was already looking around for their next activity, and Dexter watched them.
And as Dexter pushed Mira beneath the afternoon sun, he found himself thinking the same thing he’d told Selene earlier.
He didn’t hope they would recover. He knew they would recover very soon.
And when that day finally came, he intended to make sure they had an entire world waiting for them.

He immediately knew what was coming and glanced at Selene.
Selene seemed to have sensed it and her grip immediately tightened.
The carriage immediately tipped forward, and Selene’s face changed.
Mira’s eyes widened, and Lyra grinned as gravity took them.
The train plunged with a violent whoosh, and Selene grip tightened as she closed her eyes tightly and let out a silent scream.
Mira squinted her eyes and her smile widened as she giggled happily while her hair flapped backwards through the air.
She couldn’t scream aloud, but her mental shriek detonated directly inside Dexter’s head.
The train accelerated, and wind slammed into them as Selene squeezed Dexter’s right hand with both terror while Mira’s recovered hand crushed his left.
"You said you’d hold me!" Selene shouted.
The train reached the bottom and immediately shot upward again.
"The same psychopath who designed the haunted house!"
The train entered the first turn, and their bodies shifted while Mira and Selene both squeezed his hands.
Dexter was trapped between them, laughing uncontrollably, until the loop appeared and his laughter stopped.
Lyra’s eyes brightened, and Dexter stared ahead.
They entered the loop, and the world flipped.
Sky became ground, and ground became sky.
For a moment Dexter was upside down, holding both Mira and Selene while Lyra’s delighted mental laughter assaulted him, and then they came around.
Dexter blinked, his hair a disaster, while Mira looked equally stunned and Selene’s face had gone pale.
Another drop approached, and Dexter saw it while Mira saw it and Selene heard the rails changing.
The train dropped again, and Selene silent scream increased.
But halfway down, something changed as her scream became laughter.
Wind whipped her silver hair behind her, and her eyes were open.
The world rushing around her was little more than streaks of color—blue, green, white, gold—and she couldn’t see the roller-coaster tracks clearly or the faces below or the individual trees.
But she could see something, and for the first time in a very long while, the darkness wasn’t absolute.
Not because she wasn’t scared—she was terrified—but that was precisely why she was laughing.
Another turn threw them sideways, and Selene laughed harder while Dexter laughed with her.
Mira realized he was right, because a huge smile had appeared across her face.
She tried suppressing it, but another sharp turn arrived, and she inhaled deeply before she suddenly smiled again.
The train climbed another hill, not nearly as tall as the first, and Dexter’s hands remained occupied with Mira on the left and Selene on the right.
He hadn’t released either of them once, and even when his body shifted violently against the restraints, his fingers remained firmly intertwined with theirs.
Mira noticed, and she looked down at their joined hands before looking at Dexter.
His attention was currently on Selene, checking whether she was all right, and something strange flickered through Mira’s crimson eyes.
He didn’t release her, and Mira didn’t ask him to.
The train plunged again, and this time all four were ready.
Lyra’s mental scream still exploded inside Dexter’s head.
"WHY ARE YOU SCREAMING DIRECTLY INTO MY HEAD?!"
The ride continued through twists, smaller drops, and another corkscrew.
By the final stretch, Selene was no longer begging for it to stop—she was laughing.
Mira had abandoned any attempt to pretend she wasn’t enjoying herself, and Lyra looked as though she’d discovered her new favorite invention.
Dexter couldn’t remember the last time he’d laughed this much.
Eventually the train began slowing, and the station appeared ahead.
Dexter turned, because that had come from Mira.
She froze while Dexter stared at her, Selene smiled, and Lyra slowly turned.
Mira’s expression became blank, and Dexter’s grin grew monstrous.
"Did the great Crimson Valkyrie just ask the roller coaster not to stop?"
Dexter laughed as the carriage entered the station, and the brakes engaged with a loud clack.
They stopped, and for a few seconds nobody moved.
She slowly turned her face toward him, and only then did she seem to realize she was still gripping his hand very tightly.
The restraint lifted, and Dexter finally released her before turning toward Mira.
She was still holding his other hand, and Mira noticed while Dexter noticed her noticing.
Neither moved for a second, and then Mira quickly released him.
The attendant brought Mira’s wheelchair beside the carriage, and Dexter carefully lifted her from the seat with one arm behind her back and the other beneath her legs.
Mira wrapped her recovered arm around his shoulder.
He lowered her carefully into the wheelchair and adjusted her legs onto the footrests.
Mira looked up and seemed like she wanted to say something but stopped her self.
Dexter paused, because Mira didn’t thank him often, and his expression softened.
He turned to find that Lyra had just climbed from the carriage, her hair looking as though she’d fought a hurricane.
Dexter stared, and Lyra stared back before touching her hair.
Her eyes widened, and Dexter burst out laughing while Lyra glared at him.
She punched him, and Dexter laughed and dodged away.
Selene carefully stepped onto the platform, and Dexter immediately moved toward her, but he stopped when he realized she didn’t need his help.
Dexter watched as Selene reached them without assistance, her smile small but proud.
Mira looked down at her recovered hand while Lyra touched one ear, and for a brief moment, all three women seemed to understand the same thing.
They were healing—not overnight, not magically, but piece by piece.
"All right." He looked toward the festival.
She nodded enthusiastically, and Mira immediately said, "Agreed."
Dexter’s eyebrows rose, and he turned toward Selene.
Selene heard the silence, and her face changed.
Dexter thought about it, looking toward the towering roller coaster and then toward Selene.
Lyra immediately raised both arms triumphantly while Mira laughed, and Dexter shook his head.
If we go again immediately, Lyra’s going to demand a third ride, then a fourth, and we’ll never escape."
"You were already planning that, weren’t you?"
She began walking as she giggled.
She walked faster, and Dexter laughed before pushing Mira after her.
The four moved away from the roller coaster together, with Mira resting comfortably in her wheelchair and Selene walking with more confidence than before.
Lyra was already looking around for their next activity, and Dexter watched them.
And as Dexter pushed Mira beneath the afternoon sun, he found himself thinking the same thing he’d told Selene earlier.
He didn’t hope they would recover.
He knew they would recover very soon.
And when that day finally came, he intended to make sure they had an entire world waiting for them.

chapters.title: Chapter 266 | The Food Exchange
paragraphs: People were beginning to gather across the main field, and the atmosphere around the picnic area had changed. Earlier, families had mostly remained within their individual groups, eating snacks, talking, and enjoying the attractions.
Now people were moving around, carrying plates between mats and opening large containers while children ran around holding bowls and adults approached neighboring families with trays of food.
The air itself seemed different, with dozens of aromas mixing together—grilled meat, fresh bread, spices, soups, pastries, roasted vegetables, and sweet sauces.
Dexter slowed. "Looks like it’s starting."
Mira looked around. "The meal exchange?"
"Seems like it."

Dexter scanned the field, and his enhanced eyesight quickly found their picnic spot. His eyebrows rose, because they had neighbors now. Several people were seated close to their mats, and Tessa was among them. Beside her sat her father, who was currently removing several baked dishes from a large picnic basket.

There were also two elderly people Dexter didn’t recognize, and sitting comfortably among them, looking as though she personally owned the entire garden, was an old woman Dexter had seen around the neighborhood.
Old Lady Lucy was already eating, and not delicately either. She held a plate in one hand while enthusiastically discussing something with Tessa’s father.
Dexter smiled. "Looks like Tessa wasn’t joking."
Mira followed his gaze. "About?"
"Everyone taking this food exchange seriously."
A family walked past carrying a massive roasted beast leg. Dexter looked toward his wives. "How about we head back?"
Lyra’s expression fell slightly, and Dexter immediately knew why. "We’ll come back." Her eyes brightened again. "Food exchange first. Then we’ll continue exploring."
Mira nodded. "That’s fine."
Selene smiled and nodded.
Dexter looked at Lyra, who was already walking toward the picnic field. "Of course." He started pushing Mira after her. "At least pretend you’re interested in the community."
Lyra didn’t look back, but her voice entered his mind. ’I am interested.’
"In the community?"
’In their food.’
Dexter laughed. "Close enough."
"Finally!"
Tessa’s voice reached them before they arrived, and one of the old men there turned. "So this is the troublesome young man everyone’s been talking about."
Dexter scratched his head in embarrassment.
"I’ve barely done anything."
Old Lucy smiled as she nodded confidently. "Definitely troublesome.
Tessa covered her mouth, hiding a laugh.
Dexter sighed and guided Mira toward their mats. Tessa’s father stood and greeted him warmly. "There you are, Dexter."
"Sorry. We got distracted."
"So I heard."
The man’s eyes went toward the massive teddy bears they’d left nearby, then toward Lyra, then Mira, then Selene. He chuckled. "You clearly had fun."
Dexter cleared his throat. "Important festival activities."
"Naturally."

Dexter helped Mira transfer from her wheelchair onto the mat again, carefully positioning her legs and making sure she was comfortable. Selene sat beside her, Lyra sat down next, and Dexter took his place across from them.
Old Lady Lucy watched the entire process, and her sharp old eyes briefly rested on Mira’s right arm. Something flickered through them but she didn’t comment. Instead, she looked toward Dexter.
"So?"
"So?"
"Where’s your food?"
Dexter blinked, and Tessa laughed. "I told you."
Dexter raised his hands. "Fine, fine."

He pulled the cooler closer, and the moment he opened it, a rich aroma escaped. Conversation around them noticeably weakened, and Dexter paused as several heads turned. Mira noticed. Selene noticed. Lyra definitely noticed, her eyes immediately dropping toward the cooler.
Dexter lips curled as he looked at her.
Lyra licked her lips in excitement.
Dexter removed the first containers—the Grade one and two dishes he’d deliberately prepared for the festival.
He had kept the Grade Five meals separately reserved for Mira, Lyra, and Selene. Even so, the dishes were far beyond ordinary cooking.

Dexter opened another container. Then another. Rice. Tender meat cooked with herbs. Vegetables. A rich stew. Several smaller side dishes. Nothing looked absurdly luxurious—that was intentional. Dexter had deliberately avoided making anything too conspicuous.
Still...
Tessa inhaled. "That smells incredible."
Her father leaned forward. "That’s what you’ve been selling through the bakery?"
"Similar," Dexter replied.
Tessa stared at him. "Similar? You’ve been holding out on us."
Dexter laughed. "It’s only food."
Old Lady Lucy’s gaze immediately moved toward him as she smiled. "Give this old woman some."
Dexter chuckled. "Of course."
That was the entire point of the festival. People exchanged dishes, and nobody was supposed to hoard everything for themselves.
Dexter served portions, and Tessa’s father offered them some of his family’s food in exchange.
Other nearby families gradually approached too.
A woman brought grilled meat skewers, another family offered a fragrant vegetable soup, and someone else had prepared several trays of pastries.
Children moved between picnic spots exchanging sweets, and within minutes, Dexter’s mat looked less like a private picnic and more like a miniature banquet.
"Try this."
Tessa handed Dexter a pastry, and he bit into it. His eyebrows rose. "Good."
Tessa’s father looked offended. "Good?"
Dexter swallowed. "Very good."
"Better."
Mira took a small bite from another pastry. "It’s excellent."
Tessa’s father immediately smiled. "See? She understands."
Dexter rolled his eyes.

Then someone finally tasted Dexter’s cooking. It was one of the elderly men, who took a spoonful of the stew, chewed, and then stopped. Dexter noticed, and the man’s expression changed as he slowly looked down at his bowl and took another spoonful.
Tessa watched. "Well?"
The old man didn’t answer. He took a third.
Old Lady Lucy immediately slapped his arm. "Stop eating and speak."
The man frowned. "I’m still evaluating it."
Lucy glared at him. "You’ve evaluated three spoonfuls."
The old man huffed. "Quality requires thorough investigation."
"Greedy old fool."
"You’re calling me greedy?"
While they argued, Tessa tried Dexter’s food, and her reaction was almost immediate. Her eyes widened, and she stared at Dexter. "This is Grade One?"
Dexter pursed his lips but ultimately nodded. "Yes."
"You’re sure?"
"Kinda."

The food was in between grade one and grade two and some even almost entered grade 3 but he had mixed them so they basically almost looked like grade one meal. Moreover, it was tiring to hold back which was why these happened.

chapters.title: Chapter 267 | When Will You Give Birth To Little Babies?
paragraphs: Tessa’s father’s expression changed when he tasted the food.
"Boy, where did you learn to cook?"
Dexter smiled. "Just randomly."
Old Lady Lucy finally took her first spoonful, and Dexter watched her. The old woman’s expression didn’t change as she chewed, swallowed, and then took another and another.

Lucy continued eating, but her seemingly casual eyes had become considerably sharper. She could feel the food wasn’t ordinary. Even at this low grade, there was a strange purity within it. The energy was balanced almost perfectly, gentle and nourishing and clean. It didn’t violently force mana into the body. Instead, it seemed to guide the body toward repairing itself.
Lucy said nothing.
Around them, however, reactions were becoming increasingly obvious. Another neighbor tried Dexter’s food. Then another.
"What is this?"
"This tastes incredible."
"Did you cook this yourself?"
"Wait, my shoulder..."
A middle-aged man rotated his arm, and his eyes widened. "It doesn’t hurt as much."
His wife laughed. "You’re imagining things."
"I’m serious."
Another elderly woman took a bite, frowned, then took another before immediately looking toward Dexter. "Can I have more?"
Dexter laughed. "The idea is exchanging food, Grandma."
"I gave you dumplings."
"That doesn’t mean you get half the pot."
The elderly woman narrowed her eyes. "Respect your elders."
Dexter stared, and Old Lady Lucy burst out laughing. "He’s got you there, Martha."
The elderly woman glared at Lucy. "You’ve already eaten twice as much as me."
Within several minutes, the atmosphere around Dexter’s picnic area changed completely. People who had initially approached out of curiosity returned with friends.
"Try the stew."
"No, the rice is better."
"Have you tasted the meat?"
"What seasoning is this?"
"Where did he buy these ingredients?"
"Is he a Food-Smith?"
Dexter’s eyebrows slowly rose. This was getting out of hand, and Tessa noticed too. She leaned toward him. "I told you people would like your food."
"You didn’t say they’d start recruiting others."
A man walked past carrying a bowl, then stopped. "Is this where the special stew is?"
Dexter stared at Tessa, who raised both hands. "That wasn’t me."
Dexter sighed.
Lyra, meanwhile, was watching the entire situation with growing concern. Her eyes followed every bowl leaving the containers and h er expression became progressively more tragic.
Dexter noticed and leaned toward her. "Relax." Lyra looked at him. "I kept yours separately."
Her eyes instantly brightened. "Really?"
Dexter smiled as he nodded his head. "You three are my priority. Of course I made yours separately and even more tasty.
Lyra smil widened and she was immediately excited.

The meal exchange continued, and soon Dexter and his wives had received enough food from other families to fill half their mats. Mira tried a spicy roasted meat dish. Selene preferred a soft honey pastry. Lyra tried almost everything, and Dexter eventually stopped counting.

For a while, they simply ate and talked. It was strangely peaceful. Neighbors introduced themselves. Children ran past. People argued about recipes. Tessa’s father became involved in an increasingly serious discussion with one elderly man about bread fermentation.
Dexter leaned backward on his hands. This wasn’t bad at all.
Then Old Lady Lucy’s gaze moved toward his wives, and Dexter should have recognized the danger. He didn’t.
Lucy looked first at Mira, then Lyra, then Selene, and finally toward Dexter. A peculiar smile appeared. "So."
Mira immediately became suspicious. "What?"
Old Lady Lucy pointed toward the four of them. "You’ve been married for a quite a while now."
Dexter blinked. "Yes?"
Lucy continued. "Your wives should have started showing already. "
Silence. Complete silence.
Dexter blinked his eyes as he tasted a barbequed chicken and replied, a but puzzled. "Showing what?"
Old Lucy smiled as she glanced at Dexter. "Signs of pregnancy of course."
Everything went pin drop silent!
Mira froze, Selene stopped halfway through lifting her cup and Lyra’s cheeks puffed slightly because her mouth was full.
Dexter’s widened, clearly stunned.
Lucy waved her hand. "Stop acting shy."
Mira’s face began turning red. Selene slowly lowered her cup but even her pale face can do nothing to hide the embarrasment in her face.
Lyra swallowed so quickly she nearly choked.
Dexter coughed. "Grandma Lucy..."
"What?"
"That’s..."
"What?"

Dexter looked toward his wives and he saw Mira was extremely red, Selene’s cheeks had turned pink, and she had suddenly become fascinated by the grass while Lyra’s entire face was rapidly changing color.
Old Lady Lucy continued mercilessly. "This neighborhood needs more children.
One elderly man nodded. "She’s right."
Tessa’s father coughed into his fist, desperately suppressing laughter, and Lucy pointed toward Dexter. "Young man has three beautiful wives and still no little feet running around his house."
Dexter’s mouth opened, but nothing came out.
Lucy shook her head. "Young people these days."
Mira finally found her voice. "We..." She stopped as everyone looked at her, and she immediately regretted speaking.
Lucy smiled. "You what?"
Mira’s face became even redder. "We’re still..." She glanced toward Dexter, who was watching her, and that made everything worse. Mira looked away. "We haven’t discussed anything like that."
Lucy waved dismissively. "Then discuss it vigorously tonight."
Tessa choked and her father burst out laughing. One elderly woman slapped her knee. Selene’s face became crimson, and Lyra covered her face with both hands.
Dexter stared at Old Lady Lucy. This old woman was dangerous.
Lucy wasn’t finished as she muttered. "Three wives!"
Dexter rubbed his forehead. "Yes, Grandma Lucy. I’m aware."
"Each of them with at least twins. Making six children. Can’t wait."
The elderly man beside her laughed. "Lucy, leave the boy alone."
"The boy?" Lucy scoffed. "He has three wives. He’s not a boy anymore."
That sent everyone laughing again.
Dexter looked toward his wives. Mira was trying to maintain her dignity.
Selene was practically hiding behind her cup. Lyra refused to uncover her face. A chuckle escaped Dexter.
Mira’s head immediately snapped toward him, her crimson eyes locking onto his.
Dexter stopped, and the smile vanished from his face with supernatural speed. Mira continued staring, so Dexter picked up his cup and took a slow drink, his expression becoming incredibly serious.
Mira narrowed her eyes. "You were laughing."
Dexter lowered the cup. "Me?"
"Yes."
"You must be mistaken."
"Dexter."
He looked toward Tessa’s father. "This food is excellent."
Tessa’s father immediately understood what was happening and laughed harder. Mira glared, but Dexter pretended not to notice.
Old Lady Lucy slapped her thigh. "Oh, I like this family."
Selene finally laughed softly, and Lyra uncovered her face. Her cheeks were still bright red, but her mental voice reached Dexter. ’Naughty!’

chapters.title: Chapter 268 | Food! Food! Food!
paragraphs: "Excuse me."

Everyone looked up to find a middle-aged man standing at the edge of their picnic area. He held an empty bowl, and Dexter recognized him as someone who had tried the stew earlier. The man smiled awkwardly.
"Do you have any more?"
Dexter stared at the empty bowl, then at the man. "You already had some."
The man looked embarrassed. "My wife wants to try it."
A woman’s voice immediately shouted from behind him. "Don’t blame me! You ate the first bowl yourself!"
Everyone laughed, and the man turned red. Dexter shook his head. "Fine."

He reached toward the container, then stopped. It was almost empty. His eyebrows rose. That had been fast. He glanced around. Several people nearby were eating his dishes. Others were discussing them. A few more seemed to be looking in his direction.
Dexter frowned slightly. Perhaps he’d underestimated how unusual his cooking was.
Old Lady Lucy noticed his expression. She calmly took another bite, for a fraction of a second, the playful old woman disappeared. Her eyes became deep.
She could feel the changes inside her body more clearly than anyone else here. An old injury in one of her meridians, something she’d carried for years, felt... warm and soothing.
Lucy looked toward Dexter again. The young man was currently arguing with Mira because he’d apparently taken a piece of roasted meat from her plate.
"You have your own!" Mira snapped.
"Yours looked better."
Dexter smirked.
"It’s the same meat!"
She glared at him.
"Yours had more sauce."
"Give it back."
"I already ate it. Unless you want to eat what I’ve eaten."
"Give it to me."
"That would be indirect kiss and it would count as me winning our bet."
Mira stared at him, and Dexter smiled innocently.
Lucy watched them, and her smile slowly returned. Interesting. Very interesting.

Dexter’s original plan had been straightforward: bring some food, exchange a few dishes, eat with his wives, and then return to the rides before the afternoon disappeared. Instead, people kept coming.
At one point, Dexter caught an old man attempting to approach from a different direction with a different hat. Dexter stared at him, and the old man stared back. Neither spoke.
Eventually, the old man sighed. "You remembered me."
"You changed your hat, Grandpa. Not your face."
"I thought your generation had poor attention spans."
"Not when someone’s stealing my stew."
The people around them burst into laughter, and even Old Lady Lucy nearly spilled her drink.
Things had finally begun settling down when two familiar voices suddenly rang through the crowd.
"Dexter!"
"Dexter!"
Dexter closed his eyes, because he knew those voices. Mira looked toward the sound, Selene tilted her head, and Tessa glanced up from the pastry she was eating. Old Lady Lucy immediately grinned.
"Oh?"

Dexter opened his eyes to find two tiny figures charging across the grass. Peter and Paul, each twin carrying an empty plate in both hands decorated with cartoon mana beasts. Several meters behind them stood their parents, their father scratching the back of his head while their mother covered part of her face.
Both wore the resigned expressions on their faces.
Peter reached Dexter first, with Paul arriving half a second later. Both thrust their plates forward.
"Food!"
Dexter stared as Peter raised his plate higher. "Papa said your food is really good!"
Paul bounced impatiently. "We brought plates!"
"I can see that."
Dexter looked at the containers. There wasn’t much of the Grade One food remaining, so he picked up the serving spoon. "All right. Let me see what’s..."
"Wait."
Dexter looked toward Mira, who was watching the twins. Then she glanced toward the second cooler—the one Dexter hadn’t opened throughout the meal exchange.
"Give them from ours."
Dexter paused as he raised an eyebrow. "Our portion?"
Mira nodded. "Yeah."
Dexter studied her for a moment. "You sure?"
"Why wouldn’t I be?"
He turned toward Selene. "What about you?"
Selene smiled. "Give them some."

Dexter nodded, then looked toward Lyra. She froze, her gaze going toward the cooler, then toward the twins, then back toward the cooler. Dexter watched the internal war unfold across her face and nearly laughed.
"Lyra?"
She looked at him.
’It’s our food.’
Lyra’s expression became painful, as she glanced at Peter and Paul, who smiled at her and Paul waved. Lyra’s resistance crumbled, and her shoulders dropped as she reluctantly nodded.
’Fine.’
Dexter grinned. "Such generosity."
Lyra glared at him. ’Just small portions.’
Dexter laughed. "All right.

He reached for the second cooler. Until now, nobody except the four of them had paid much attention to it. Why would they? The Grade One dishes had already been extraordinary enough to dominate the exchange.
Dexter opened it and a rich fragrance escaped. Everywhere turned silent.
Dexter noticed, he simply behaved as though he hadn’t.
The difference between these dishes and what he’d been serving everyone else was enormous.
These were Grade five nourishing meals, food Dexter had specifically prepared for his wives.
The fragrance alone seemed unusually pure, and warm steam curled from the containers, carrying mana so gentle and refined that even people without exceptional perception could feel something unusual.
Tessa swallowed. "Dexter..."
"Hm?"
"What is that?"
"Food of course."
Tessa stared at him, and Old Lady Lucy’s eyebrow twitched. Tessa’s father slowly looked toward Dexter.
"I know it’s food."
"Good. I was worried."

Tessa glared, and Dexter smiled innocently. He could feel the elderly people’s attention on his hands. They knew. Perhaps not precisely what grade the food was, but they knew this wasn’t ordinary food.
Lucy glanced at Dexter, who was casually filling two children’s plates as though he were serving ordinary rice. Her eyes narrowed.
Dexter finished Peter’s plate, then Paul’s. "Here."
Peter stared down, his eyes widening, while Paul inhaled deeply. "Smells good!"
"Very good!" Peter agreed.
Dexter smiled. "Eat slowly."
Both immediately began bouncing. "Food! Food! Food!"
Selene laughed. "Don’t spill it."
Dexter was about to tell them to walk carefully when Lyra stood and brushed down her dark dress. ’I’ll take them.’
Dexter looked up. "You don’t have to."
Lyra had already taken both plates, and Peter immediately grabbed the hem of one side of her dress while Paul grabbed the other. Lyra blinked as the twins started walking.
"Food!"
"Food!"
Lyra followed.
"Food!"
Both boys stopped and looked up at her. Lyra couldn’t make the sound aloud, but she’d mouthed it, and her eyes were smiling.
The twins burst into giggles, and then all three continued to chant as they walked.
