chapters.title: Chapter 269 | The Intruders
paragraphs: Lyra was almost skipping with the kids too.
Her long black hair swayed behind her as she walked between the twins, carefully holding their plates beyond the reach of their chaotic little hands.
"Food!"
"Food!"
Lyra silently mouthed the word again, and the boys laughed harder.
Dexter watched them, and something softened inside him.
Lyra was different around the children, she looked young, happy, playful and incredibly beautiful.
"Cute."
The thought surfaced naturally, and then another followed before Dexter could stop it. For just a moment, Peter and Paul disappeared from his imagination. In their place were two other children.
His children, their children.

One with Lyra’s dark hair. Maybe another with her violet eyes. He imagined Lyra walking through their garden with them holding her dress exactly like this. He imagined her chasing them, feeding them, perhaps pretending to be angry when they stole food from the kitchen. He could almost picture them running toward him afterward.
’Dad.’
The thought struck harder than expected, and Dexter smiled unconsciously.
"What are you thinking about?"
Selene’s voice sounded from within the daydream. Dexter turned to find her facing him. Her pale eyes couldn’t yet focus perfectly on his face, with a small smile on ge face.
Dexter answered unconsciously. "I was thinking how nice it’d be if you girls were playing with our kids someday."

Mira slowly turned, and Selene’s smile froze. Tessa stopped chewing, her father immediately became fascinated by his plate, and one of the elderly men raised his eyebrows. Old Lady Lucy’s face lit up with such terrifying delight that Dexter immediately realized his mistake.
Mira’s crimson eyes narrowed. "Pervert."
Dexter looked at her. "How does wanting children with my wives make me a pervert?"
Mira’s cheeks were already becoming red. "Because..." She stopped.
Dexter waited as Mira apparently couldn’t find an answer that didn’t make things worse. His lips curled. "You’re my wife, after all."
Mira’s blush deepened, and she scoffed and turned away. "Hmph!"
Dexter chuckled, and Mira immediately glared back. He stopped laughing.
Old Lady Lucy slapped her knee. "I knew it!"
Dexter’s expression changed. "Please don’t start again."
Lucy pointed at him. "See? The boy has plans!"
"I made one comment."
"Three wives, three opportunities."
"Grandma Lucy!"
The elderly people laughed, Tessa covered her mouth, and Mira looked ready to throw something at Dexter.
Selene, however, remained quiet. Dexter didn’t notice the way she was looking at him. Her smile had changed. It was deeper now and a ofter.

There was a warmth in her expression that hadn’t been there moments earlier. She couldn’t clearly see Dexter’s face, but she could see his vague shape, his colors, his presence. And she’d heard every word.
’Our kids.’
Her fingers tightened gently against her dress, and she looked away before anyone noticed. At least, before Dexter noticed.
Old Lady Lucy noticed everything. Her eyes briefly moved toward Selene, and the old woman’s smile widened but she didn’t say anything and laughed again.
Meanwhile, Lyra had nearly reached Peter and Paul’s parents. The twins were still attached to her dress, and their father smiled apologetically. "Sorry about them."
Lyra shook her head. She didn’t mind.
The mother smiled warmly. "They seem to like you."
Peter immediately declared, "She’s pretty!"
Paul nodded. "Very pretty!"
Lyra blushed slight and then smiled.
Their mother laughed. "At least they have good manners sometimes."
Lyra handed over the plates, and the father accepted one. The instant the aroma reached him, his expression changed. "What..."
His wife noticed too, and she looked down at the food. "This is Dexter’s?"
Lyra nodded.
Peter immediately reached for his plate. "Mine!"
His father lifted it away. "Wait."
Peter looked betrayed. "It’s mine!"
"I’m checking if it’s too hot."
Paul hugged his mother’s leg. "Don’t eat mine!"
The mother laughed. "We’re not stealing your food."
The father stared at the dish another second, then looked across the field toward Dexter. His expression became thoughtful, and Lyra noticed but didn’t react. She gave the twins a final wave.
Peter waved back. "Bye!"
Paul followed. "Bye, Dexter’s wife!"
Lyra nearly stumbled, and their parents froze.
Peter frowned at his brother. "She has a name."
Paul looked confused. "What is it?"
Peter opened his mouth, then stopped. He didn’t know either.
Lyra covered her mouth, shoulders shaking with silent laughter. She waved once more and turned away.
That was when she noticed them.
Two men stood several meters ahead. Middle-aged and in ordinary clothes. Nothing outwardly remarkable. Yet they weren’t looking at the festival. They were looking directly at her.
Lyra slowed, and the laughter disappeared from her face.
The men approached and one stepped into her path while the other stopped slightly behind him.
Then, without warning, both placed closed fists against their chests and bowed their heads.
"Greetings, Shadow Monarch."
Lyra stopped as her violet eyes narrowed, and she looked behind herself. Nobody. They were definitely speaking to her.
Her voice entered their minds. ’Excuse me?’
The first man’s head rose, his expression changing from confusion to recognition as he studied Lyra’s face. The second man did the same, and something passed silently between them.
The first man frowned. "Seems this personality has temporarily taken over."
Lyra frowned in confusion. ’What are you talking about?’

They ignored the question, and the second man nodded slowly. "Hmm." He looked around. People were everywhere, families, children, Heroes, ordinary residents. Too many witnesses. "We can’t remain here."
The first man nodded. "We’ll take her by force."
Lyra’s eyes sharpened, and the second man’s voice lowered. "Do it quickly before we’re noticed."
Lyra took one step backward, and shadow mana instinctively stirred within her, ready to activate her necklace. ’Who are you?’
Neither answered and suddenly, the first man vanished with speed that surpass that of a Superhuman realm.
Lyra’s pupils contracted. ’Fast!’
In a split second, he appeared directly beside her, and a palm shot toward her neck to knock her unconscious. Lyra tried to move, but she was too slow.
The palm approached, 10 centimeters, 5, 2.
Then... everything stopped.
Lyra’s violet eyes widened as a familiar coldness crawled through her mind. Something that had been sleeping and the playful warmth she’d carried moments ago disappeared.
Her expression became empty and incredibly cold.

The attacker’s palm was centimeters from her neck when a voice entered both men’s minds. It was no longer Lyra’s gentle mental voice. This one carried crushing authority, cold enough to make both men stiffen.
’You dare.’
The man’s palm stopped, his eyes widening. The second man’s face changed instantly.
Both recognized that voice as their bodies shook instantly.
The attacking man immediately withdrew his hand and dropped to one knee. His companion followed.
"Monarch."
The woman before them stared down. Her posture had changed. There was no obvious physical change but she seemed to have grown even taller, untouchable like a goddess.
The warmth was gone from her eyes and even her breathing seemed different.
Aurelyx...
The first man lowered his head. "Forgive us. We didn’t realize you had returned. We meant no disrespect."
Aurelyx looked toward the distant picnic area.
Her eyes found Dexter immediately—sitting beside Mira and Selene, laughing, unaware. Something unreadable flickered within her gaze, then vanished. She looked back at the kneeling men.
’Let’s go.’
The two men raised their heads. Neither questioned her.
"Yes."

chapters.title: Chapter 270 | Let Lyra Out!
paragraphs: Dexter smiled at something one of the older people said. And he unconsciously looked to around at his wives and then, his smile slowly disappeared.
It had been almost two minutes since Lyra walked away with Peter and Paul, yet she wasn’t back.
He looked at the direction she went and saw that the twins were safely back with their parents, eating.
But Lyra was nowhere in sight.

Dexter stood beside the picnic mats and slowly swept his gaze across the festival. Hundreds of people filled the field. Children chased one another between colorful mats. Families exchanged dishes and vendors shouted from distant stalls. Too many people, too many sounds and too much noise.
Mira noticed the change in him immediately. "Dexter?"
He didn’t answer immediately as his eyes narrowed as he looked around, but still, nothing. His jaw tightened.
Selene slowly stood. "Dexter."
"I’m checking."
He inhaled, then closed his eyes.
’Enhanced Hearing.’

Dexter stopped listening to the festival as one enormous collection of noise. Instead, he separated it. The world changed. The laughter closest to him disappeared first, then the conversations, the clinking plates, children shouting, footsteps, roller-coaster tracks, music, wind, water. He pushed all of it aside.
Hundreds of heartbeats emerged. ’Thump. Thump. Thump. Thump.’ Too many.

Dexter’s brow furrowed as he filtered them. Old. Young. Fast. Slow. People moving. People sitting. People laughing. Children whose hearts raced from excitement. Heroes whose stronger bodies produced slower, heavier rhythms. One by one, Dexter eliminated them.
He knew Lyra’s heartbeat. He had spent enough nights in the same house with her, listening without realizing he was memorizing it. He knew Mira’s. He knew Selene’s. And he knew Lyra’s.
Dexter expanded his hearing. Two hundred meters. Nothing. Three hundred. Nothing. Four hundred. Nothing. His expression darkened. Five hundred. Six hundred. Nothing.
His breathing changed, and Mira saw his hands slowly close into fists. "Dexter?"
Seven hundred meters. Nothing. Eight hundred. Still nothing. The muscles in Dexter’s jaw tightened, and something hot stirred beneath his skin. Mira felt it.
So did Tessa. Even Old Lady Lucy’s previously amused eyes shifted toward Dexter. The temperature around him had begun increasing, and Selene’s face changed slightly.
She couldn’t see his expression clearly, but she could hear his heart. It was becoming faster.
"Dexter..."
He didn’t answer. Nine hundred meters. Nothing. His face turned ugly, and a terrible possibility entered his mind. If Lyra’s heartbeat had disappeared because someone had...
No. The thought didn’t finish. Flames stirred beneath Dexter’s skin, and the grass beneath his boots began drying.
"Dexter." Mira’s voice was firmer now.
He still didn’t answer. His hearing stretched farther. Almost a mile.
Then... ’Thump.’
Dexter froze.
’Thump. Thump. Thump.’
His eyes snapped open. There. Familiar. Distant. Moving rapidly away from the festival. And beside it... two other heartbeats.
Dexter’s pupils narrowed. He recognized something else too. Lyra’s heartbeat was familiar, but its rhythm wasn’t. It was calm and cold. His expression became murderous.
"Aurelyx."
The name escaped as a growl, and Mira’s face changed. "What?"
Dexter turned towards her and Selene as he forced a smile.
"Stay here. I want to go check something out."
The two girls frowned but Dexter’s gaze was absolute so they reluctantly nodded their head.
Dexter merged into the crowd and when he wasn’t visible to them, flames exploded beneath his feet. "Flame Burst Step!"
’BOOM!’
The grass erupted, and Dexter vanished.
’BOOM!’

Flames exploded behind Dexter as his body shot through the festival grounds. People barely saw him. Some felt only a sudden gust of hot wind. Dexter avoided the densest parts of the crowd, cutting between tents and stalls before vaulting over a low wall. His foot struck the pavement outside.
He accelerated as buildings blurred and his clothes snapped violently in the wind.
There was only one sound in Dexter’s world now. ’Thump. Thump. Thump.’ Lyra. Almost a mile away and it was moving.
His face hardened. "Aurelyx."
He knew that heartbeat belonged to Lyra, but he knew who was controlling her body.

The second personality. The woman Lyra had once been. Or perhaps the woman still buried somewhere inside her. Dexter didn’t care what complicated explanation existed behind it. Aurelyx was taking her lyra away from him without permission!
He shot around a corner, and several pedestrians jumped. "What the hell was that?!
Dexter was already gone.

Eight hundred meters. Seven hundred. Six hundred. The city thinned around him, and the paved streets gave way to a quieter district near the outskirts of the festival grounds. Beyond it stood a forested region surrounding several hills and mountains.
Dexter frowned. They were heading there. Why?
Five hundred meters. His bloodline stirred. Four hundred.
Dexter jumped. Flames exploded beneath his boots and launched him over a wall, and he landed in the forest.
’CRACK!’
The ground fractured, and birds erupted from the trees. Dexter immediately accelerated again. Branches whipped past him. Three hundred meters. Two hundred.
Then... he saw them.
Three figures moving through the forest. Two middle-aged men. And between them... Lyra.
Dexter’s expression became glacial. "Where do you think you are going?"
His voice exploded through the forest, and all three stopped. Birds scattered from distant branches. One of the middle-aged men turned sharply while the other frowned. Lyra slowly looked back.
No. Not Lyra. Aurelyx.
Her violet eyes met Dexter’s, and there was none of Lyra’s usual warmth in them. No embarrassment. No softness. No playful hunger whenever food was involved. Only cold amusement.
Dexter stepped forward, and the first man stared at him. "Who are you?"
Dexter ignored him completely, his gaze remaining locked on Aurelyx.
The second man’s face darkened. "Boy, he asked you a question."
Nothing. Dexter looked only at the woman standing between them.
Aurelyx’s lips curved faintly, and her voice entered his mind. ’You caught up to us quite quickly.’
Dexter’s eyes narrowed. "You’re speaking as though you’re the true owner of that body."
The smile disappeared from Aurelyx’s face, and Dexter took another step. "Let Lyra out." The forest seemed to become quieter. "And I’ll choose to ignore this slight."
Aurelyx stared, then laughed. No sound came from her lips. The laughter existed only inside Dexter’s mind. Cold. Mocking.
’Let Lyra out?’ Her eyes sharpened. ’Don’t be naive.’

The woman Lyra had once been.
Or perhaps the woman still buried somewhere inside her.
Dexter didn’t care what complicated explanation existed behind it.
Aurelyx was taking her lyra away from him without permission!
He shot around a corner, and several pedestrians jumped.
The city thinned around him, and the paved streets gave way to a quieter district near the outskirts of the festival grounds.
Beyond it stood a forested region surrounding several hills and mountains.
Flames exploded beneath his boots and launched him over a wall, and he landed in the forest.
The ground fractured, and birds erupted from the trees.
Three figures moving through the forest.
"Where do you think you are going?"
His voice exploded through the forest, and all three stopped.
One of the middle-aged men turned sharply while the other frowned.
Her violet eyes met Dexter’s, and there was none of Lyra’s usual warmth in them.
No playful hunger whenever food was involved.
Dexter stepped forward, and the first man stared at him.
Dexter ignored him completely, his gaze remaining locked on Aurelyx.
Dexter looked only at the woman standing between them.
Aurelyx’s lips curved faintly, and her voice entered his mind. ’You caught up to us quite quickly.’
"You’re speaking as though you’re the true owner of that body."
The smile disappeared from Aurelyx’s face, and Dexter took another step.
"Let Lyra out." The forest seemed to become quieter.
"And I’ll choose to ignore this slight."
No sound came from her lips.
The laughter existed only inside Dexter’s mind.
’Let Lyra out?’ Her eyes sharpened. ’Don’t be naive.’

chapters.title: Chapter 271 | Every Pain Makes Me Stronger
paragraphs: ’Don’t be naive, Dexter.’
Dexter’s fist tightened as he glared at her.
She continued.
’I’ve played house with you for long enough, don’t you think?’
Something inside Dexter went still. Not calm. Still. There was a difference.
Aurelyx turned away. ’I’m getting bored.’She took a step. ’If there’s nothing else, scram.’

Dexter’s eyes became cold, and the two middle-aged men immediately moved. One stood between Dexter and Aurelyx while the other remained slightly behind. The first man studied Dexter’s face, and recognition appeared. Then contempt.
"So you’re him." Dexter finally looked at him. "The useless bastard from the Ashford family."
Dexter’s expression barely changed. One thought crossed his mind. ’Ireally should change that name.’
Apparently every enemy he met had received the same insult handbook.

The second man chuckled. "Imagine chasing the Monarch all the way here." His gaze moved over Dexter. "Kid, go back to your picnic." The first man smiled. "Take care of your other wives. You still have two more, after all."
Dexter stared at them, and then his mana began rising. Slowly. The leaves around his feet trembled. The men stopped smiling. Heat spread through the forest.
Dexter rolled his shoulders. "If I have to take her back by force..." His eyes moved toward Aurelyx. "I won’t mind doing it."
The two men stared, then both sighed. "Hehehe." The first man’s expression turned cold. "Little kid."
His aura erupted.
’BOOM!’
Trees bent, and leaves exploded outward. Peak Ultra Realm.
Dexter’s eyes narrowed.
Then the second man’s aura erupted too.
’BOOM!’
The pressure doubled. Peak Ultra Realm. Both of them. And not ordinary Peak Ultra Realm experts. Their mana was dense, far stronger than the Ultra Realm enemies Dexter had encountered before.
The ground cracked beneath their feet merely from the pressure.
Dexter’s expression changed slightly, and the first man noticed. "Now you understand."
The second smiled. "Leave."
Dexter inhaled as he lowered his center of gravity. "Not until she comes with me."
The man’s smile vanished. "Then die.
Dexter disappeared. So did the second man.
A palm appeared between them, and Dexter’s fist crashed into it.
’BOOM!’
The collision detonated through the forest. The ground beneath both men collapsed as the trees shook violently.
A barely visible circular shockwave ripped leaves from branches and the Peak Ultra expert actually slid backward half a step. His eyes widened.
Dexter narrowed his eyes. ’Strong.’
Before Dexter could strike again, the man’s wrist rotated, and his palm shot toward Dexter’s chest. Dexter crossed both forearms.
’BANG!’
The impact launched him backward. He flew nearly thirty meters before his boots struck the ground.
’SCRAAAAAPE!’
Two trenches formed beneath his feet, and Dexter finally stopped. His forearms throbbed. He lowered them.
The Ultra expert looked at his palm. A red mark crossed it, and his expression darkened. "A Superhuman with the physical strength of an Ultra Human?"
Dexter didn’t answer as his eyes shifted. Aurelyx was walking away, and the second man accompanied her.
Dexter’s face darkened.
"GET BACK HERE!"
Heat erupted. "Scorching Fury!"
’BOOM!’
Massive flames exploded from Dexter’s body as the air distorted, and leaves near him curled instantly from the heat.
Black-red flames crawled across his shoulders and arms as his Flame Demon Bloodline surged.
The first man frowned. "What bloodline is that?"
The second glanced backward, and his expression became serious for the first time. "Doesn’t matter." He turned away. "You should be able to take him down. Don’t let him disturb the Monarch."
The first man smiled. "I am more than enough."
The second continued after Aurelyx.
Dexter’s eyes flashed. "Flame Burst Step!"
’BOOM!’
He disappeared, and the first man reacted immediately, punching toward Dexter’s expected path. Nothing. His eyes widened. Dexter had changed direction halfway through the burst.
A second explosion came from the side.
’BOOM!’
Dexter appeared behind the second man. His fist was covered in Abyssal Heavenly Flame. The second man’s instincts screamed and he turned but it was too late.
Dexter’s left foot struck the earth as his hips rotated. Every muscle from his leg to his shoulder transferred power into the punch. The second man raised both arms, and Dexter’s fist landed.
’BOOOOOOM!’
The man’s expression changed. His feet left the ground as he became a projectile.
’BANG!’
He struck a massive tree that was thicker than three men surrounding it with their arms outstretched.
The trunk exploded and man continued through it.
’Bang!’
A second tree snapped and he finally struck a boulder, and stone fractured.
Dexter immediately turned toward Aurelyx. "Lyra!"
He took one step.
’WHOOOOSH!’
Something screamed through the air. Dexter twisted instantly as a gray chain covered in vicious thorns ripped past his face. It curved unnaturally and came back.
The first man stood several meters away with one hand extended. Gray mana poured from his fingers. "I said..." The chain multiplied. "...I am your opponent!"

Three thorn-covered chains lashed toward Dexter. His pupils contracted. One came for his throat. One for his legs. One for his torso. His body reacted. The first missed. He jumped over the second. The third changed direction. Dexter reached out.
’CLANG!’
His hand caught it, and the Ultra expert blinked. Then smiled. "Idiot."
The chain moved like a living serpent, wrapping around Dexter’s forearm once. Twice. Three times. The thorns dug through his skin. Blood appeared, and the man’s smile widened.
"You dare grab my Violet Violent Thorn Vine?"
Dexter’s eyes narrowed.
As the man smiled and spoke. "Explode."
’BOOM!’
The thorns detonated. Blood sprayed. Chunks of flesh tore from Dexter’s forearm. Several thorns drove deep enough to scrape bone. The man expected a scream. None came.
Dexter looked at his arm, then at him. The man’s smile faded. "What?"

Pain, Dexter knew pain intimately. For months, the strange bond created through his investments and his wives’ conditions had forced him to endure echoes of agony that should have broken ordinary people. He had endured that for months and with the indestructible Buddha Endurance Scripture, every pain makes him stronger!
Dexter lifted his gaze. "That’s it?"

chapters.title: Chapter 272: 272 | Void Star Saber! Type 5!
paragraphs: The man’s expression changed. Dexter immediately grabbed the chain tighter, then pulled.
“What—”
The Ultra expert was yanked forward, his eyes widening. Dexter raised his knee.
‘BANG!’
The man twisted at the last instant, and Dexter’s knee crashed into his side instead of his abdomen.
‘CRACK!’
At least one rib broke. But the man was experienced. His elbow came down simultaneously.
‘BANG!’
It struck Dexter’s shoulder. Pain exploded down his arm, and Dexter staggered. A presence appeared on his right. The second man had returned. Fast. A palm slammed into Dexter’s ribs.
‘BOOM!’
Dexter flew sideways and twisted in midair and landed, his boots scratching across the ground.
The two Peak Ultra experts moved together with perfect coordination. One high. One low.
Dexter blocked a fist aimed at his head. The second man’s leg swept toward his knee. Dexter jumped. A palm followed and he twisted but another fist brushed across his jaw.
‘BANG!’
His head snapped sideways, and blood filled his mouth. Dexter staggered backward as the first man appeared behind him.
A thorn chain wrapped toward his throat. Dexter ducked, and the second attacked immediately. A kick slammed into Dexter’s stomach.
‘BOOM!’
He flew backward, and a tree exploded behind him. Dexter crashed through it, wood splintering everywhere, and landed hard.
The two men advanced. One smiled coldly. “You should have stayed at your picnic.”
Dexter slowly stood up as blood ran from the corner of his mouth. His damaged forearm was already beginning to heal, and the men noticed. Their expressions changed slightly.
The second frowned. “Regeneration?”

Dexter spat blood onto the ground, then opened his right hand. Space rippled, and a weapon appeared in his hand. It was a saber. The instant it materialized, the atmosphere changed. The blade was dark, with a faint star-like patterns shimmered along its surface as though pieces of the night sky had been trapped within the metal.
‘Type-5 Void Star Saber.’
The first man’s eyes narrowed. Dexter wrapped his fingers around the hilt, and a low hum rolled from the blade as the earth beneath him vibrated.
“Move.”
The first man stepped backward instinctively, and his expression changed when he realized he’d done it.
Dexter vanished as thunder exploded.
‘Crackle!’
The Ultra expert raised both palms as a mountainous barrier formed. “Mountain Fortress Barrier!”
A translucent wall appeared, and Dexter’s saber descended.
“Thunder GodKill Saber Art.”
Lightning crawled over the blade, and the Void Star Saber’s spatial patterns illuminated.
“Void Godslayer Slash!”
He cut. For one instant, nothing happened. Then the barrier split. The man’s pupils contracted. “What?”
The saber continued through.
‘SLASH!’
Blood erupted from his chest as he flew backward like a missle!
‘BANG!’
He smashed through a stone wall hidden among the forest ruins.
The second man’s face changed. “A Type-5 weapon!”
Dexter was already turning as blue lightning climbed the saber and flames followed like thunder.
Lighting and fire twisted together. The veins in Dexter’s arm bulged and his muscles screamed. He poured mana into the weapon.
“Thunder GodKill Saber Art, third Form.”
Dexter raised the saber and slashed. “Eightfold Lightning Severance!”
‘CRAKLE!!!’
One slash. No, eight.
The first thunderclap shook the forest. The man’s face hardened, and his palms rose toward the sky. Dark mana erupted. Clouds gathered unnaturally overhead.
“Shadow Bone Demon Finger!”
The sky darkened and a gigantic finger emerged from the swirling shadow clouds. It looked skeletal, ancient and demonic.
Black runes covered every joint as the enormous finger descended toward Dexter. Trees beneath it bent and the ground cracked.
Dexter’s first lightning blade rose.
‘BOOM!’
It struck the finger. Nothing.
The second followed.
‘BOOM!’
The finger slowed.
The third thunder blade crashed upward.
‘CRACK!’
The descending finger stopped. The man’s expression changed. “Impossible.”
Fourth.
‘BOOM!’
A crack appeared across the finger.
Fifth.
‘CRACK!’
More fractures spread.
Sixth.
‘BOOOOOOM!’
The demonic finger shattered as dark energy exploded through the sky.
The seventh lightning blade tore through the collapsing technique. It continued downward. The man roared. “Barrier!”
A thick Ultra Realm shield appeared.
‘CRACK!’
The seventh strike shattered it. His eyes widened. Then he saw the eighth.
‘BOOM!’

The final blade struck. The man disappeared. Trees exploded one after another. One. Two. Three. Four. He slammed through them before crashing into a massive boulder. The boulder detonated as dust erupted.
Silence descended through the entire forest.
Dexter stood in the center of the destruction as lightning crawled over his saber.
Flames burned around his shoulders as blood dripped from his knuckles. His chest rose and fell heavily and every breath stabbed his ribs.
One Peak Ultra expert lay buried beneath a ruined wall. The other was somewhere inside the cloud of shattered stone.
Dexter turned and Aurelyx stood farther ahead. She had stopped walking as her violet eyes rested on him.
Dexter lowered the saber. “Come here.”
Aurelyx’s brow furrowed. ”Annoying.’
She turned away, and something snapped inside Dexter.
“Lyra!”
He moved and he had only moved two steps when his pupils contracted.
The air beside Aurelyx distorted as space itself seem to have ffolded. Dexter stopped.
Someone stepped out: an older man in plain dark robes. His white hair was tied neatly behind his head. He carried no armour, no visible weapon, and no aura.
Dexter detected no footsteps or breathing. Most unsettling, he heard no heartbeat—even now. The silence remained absolute. The old man might as well have been a corpse.
He calmly placed one hand on Aurelyx’s shoulder, and she stopped. Her expression changed.
Dexter’s grip tightened around his saber. “Take your hand off her.”
The elderly man surveyed the wreckage: broken trees, shattered stone, cracked earth. Two injured Peak Ultra experts lay nearby. At last, his attention turned to Dexter.
“You have made quite a mess.”
Dexter raised the blade, and flames climbed it. “I said... let her go.”
The old man’s eyes briefly moved toward the saber. “A good blade.”
Then toward Dexter’s flames. “And a troublesome bloodline.” His expression remained completely indifferent. “But you should learn when to lower your head.”
The old man lifted one hand as his index finger extended towards Dexter.

chapters.title: Chapter 273: 273 | Get Away From My Wife!
paragraphs: The old man’s eyes briefly moved toward the saber. “A good blade.”
Then toward Dexter’s flames. “And a troublesome bloodline.”
His expression remained completely indifferent. “But you should learn when to lower your head.”
The old man lifted one hand as his index finger extended towards Dexter.
Dexter’s entire body froze as a single world reverberated through his entire body.
‘Death!’
Every hair on his body rose as his heartbeat thundered.
In that split second, his bloodline reacted before his mind did. The old man hadn’t attacked yet, yet Dexter felt as though he were already standing before the gates of death.
His fingers tightened as mana erupted with an explosive force!
“Asura Slaughter Demon Body!”
Patterns crawled across Dexter’s flesh as his muscles expanded and a murderous pressure erupted like a tsunami.
“Indestructible Buddha Endurance Scripture!”
Golden energy surged beneath his skin as his flesh tightened and his bones hardened. His organs became protected beneath layers of cultivated strength.
The old man’s eyebrow moved slightly.
But Dexter wasn’t finished. “Flame Demon Transformation!”
“BOOOOOOM!!!”
Dark flames erupted toward the sky like an nuclear explosion shooting out massive pillar of light into the skies.
Dexter’s form changed as g laming markings spread across his body. His hair whipped upward as his eyes burned like two suns.
Blue lightning wrapped around his right side and Abyssal Heavenly Flame covered his left.
Flame. Thunder. Bloodline. Body cultivation. Weapon. Everything merged making Dexter looked less like a Superhuman Realm cultivator and more like a demon god dragged from a battlefield.
The old man watched. “Interesting.”
Suddenly, he included his middle finger with his index finger as he pushed forward.
Dexter roared and the Void Star Saber screamed.
Spatial patterns across the blade erupted as space itself twisted and churned along its edge. Dexter slashed forward with his might.
“Rumble!!!”
The old man face turned cold as he tapped forward with his fingers.
But as the two strikes connected, there was no explosion, nor was there any dramatic manifestation.
Just one finger as a thin invisible force touched Dexter’s blade.
Then... silence!
Dexter’s eyes widened as the lightning vanished first as though erased from existence. Then the flames split and his spatial slash collapsed.
Dexter’s eyes widened as the force continued, his arms shook and his teeth clenched tightly and even the earth beneath him cracked into a massive crater.
For one impossible instant... he actually held it.
The old man’s expression finally changed slightly.
Dexter roared. “GET...” Blood vessels burst across his arms. “...AWAY...” His muscles tore. “...FROM...” He forced the saber sideways. “...MY WIFE!”
The finger force shifted slightly. But enough. The attack that had been aimed directly at Dexter’s chest moved as it penetrated.
‘PSSSH!’
Dexter’s body trembled.
Something punched through his left shoulder.
A perfect hole appeared as blood sprayed behind him and then the remaining force detonated.
‘BOOM!’
Dexter vanished as he flew through the forest like an artillery shell.
One hundred meters, two, three!
‘BANG!!!’
His body struck the side of a mountain and the entire mountainside trembled.
“RUMBLE!”
“CRAAAAACK!”
Fractures spread across the rock as birds exploded from trees. Loose stones tumbled downward and Dexter fell to the ground.
‘BANG!’
One knee struck the ground as his saber scraped beside him.
For several seconds, he couldn’t breathe as nothing entered his lungs. His mouth opened but there was no air.
Then suddenly... “GAAH!”
He dragged in a breath as pain exploded through him. His left shoulder was gone through as Blood poured down his chest. His shirt rapidly became soaked and his left arm hung uselessly.
Dexter looked at it. Then toward the distant old man. The elder stared back, and a faint crease appeared between his brows.
“You diverted it.”
His lips curled. “Even if you diverted it, my Transcendent energy should kill you soon.”
Dexter coughed as blood splattered the ground and a mysterious force surged through his entire body like a parasite destroying his bones, tissue, organs and flesh rapidly.
But Dexter wasn’t an ordinary person! His bones were comparable to iron, his flesh was thicker than leather and his organs were already forged. It wouldn’t be easy to destroy them.
The finger had been aimed at his chest but at the final instant, Dexter had forced the attack sideways. Barely.
The old man lowered his hand. “Consider that your warning.”
He turned and behind him, the two Peak Ultra experts were struggling out of the rubble.
The first held his chest where Dexter’s saber had opened a deep wound. The second’s arm hung unnaturally after the Eightfold Lightning Severance.
“Seventh Elder...”
The old man didn’t look at them. “Pathetic.”
Both lowered their heads. “We apologize.”
“Take yourselves back.”
Space began rippling beside him. The old man’s hand returned to Aurelyx’s shoulder.
Dexter saw it and his eyes became bloodshot. He planted the Void Star Saber into the ground as he stood up. Blood poured from his shoulder. His left arm remained useless. But he stood.
“Where...” The old man stopped. Dexter pulled the saber free. Blood ran over his lips. “Where do you think you’re taking my wife?”
Aurelyx looked toward him and for one brief instant, something changed in her eyes.
But then Aurelyx’s cold expression returned.
The old man looked back, and irritation finally appeared. “You survived because I allowed it.”
Dexter took one step, his boot leaving blood behind. The saber trembled in his hand. “Then...” Another step. “...try again.”
The two injured Ultra experts stared. One almost couldn’t believe what he was seeing. The old man’s expression darkened, and his finger rose again. This time, the pressure was different. Far worse.
Dexter felt the mountain behind him groan. He lifted his saber as his body screamed.
It didn’t matter. Lyra was behind that man. Dexter would rather crawl back to the festival carrying her than walk back without her.
The old man’s finger straightened. “Fool.”
Then a voice came from above. “Who gave you permission...”
The old man’s finger stopped.
“...to do as you wish here?”
Silence. Everyone looked up.

An elderly woman stood on top of a massive boulder. Her hands were behind her back. Gray hair stirred gently in the wind with absolutely no aura and mana pressure. There was nothing that gave away her position.

But as the two strikes connected, there was no explosion, nor was there any dramatic manifestation.
Just one finger as a thin invisible force touched Dexter’s blade.
Dexter’s eyes widened as the lightning vanished first as though erased from existence.
Then the flames split and his spatial slash collapsed.
Dexter’s eyes widened as the force continued, his arms shook and his teeth clenched tightly and even the earth beneath him cracked into a massive crater.
For one impossible instant... he actually held it.
The old man’s expression finally changed slightly.
“GET...” Blood vessels burst across his arms.
The attack that had been aimed directly at Dexter’s chest moved as it penetrated.
Something punched through his left shoulder.
A perfect hole appeared as blood sprayed behind him and then the remaining force detonated.
Dexter vanished as he flew through the forest like an artillery shell.
His body struck the side of a mountain and the entire mountainside trembled.
Fractures spread across the rock as birds exploded from trees.
Loose stones tumbled downward and Dexter fell to the ground.
One knee struck the ground as his saber scraped beside him.
For several seconds, he couldn’t breathe as nothing entered his lungs.
His mouth opened but there was no air.
He dragged in a breath as pain exploded through him.
His left shoulder was gone through as Blood poured down his chest.
His shirt rapidly became soaked and his left arm hung uselessly.
Then toward the distant old man.
The elder stared back, and a faint crease appeared between his brows.
“Even if you diverted it, my Transcendent energy should kill you soon.”
Dexter coughed as blood splattered the ground and a mysterious force surged through his entire body like a parasite destroying his bones, tissue, organs and flesh rapidly.
But Dexter wasn’t an ordinary person!
His bones were comparable to iron, his flesh was thicker than leather and his organs were already forged.
It wouldn’t be easy to destroy them.
The finger had been aimed at his chest but at the final instant, Dexter had forced the attack sideways.
The old man lowered his hand.
He turned and behind him, the two Peak Ultra experts were struggling out of the rubble.
The first held his chest where Dexter’s saber had opened a deep wound.
The second’s arm hung unnaturally after the Eightfold Lightning Severance.
The old man didn’t look at them.
The old man’s hand returned to Aurelyx’s shoulder.
Dexter saw it and his eyes became bloodshot.
He planted the Void Star Saber into the ground as he stood up.
“Where do you think you’re taking my wife?”
Aurelyx looked toward him and for one brief instant, something changed in her eyes.
But then Aurelyx’s cold expression returned.
The old man looked back, and irritation finally appeared.
Dexter took one step, his boot leaving blood behind.
The saber trembled in his hand.
The two injured Ultra experts stared.
One almost couldn’t believe what he was seeing.
The old man’s expression darkened, and his finger rose again.
This time, the pressure was different.
Dexter felt the mountain behind him groan.
He lifted his saber as his body screamed.
Dexter would rather crawl back to the festival carrying her than walk back without her.
Then a voice came from above.
An elderly woman stood on top of a massive boulder.
Her hands were behind her back.
Gray hair stirred gently in the wind with absolutely no aura and mana pressure.
There was nothing that gave away her position.

chapters.title: Chapter 274 | We Shall Meet Again!
paragraphs: Old Lady Lucy.
Dexter’s eyes widened. "Grandma Lucy?"
He hadn’t heard her approaching.
Lucy looked down as her eyes first went toward Dexter. His blood-soaked clothes and his ruined shoulder.
Then she looked toward the devastated forest. Broken trees and shattered stone with by rning patches of earth.
Her gaze finally settled on the old man but her expression didn’t change. "There are children nearby."
The old man’s eyes remained fixed on her. Something appeared on his face. He seemed to have recognized her as he stared in disbelief. "You..."
Lucy stepped off the boulder and Dexter’s eyes widened. There was nothing beneath her feet and yet, she didn’t fall. She simply walked. One step, then another across empty air!
Her pace was slow and lazy as though invisible stairs existed beneath her feet.
The two injured Peak Ultra experts became pale. One whispered, "Impossible..."
Lucy descended until she stood several meters above the ground.
The place turned entirely silent.
Aurelyx’s eyes narrowed. ’Interesting.’
Lucy descended until she stood several meters above the ground.
The old man’s expression had become completely serious. "This is a private matter."
Lucy looked toward Aurelyx. More specifically... at the hand on her shoulder. "Let her go."
The elder’s jaw tightened. "This does not concern you."
Lucy tilted her head. "I wasn’t asking whether it concerned me."
The forest seemed afraid to make noise. Even Dexter felt something strange. There was no pressure coming from Lucy.
Yet the atmosphere had changed completely. The old man had nearly killed Dexter with one finger. And now that same man was hesitating.
Lucy descended one final step as her feet touched the ground.
"I’m waiting."
The old man’s fingers tightened on Aurelyx’s shoulder. "The girl belongs..."
Lucy raised her eyes. "Think carefully about the rest of that sentence."
The words were quiet and gentle but the old man stopped speaking as the distortion behind him trembled. Then... ’Pop.’ It vanished.
Dexter’s eyes narrowed. The old man hadn’t dismissed it. Lucy had.
He looked toward her. For the first time since arriving, genuine anger appeared on the elder’s face. "You haven’t changed."
Lucy smiled faintly. "And you still talk too much."
The two wounded men looked between them and neither dared breathe loudly.
The elder’s jaw tightened. "You know what she is."
Lucy looked at Aurelyx. "I know enough.
"Then you understand she cannot remain here."
"That sounds like your problem."
"Lucy."
The name came out coldly and Dexter’s eyes narrowed. Seems like theyknew each other.
Lucy smiled. "There." She pointed lazily. "You remembered my name. We’re making progress."
The old man’s expression darkened. "This matter predates that boy."
Dexter didn’t say anything.
Lucy looked toward Aurelyx, then toward Dexter. "Does she want to leave?"
Aurelyx’s expression remained cold. ’I do.’
The words entered every mind present, and Dexter’s jaw tightened.
Lucy glanced at him.
Dexter immediately spoke. "It’s complicated, but she’s not leaving."
Aurelyx looked toward him. ’You don’t know what I want.’
Dexter’s gaze hardened. "No matter what, you’re not leaving here."
Aurelyx’s expression changed slightly and go r the first time, Aurelyx didn’t have an immediate response.
The old man’s expression hardened. "Enough." His grip tightened. "She returns with us."

Lucy looked at his hand and old man froze. Nothing visible happened but the ground within half a kilometer radius pressed in by a half a meter deep into the ground as though a hydraulic pressed slapped forcefully against the ground.
The two Ultra experts stared and the old man’s eyes became cold.
Lucy sighed. "I dislike repeating myself."
The elder’s arm trembled and for a moment, Dexter thought he would attack.
Instead, the old man stared at Lucy for a long while, then he slowly lowered his arm.
Aurelyx stepped away.
Dexter immediately extended his good hand. "Come here."
Aurelyx looked at it and then at him as her eyes moved toward his shoulder.
Blood still poured from the hole and his clothes were torn with his face bruised.
One arm hung uselessly but yet, he was still holding the saber and standing. Still glaring at everyone between himself and her.
Aurelyx’s lips tightened. ’Idiot.’
Dexter’s expression didn’t change. "Come here."
’You cannot order me.’
"Fine."
Dexter took a step toward her and his leg nearly buckled but he caught himself.
Aurelyx’s expression flickered.
Dexter extended his hand again. "Please."
Something changed and for the briefest instant, the coldness in Aurelyx’s eyes cracked as Lyra appeared beneath it. Then vanished.
Aurelyx clicked her tongue mentally. ’Annoying.’
She walked toward him. Dexter’s fingers closed around her wrist.
Thump. Thump. Thump.
There.
He exhaled. Only now did Dexter realize he’d been holding his breath.
Aurelyx looked down at his hand. Then at his shoulder and her expression became difficult to read.

Dexter pulled her behind him. Despite barely standing, despite having one functioning arm and despite the enemy elder being overwhelmingly stronger, Dexter still placed himself between Aurelyx and the others.
Lucy noticed, and her eyes flickered with amusement. The elder noticed too, and his expression became colder.
"This matter is not finished."
Lucy glanced toward him. "I didn’t say it was."
His gaze shifted to Dexter. "Boy." Dexter’s eyes narrowed. The old man continued. "You have no understanding of what you’ve involved yourself in."
Dexter’s grip tightened on the saber. "I understand enough."
"No." The elder looked toward Aurelyx. "You understand nothing."
He turned toward his injured subordinates.
"Take them," Lucy said.
The elder stopped, and Lucy nodded toward the two wounded men. "And leave."
The elder’s expression darkened. "You should know we are both half way to that realm. If we fought, things would get out of hand. Don’t push me."
Lucy smiled. "No?"
The old man’s face twitched. Dexter almost chuckled.
The elder gave a cold harrumph. "Hmph!"
Space distorted behind him but this time Lucy didn’t stop it. The elder swept his sleeve, and invisible force wrapped around the two injured Peak Ultra experts as they were dragged toward him.
One stared at Dexter, humiliation burning in his eyes. The other looked at Aurelyx. "Monarch..."
Aurelyx’s expression remained unreadable.
The old man stepped into the distortion. Before disappearing, he looked at Lucy, then at Dexter. Finally Aurelyx.
"We will meet again."

chapters.title: Chapter 275 | There You Are...
paragraphs: Dexter lifted his saber. "Next time, I will kill you."
The old man’s eyes narrowed.
Lucy looked toward Dexter. "Little Chef."
"What?"
"Stop provoking the man who nearly put a hole through your heart."
Dexter lips curled to a smirk. "He missed."
Aurelyx slowly turned her head toward him. Even with her cold personality, disbelief crossed her face.
Lucy chuckled slightly. "You really are troublesome."
The elder stared at Dexter for a long while then he disappeared. The two men vanished with him as the distortion in the air closed.
Silence returned and the forest became strangely peaceful as smoke drifted between broken trees. Small fires burned in patches and dust slowly settled.
Dexter continued staring at the space where the elder had disappeared.
Only after he was certain they were gone did he lower the saber.
The moment he did... his knees buckled but he caught himself.
Aurelyx stared at him with disdain. ’Pathetic.’
Dexter breathed heavily and stared at her indifferently but he wasn’t successfully ragebaited as he ignored her.
Aurelyx brows furrowed slightly and her eyes became slightly cold.
Lucy approached Dexter. "Sit."
"I’m fine."
Lucy stared at him with raised eye brow and Dexter paused, then sat.
"Good."
"I was going to sit anyway."
"Of course."

Dexter leaned against a broken boulder. His regeneration was already working as the flesh around the shoulder wound twitched and started to heal. However, the destructive energy from the man attack rapidly ravage his organs, tissues, bones and even his flesh.

However, Dexter wasn’t an ordinary person. His body had been tempered with the indestructible Buddha Endurance Scripture. His bones were even harder than steel, his flesh harder than an Ox’s skin and his organs stronger.
The energy which was supposed to ravage the organs of an Ultra rank Hero to death only stopped his injury from healing!
Lucy noticed the dilemma as she spoke. "His energy remains inside your body."
"You’re regenerating but his energy keeps destroying it."
Dexter’s expression hardened. "Annoying old bastard."
Lucy chuckled. "You’ve got courage."
Aurelyx remained beside him. Dexter turned toward her. "Now." She looked back. "Give her back."
Aurelyx’s expression became cold. ’No.’
Dexter’s eyes narrowed. "You’re using my wife’s body."
Aurelyx’s eyes sharpened as she stared at him indifferently. ’This is our body.’
Dexter stared at her for what seem to be a while before he slowly nodded his head. "Your shared body."
Aurelyx seemed slightly surprised.
Dexter continued. "But Lyra gets a say.
’And I don’t?’
"You do."
That answer surprised her more.
Dexter continued. "But you don’t get to suppress her, disappear without warning and leave with two strangers who tried to knock her unconscious."
Aurelyx’s eyes darkened. ’They weren’t strangers to me.’
"They were to Lyra."
Dexter stared into her eyes. "You called what we’ve been doing ’playing house.’"
Aurelyx said nothing.
"Maybe that’s what it feels like to you." His voice became quieter. "But it isn’t a game to her."
Aurelyx’s expression flickered.
"And it isn’t a game to me." Dexter pointed weakly toward the destroyed forest. "I just fought two Peak Ultra Realm experts and an old monster who nearly killed me."
Lucy raised an eyebrow. "Old monster?"
Dexter glanced at her as he scratched his head. "Not you Grandma Lucy."
Lucy’s lips curled upwards as her slightly wrinkled eye squinted. "Smart."
He looked back at Aurelyx. "I didn’t do all that because I’m bored."
Aurelyx stared.
Dexter’s voice hardened. "If Lyra wakes up tomorrow and tells me she wants to leave..." His jaw tightened. "I’ll listen."
Aurelyx’s eyes shifted.
"But you don’t get to make that choice for her."
For several seconds, neither spoke. Then Aurelyx looked away. ’You talk too much.’
Dexter smiled as he shrugged. "Lyra never complained."
’Perhaps the oldman should have hit your mouth instead.’
Dexter blinked his eyes. "You’re quite cruel."
Aurelyx glared and Dexter chuckled. Pain immediately stabbed through his ribs, making him cough repeatedly.
Suddenly, Aurelyx instinctively reached toward him but her hand stopped halfway. Dexter immediately noticed and she withdrew her hand but it was too late.
Dexter brows furrowed slightly as he glanced at her. "Interesting."
Lucy watched the exchange and laughed.
Both looked at her. "What?"
Lucy shook her head. "Young people."
She then turned to Aurelyx and spoke quietly. "Come here."
Aurelyx didn’t move. ’Why?’
Lucy smiled. "Because I’m asking nicely.
Aurelyx’s eyes narrowed. ’And if I refuse?’
Lucy looked toward the destroyed mountain. "Then I’ll ask less nicely."
Dexter almost laughed.
Aurelyx stared at the old woman, then reluctantly stepped forward. Lucy lifted two fingers. Aurelyx immediately stepped back.
’Don’t touch me.’
Lucy paused, then lowered her hand. "Fair."
Her gaze moved across Aurelyx’s body and Dexter could feel a strange fluctuation in the air. Suddenly, Lucy’s expression changed slightly.
"Hmm."
Dexter frowned. "What?"
Lucy ignored him. "Interesting."
"What’s interesting?"
Still nothing.
"Grandma Lucy."
She looked at him. "You’re nosy." But Lucy pointed toward Aurelyx as she spoke. "The two personalities might not be as separate as either believes."
Dexter’s expression changed, and Aurelyx’s eyes narrowed. ’Explain.’
Lucy shook her head. "Not here."
Dexter frowned. "Why?"
Lucy ignored him, turned around as she spoke. "We should return."
Dexter attempted to stand but his legs shook slightly.
Aurelyx reached for him again, and he leaned partly against her. At that moment, she suddenly frowned.
’You’re heavy.’
Dexter smiled. "Thought you were a mighty Shadow Queen."
Her eyes narrowed as she said indifferently. ’I can drop you.’
"You won’t."
’Try me.’
Dexter looked toward her and for a moment, the coldness in her eyes suddenly changed as a tiny twitch at the corner of her mouth.
Dexter’s smile softened, he knew that expression.
"Lyra?"
Aurelyx froze and her violet eyes flickered. Cold, warm, cold again and then her body stiffened as her hand moved to her temple.
Dexter’s expression changed. "Lyra?"
Aurelyx stumbled and Dexter immediately caught her. "Hey."
Her breathing became uneven as her eyes closed. And for several seconds, Dexter heard her heart beat pick up rapidly as her Shadow energy surged and then as rapid as it started, it all settled.
Her eyes opened and there was confusion, fear and then lastly, recognition.
Lyra stared at Dexter and her eyes widened when she saw the bloody hole in his shoulder and his shattered clothes.
Her face slightly became pale but Dexter immediately smiled. "There you are."

chapters.title: Chapter 276 | If Something Had Happened To You...
paragraphs: Lyra looked up to find Dexter, and relief appeared immediately before vanishing just as quickly.
Her eyes widened at the blood on him. His clothes were damaged, one sleeve ripped apart, and his forearm was covered in punctures and torn flesh.
His shoulder was worse as a bloody hole had been punched completely through it.
Lyra’s face drained of color, and her mental voice slammed into Dexter’s mind. ’Dexter?!’
He squinted and winced. "Not so loud."
Lyra rushed toward him, her hands hovering over his shoulder as she tried to find somewhere safe to touch. ’What happened?!’
Dexter glanced at Grandma Lucy, who stood several meters away quietly observing them, then looked back at Lyra. "We were ambushed."
Lyra froze. ’Ambushed?’
"Yeah."
Her brows furrowed, and Dexter saw the suspicion immediately. Lyra remembered those men. She remembered the hand approaching her neck. After that... nothing. It seemed they knocked her unconscious.
Dexter looked into her confused violet eyes. Lyra was optimistic, kind, sometimes ridiculously obsessed with food, and also playful when she felt safe and comfortable with you.
There was an innocence in her that had somehow survived everything she’d experienced. What would happen if he told her the truth?
Even the strongest person would struggle with that knowledge. And for Lyra? She might begin to spiral.
Fear would become sadness, sadness would feed the shadow corruption.

No, Dexter sure wasn’t going to tell her that another consciousness existed inside her, because that would simply make her depressed and sad and whenever Lyra’s negative emotions increased, so did her Shadow Corruption!
Once the corruption reached 100%, it could eventually transform her into a gateway connecting their world to the Shadow Realm, killing her in the process.
Lyra touched his injured forearm, her expression distressed. ’Did those two men do this?’
Dexter slowly nodded his head.
Lyra’s eyes turned a bit watery. ’It’s because of me. You’re like this because of me.’
Dexter immediately shook his head. "You’re thinking too much about it. They simply attacked you at random because you look like someone they knew."
Lyra looked into Dexter eyes searching if he was lying but Dexter wasn’t because he was telling half the truth. She looked like someone they knew, Aurelyx.
She sighed in relief but was still worried. ’You shouldn’t have fought them yourself, from my estimation, their strength is at the Peak of Ultra realm.’
’Since you’re a Hero working for the Hero Association, once you press the distress signal, a nearby Hero would come to your aid.’
’If something had happened to you...’ She paused and didn’t want to complete those words.
Dexter smiled, raising his hand to gently stroke her cheek. "Nothing happened Lyra. Moreover, my skin is very thick."
Lyra’s cheeks puffed, and Dexter almost laughed.

Lyra knelt beside Dexter and carefully examined his forearm first. The Violet Violent Thorn Vine had left ugly injuries, with thorns that had pierced deep and some that had exploded inside his flesh. His regeneration was already repairing the damage, but the wounds still looked terrible. Lyra’s hands trembled, and Dexter noticed.
"Hey." She looked up. "I’m okay."
Her expression said she didn’t believe him, so Dexter smiled. "Seriously."
She opened a small emergency medical pouch from the supplies Dexter carried in his spatial storage, and Dexter raised an eyebrow. "When did you learn first aid?"
Lyra stared at him.’I was once an high ranking Hero.’
"Right."

He sometimes forgot. Before their injuries, his wives hadn’t been helpless noblewomen. They had entered dungeons, fought monsters, seen blood. Mira had been known as the Crimson Valkyrie. Selene had been a powerful A-rank Hero. And Lyra... Dexter glanced at her. The Shadow Saintess, Aurelyx.
His smile faded slightly, and Lyra noticed. ’Does it hurt?’
Dexter immediately smiled again. "No."
She stared.
Dexter corrected himself. "A little."
Satisfied with his honesty, Lyra returned to the wound and cleaned his forearm carefully. Dexter didn’t flinch, but when she wrapped the bandage around his arm and tightened it...
"Ow."
Lyra immediately loosened it, and Dexter grinned. "Got you."
She froze, then realized he’d tricked her. Her eyes narrowed. ’You...’
"Made you stop worrying.
She immediately smacked his uninjured arm.
"You’re becoming as Violent as Mira."
She immediately smacked his arm again.
"Okay, okay."
Grandma Lucy watched them, then her gaze moved toward Dexter with a raised eyebrow as though asking. You’re really not telling her?
Dexter met her gaze, then winked. Lucy’s eyes narrowed then she sighed and didn’t say anything.
Dexter didn’t know exactly how much Lucy understood about Aurelyx or Shadow Corruption, but judging from her reaction earlier, she understood enough.
While she was wrapping his forearm, Dexter stared at her beautiful face, he couldn’t imagine losing her today. It would be devastating.
Lyra glanced at him and he quickly closed his eyes.
As he closed his eyes, he remebered the destructive energy within his body. If it were anybody else, it would have been impossible to handle but this was Dexter.
But not to mention the pure energy of the Limitless Grand Cosmos Scripture, he has several ways of purging the energy. Dexter chose to use the fastest way, the Abyssal Heavenly Flame.
Flames instantly surged from within him as it flowed through every path of his body, instantly burning the energy evaporating it instantly.

When he reached the wound on his shoulder, his jaw tightened as the destructive energy left by the white-haired elder reacted violently, like burning needles buried inside his flesh. Dexter inhaled, and the Heavenly Flame burned even hotter.
’Sssssss!’
Tiny strands of foreign energy began escaping, but Dexter’s face remained indifferent to the pain.
One minute, two and then three minutes.

Then the last trace vanished, and Dexter’s regeneration immediately exploded into action. Lyra raised an eyebrow as the bleeding stopped and his muscle fibers stretched across the hole, bone began repairing, and skin gradually formed.
Within minutes, what had been a horrifying wound started to heal rapidly.
Lyra cleaned the wound and bandaged it just in case and Dexter let her do it for her peace of mind.

sentences.text: Lyra looked up to find Dexter, and relief appeared immediately before vanishing just as quickly.
Her eyes widened at the blood on him.
His clothes were damaged, one sleeve ripped apart, and his forearm was covered in punctures and torn flesh.
His shoulder was worse as a bloody hole had been punched completely through it.
Lyra’s face drained of color, and her mental voice slammed into Dexter’s mind. ’Dexter?!’
Lyra rushed toward him, her hands hovering over his shoulder as she tried to find somewhere safe to touch. ’What happened?!’
Dexter glanced at Grandma Lucy, who stood several meters away quietly observing them, then looked back at Lyra.
Her brows furrowed, and Dexter saw the suspicion immediately.
She remembered the hand approaching her neck.
It seemed they knocked her unconscious.
Dexter looked into her confused violet eyes.
Lyra was optimistic, kind, sometimes ridiculously obsessed with food, and also playful when she felt safe and comfortable with you.
There was an innocence in her that had somehow survived everything she’d experienced.
What would happen if he told her the truth?
Even the strongest person would struggle with that knowledge.
Fear would become sadness, sadness would feed the shadow corruption.

No, Dexter sure wasn’t going to tell her that another consciousness existed inside her, because that would simply make her depressed and sad and whenever Lyra’s negative emotions increased, so did her Shadow Corruption!
Once the corruption reached 100%, it could eventually transform her into a gateway connecting their world to the Shadow Realm, killing her in the process.
Lyra touched his injured forearm, her expression distressed. ’Did those two men do this?’
Lyra’s eyes turned a bit watery. ’It’s because of me.
You’re like this because of me.’
They simply attacked you at random because you look like someone they knew."
Lyra looked into Dexter eyes searching if he was lying but Dexter wasn’t because he was telling half the truth.
She looked like someone they knew, Aurelyx.
She sighed in relief but was still worried. ’You shouldn’t have fought them yourself, from my estimation, their strength is at the Peak of Ultra realm.’
’Since you’re a Hero working for the Hero Association, once you press the distress signal, a nearby Hero would come to your aid.’
’If something had happened to you...’ She paused and didn’t want to complete those words.
Dexter smiled, raising his hand to gently stroke her cheek.
Moreover, my skin is very thick."
Lyra’s cheeks puffed, and Dexter almost laughed.
Lyra knelt beside Dexter and carefully examined his forearm first.
The Violet Violent Thorn Vine had left ugly injuries, with thorns that had pierced deep and some that had exploded inside his flesh.
His regeneration was already repairing the damage, but the wounds still looked terrible.
Lyra’s hands trembled, and Dexter noticed.
Her expression said she didn’t believe him, so Dexter smiled.
She opened a small emergency medical pouch from the supplies Dexter carried in his spatial storage, and Dexter raised an eyebrow.
Lyra stared at him.’I was once an high ranking Hero.’
Before their injuries, his wives hadn’t been helpless noblewomen.
They had entered dungeons, fought monsters, seen blood.
Mira had been known as the Crimson Valkyrie.
Selene had been a powerful A-rank Hero.
His smile faded slightly, and Lyra noticed. ’Does it hurt?’
Satisfied with his honesty, Lyra returned to the wound and cleaned his forearm carefully.
Dexter didn’t flinch, but when she wrapped the bandage around his arm and tightened it...
Lyra immediately loosened it, and Dexter grinned.
She froze, then realized he’d tricked her.
She immediately smacked his uninjured arm.
She immediately smacked his arm again.
Grandma Lucy watched them, then her gaze moved toward Dexter with a raised eyebrow as though asking.
Dexter met her gaze, then winked.
Lucy’s eyes narrowed then she sighed and didn’t say anything.
Dexter didn’t know exactly how much Lucy understood about Aurelyx or Shadow Corruption, but judging from her reaction earlier, she understood enough.
While she was wrapping his forearm, Dexter stared at her beautiful face, he couldn’t imagine losing her today.
Lyra glanced at him and he quickly closed his eyes.
As he closed his eyes, he remebered the destructive energy within his body.
If it were anybody else, it would have been impossible to handle but this was Dexter.
But not to mention the pure energy of the Limitless Grand Cosmos Scripture, he has several ways of purging the energy.
Dexter chose to use the fastest way, the Abyssal Heavenly Flame.
Flames instantly surged from within him as it flowed through every path of his body, instantly burning the energy evaporating it instantly.
When he reached the wound on his shoulder, his jaw tightened as the destructive energy left by the white-haired elder reacted violently, like burning needles buried inside his flesh.
Dexter inhaled, and the Heavenly Flame burned even hotter.
Tiny strands of foreign energy began escaping, but Dexter’s face remained indifferent to the pain.
One minute, two and then three minutes.
Then the last trace vanished, and Dexter’s regeneration immediately exploded into action.
Lyra raised an eyebrow as the bleeding stopped and his muscle fibers stretched across the hole, bone began repairing, and skin gradually formed.
Within minutes, what had been a horrifying wound started to heal rapidly.
Lyra cleaned the wound and bandaged it just in case and Dexter let her do it for her peace of mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 277: 277 | I’m The Handsome Escort!
paragraphs: Dexter rotated his shoulder. “Much better.”
Lyra stared at him and Dexter grinned. “See?”
She slapped his arm again.
“Ow.”
‘Stop smiling!’
“What should I do? Cry?”
Lyra looked exasperated, and Dexter laughed before his expression became more serious. “Lyra.” She looked at him. “Don’t tell Mira and Selene.”
Lyra blinked. ‘About what?’
“The ambush and the injury.”
Her expression changed as she frowned. ‘What? Why?’

Dexter continued before she could protest. “Today was supposed to be a happy day.” He looked back toward the distant festival where faint music drifted through the trees. “Mira and Selene were having fun while you almost emptied the candy store.” His expression softened.
Lyra looked offended by the last accusation, and Dexter ignored it. “I don’t want them spending the rest of today worrying.”
“I’m healed.” He showed his shoulder. “Mostly.” Then his bandaged forearm. “And this will be fine soon.”
Lyra remained hesitant, and Dexter smiled. “Just for now, when we get home, we can tell them everything, together..”
Her violet eyes narrowed. ‘You’re asking me to lie.’
“Not really, just avoid saying somethings.”
Grandma Lucy snorted. “That’s still called lying.”
Dexter looked at her. “Whose side are you on?”
“My own.”

Lyra folded her arms, but she reluctantly nodded her head in understanding. It had been three years since any of them had fun last, the fact that Dexter was still thinking about them at this moment made Lyra’s heart tighten and her face warmed involuntarily.
Dexter smiled. “Good girl.”
Lyra immediately glared at him but didn’t refute as her face burned even more.
Dexter flipped his hand and his spatial ring opened. A fresh outfit appeared in his hand, it was a black shirt with long sleeves.
Perfect.

Dexter changed behind a large tree while Lucy and Lyra waited, and when he returned, the bandages around his forearm were completely hidden, his shoulder looked normal, his trousers were clean, and his hair was... acceptable.
“How do I look?”
Lyra stared. ‘Suspicious.’
Dexter frowned. “How does someone look suspicious?”
She pointed at the clean shirt. ‘Different clothes.’
Dexter looked down. “...Right.”
Lucy laughed. “Your wives aren’t idiots.”
He smiled bitterly but his chest puffed with pride. ” know.”
“Then this should be entertaining.”
Dexter sighed. “Let’s go.”
The festival was exactly as they’d left it. Children ran around, music played, the artificial waterfall glittered beneath the afternoon sun, and families continued exchanging food.
Nobody knew that more than a mile away, a section of forest had nearly been flattened.

Dexter walked beside Lyra with Grandma Lucy following several steps behind them. As they approached the picnic area, Dexter immediately saw Mira was seated in her wheelchair already with a terrible expression while Selene stood beside her and Tessa sat nearby. Nobody was eating.
Dexter frowned and increased his pace.
Mira saw him, and her shoulders visibly relaxed.
Selene heard the approaching footsteps turned and she sighed in relief once she saw Dexter and Selene walking toward them.
Mira looked through Lyra first then only then did she look at Dexter and her eyes immediately narrowed.
Dexter frowned slightly and asked. “Why aren’t you two eating?” But they didn’t say anything.
Dexter looked between them. “What?”
Selene brows furrowed as she approached him. “Did something happen?”
Dexter chuckled. “What could happen?”
Selene stopped in front of him. While her eyes couldn’t see details clearly, but she could perceive his general shape.
She tilted her head, and Dexter suddenly remembered something unfortunate. Selene didn’t need eyes to examine him. Her ears were becoming terrifying. She could hear his heartbeat.
He kept his expression relaxed. “Nothing happened.”
Mira looked at his shirt. “You changed clothes.”
Dexter looked down. “Oh.”
Mira waited, and Dexter’s brain moved quickly. “Lyra went to the restroom.” Silence. Tessa blinked. Mira stared. Dexter continued. “I escorted her so she wouldn’t get lost.”
Mira’s eyes narrowed. “And that explains your shirt?”
Dexter paused. “No.”
Selene’s lips twitched, and Dexter cleared his throat. “There was... water.”
“Water.”
“Yes.”
Mira stared. “A lot of water.”
“At the restroom?”
“Near it.”
Mira looked toward Lyra, and Dexter also looked toward Lyra.
Lyra froze as everyone stared at her. She swallowed, and her mental voice entered their minds. ‘Y-Yes.’
Dexter almost closed his eyes. Terrible. Absolutely terrible.
Lyra couldn’t lie. ‘It is true.’
Mira’s eyebrow rose, and Selene slowly turned her head toward Dexter but he simply smiled.
Nobody believed them and not even Tessa.
Tessa’s father looked away, probably because he didn’t want to become involved, and Old Lady Lucy returned to her place and calmly picked up her bowl.
Mira looked at her. “Grandma Lucy?”
“Hm?”
“You went after them.”
Lucy took a spoonful. “I went for a walk.”
Dexter stared at her. ‘Really?’
Lucy didn’t look at him, and Mira’s eyes narrowed further but she didn’t push.
Selene stepped closer to Dexter and inhaled slightly. Dexter froze.
“You smell like smoke.”
“...Festival.”
“There’s no smoke here.”
“Grilled meat.”
Selene tilted her head. “And something else.”
Dexter remained silent as she reached toward his arm. He casually moved away and grabbed a pastry. “Hungry?”
Selene’s expression changed as Dexter bit into it. “Mmm. Good.”
Mira stared while Lyra looked guilty and Lucy ate peacefully. Finally, Mira sighed. “Fine.”
She looked directly at him. “We’ll talk later.”
Dexter suddenly preferred fighting the two Peak Ultra Realm experts. “About what?”
Mira smiled, and nothing about that smile was friendly. “Later.”
Dexter swallowed. “Right.”
Fortunately, the festival provided an excellent escape.
After another 10 minutes of eating, talking, and pretending nothing unusual had happened, Dexter stood. “All right.”
Mira looked up. “What now?”
Dexter pointed toward the amusement area. “We didn’t come here just to eat.”
Lyra’s eyes immediately brightened, and Selene smiled while Mira leaned back. “What are you planning?”
Dexter looked across the field and pointed at a particular section. “That.”
Mira followed his gaze, and her eyes widened slightly. “Paintball?”
“Paintball.”
Selene was silent for several seconds, and then she shook her head. “We don’t have to do it anymore.”
Dexter’s eyebrows furrowed. “Why?”
“We’ve already done plenty.” Selene smiled. “I had fun.”
