chapters.title: Chapter 278: 278 | Tiny Victories
paragraphs: Dexter continued to stare at her.
Her smile weakened slightly, and Dexter studied her as she clasped her hands together. “It’s getting late, everyone must be tired.”

Dexter immediately understood. She wasn’t thinking about herself, she was thinking about them. Probably him most of all. Maybe she’d noticed more than Dexter realized. Selene might not know exactly what had happened, but she wasn’t stupid.
Dexter shook his head. “No.”
Selene blinked. “No?”
“Don’t give up something you wanted because you’re worried about everyone else.” Her expression softened as Dexter continued. “Today belongs to you three.”
Mira raised an eyebrow. “Us?”
“Yes.”
“What about you?”
Dexter thought for a moment. “I’m the handsome escort.”
Mira rolled her eyes while Lyra immediately shook her head and Selene laughed. Dexter looked offended and he snapped.
“That received far too much disagreement.”
Lyra nodded again.
Dexter’s lips cruled to a sneer. “Traitor.”
Selene smiled. “Fine.” Dexter looked toward her, and she nodded. “Let’s play then .”
Dexter’s grin returned. “That’s what I wanted to hear.”
The paintball arena was much larger than it appeared from outside.

It had been designed as a miniature ruined town with artificial stone buildings throughout the field, wooden fences creating narrow passages, and large barrels, abandoned carts, broken walls, providing cover. A shallow artificial stream divided one section, elevated platforms overlooked several lanes, and colorful paint splatters covered almost every surface.
Dexter nodded approvingly. “This is actually impressive.”
An attendant approached. “First time?”
“Yes.”
The attendant looked at Mira’s wheelchair, then smiled. “We have adaptive equipment.”
Ten minutes later, Mira’s wheelchair had been temporarily fitted with larger outdoor wheels and protective side panels.
Mira frowned as she looked down. “This is ridiculous. You guys can play, I will watch.”
Dexter stared at her wheelchair, which now resembled a miniature armored vehicle and said in awe. “It’s beautiful.”
Mira glared as Dexter tutted.
“I’m jealous.”
Her lips curled up as she smiled. “Good.” The thought of quitting temporarily left her mind.
The attendant explained that the arena had formations preventing participants from using abilities beyond ordinary physical movement, and Mira smiled. “Perfect.”
Dexter looked at her. “Why are you smiling?”
“Because now you can’t cheat.”
“I wasn’t planning to cheat.”
Dexter stared, and Mira stared back. Neither believed the other.
They changed into protective gear, Dexter in black, Mira in red, Selene in blue, and Lyra in purple and each received a paintball marker.
The attendant divided them. “Two teams. Choose your partner.”
Dexter thought for a while and immediately spoke before any of them could. “Me and Selene.”
Mira placed one arm on her hip as she frowned. “Why?”
Dexter lips curled upwards.
“Because if you and I are on the same team, you’ll shoot me anyway.”
Mira chuckled but didn’t disagree with him.
Lyra pointed at herself and Mira, and the attendant nodded. “Red and Purple against Black and Blue.”
Dexter looked toward Selene as he clenched his fist. “We’ve got this.”
Selene smiled. “You’re more excited than I am.”
Dexter blinked his eyes. “I’ve always wanted to shoot someone.”
Selene hovered her mouth as she giggled.
Across from them, Mira whispered to Lyra—well, Mira whispered while Lyra communicated mentally. Dexter narrowed his eyes. “What are you plotting?”
Mira looked up. “Nothing.”
“Suspicious.”
“You’re suspicious.”
The attendant raised a whistle. “Positions!”
They separated, and Dexter helped Selene toward their starting area. “Remember, listen for movement.”
Selene smiled. “You’re not supposed to use hero abilities.”
“The formation only supress one of your talent, you should be able to use the second one.”
Selene shook her head with a smile as Dexter grinned in return.
The whistle blew.
‘FWEEEEET!’
Dexter immediately dove behind a wall while Selene calmly stepped behind a barrel.
‘POP!’
A paintball exploded against the wall where Dexter’s head had been. He froze as red paint dripped downward. “Mira!”
Her laughter came from somewhere ahead. “You talk too much!”
‘POP! POP! POP!’
Dexter ducked as three more shots splattered around him. “She isn’t even trying to hit Selene!”
Selene smiled from behind the barrel. “I think this may be personal.”
“You think?”
Another barrage arrived, and Dexter rolled as a paintball narrowly missed his shoulder. His wound twinged, and he ignored it. “All right.” He raised his marker. “War.”
Dexter peeked around the wall but there was nothing.
The formation only supress one talent. The others have two which meant they could use their second talent!
While he couldn’t use Enhanced Hearing, which was annoying.
He moved carefully with Selene following. “Can you locate them?”
“Maybe.”
Dexter stared. “Maybe?”
“I hear movement.”
“Where?”
Selene pointed, and Dexter looked toward a ruined building. “Lyra?”
“Probably.”
Dexter smiled. “Cover me.”
Selene raised her marker as Dexter sprinted.
‘POP!’
A purple paintball struck the ground. “Missed!”
‘POP!’
Dexter ducked.
‘POP!’
Another nearly struck his leg. “Still missed!”
He reached the wall, and then something red struck him directly between the shoulder blades.
‘SPLAT!’
Dexter stopped as Mira’s laughter erupted.
He slowly turned to find Mira sitting behind a wooden barricade twenty meters away, her marker resting comfortably against the adaptive support attached to her chair as she waved.
Dexter looked down at the red paint and glared at her.
“Hmph!”
Lyra suddenly appeared above him on a platform, her marker pointed directly at his head. Dexter’s eyes widened. “Lyra.”
She smiled.
‘POP!’
Dexter jumped sideways as purple paint exploded against the wall, then ran as Lyra chased him with shots.
‘POP! POP! POP!’
“This is bullying!”
Mira shouted from behind. “Stop whining!”
Dexter dove behind a fake cart where Selene was laughing. He looked at her. “Some teammate you are.”
“I’m covering you.”
“From what?”
‘POP!’
A blue paintball flew past Dexter and struck Mira’s barrier. Mira ducked, and Dexter grinned. “Never mind. Excellent work.”
Selene tilted her head. “I heard her chair.”
Mira’s expression changed. “That’s cheating.”
Selene smiled. “I’m blind.”
Mira paused. “That’s...”
She couldn’t finish, and Dexter burst out laughing. Selene used the opportunity.
‘POP!’
Blue paint struck Mira’s protective side panel.
‘SPLAT!’
Mira looked down. Silence. Dexter stopped laughing as he recognized that expression.
“Mira?”
She slowly raised her marker. “Run.”
Dexter blinked. “I wasn’t the one who shot you!”
‘POP! POP! POP!’
“WHY ME?!”
He ran while Selene laughed so hard she nearly lost her orientation.
The first round became chaos. No strategy survived longer than thirty seconds.
The second round became even worse. This time, everyone against Dexter. He hadn’t agreed to that. Apparently democracy had spoken. Three wives. One husband.
Dexter stood at one end of the arena while Mira, Selene, and Lyra stood opposite him. He stared at the attendant. “You’re allowing this?”
The attendant shrugged. “They requested it.”
Dexter looked down at himself, paint covering nearly every part of his protective gear.
The attendant blew the whistle.
Dexter dodged immediately.
‘POP! POP! POP!’
Paintballs chased him. “You women have no loyalty!”
Lyra’s mental voice reached him. ”Surrender.”
“Never!”
A blue paintball exploded beside his head. Selene.
Dexter peeked to find Mira holding center, Selene covering the right lane, and Lyra missing.
He narrowed his eyes. “Not this time.”
He moved fast as he sprinted through the ruins. Mira fired, and Dexter ducked. Selene fired, and he slid behind cover. “Missed!”
Then purple paint exploded against his backside.
‘SPLAT!’

Dexter froze as the entire arena became silent. He slowly turned to find Lyra standing behind him, her eyes widened because she hadn’t meant to hit him there. Mira saw the paint and burst into laughter.
Selene heard. “What happened?”
Mira could barely speak. “Lyra... shot...”
She laughed harder, and Dexter’s face became dark.
Selene tilted her head. “Where did she hit you?”
“Nowhere.”
Mira wheezed. “His backside!”
Selene covered her mouth, then started laughing. Lyra’s entire face turned red, and Dexter pointed at her. “You...”
‘Sorry!’ Lyra immediately apologized.
Mira rolled her eyes. “You’re still standing.”
Dexter fell theatrically. “Tell my story.”

By the fourth round, even the attendants were laughing. Several festival visitors had gathered outside the arena to watch, and Dexter had somehow become the villain. Every time he was hit, people cheered.
“This is ridiculous!”
A child shouted from outside. “Get him!”
Dexter pointed. “I don’t even know who you are!”
The child laughed.
After paintball, they tried the shooting gallery. Dexter expected to dominate. He did not.
Mira’s years as a Hero showed immediately. Even seated in her wheelchair, she calmly aimed the light rifle and hit the targets. Ten shots. Ten hits.
Dexter stared as Mira handed the rifle back.
“I underestimated you.”
“Obviously.”
Dexter tried. Ten shots. Nine hits. Mira smiled as Dexter looked at the missed target. “I was distracted.”
“By?”
“The sun.”
They were under a canopy. Mira stared.
Dexter cleared his throat. “Wind.”
“No wind.”
“Weapon calibration.”
Mira laughed.
Selene stepped forward, and Dexter hesitated. “Want to try?”
“Yes.”
She held the rifle, and the targets produced small sounds whenever they moved. Selene listened.
First shot. Hit. Second. Hit. Third. Miss. Fourth. Hit.
By the end, she’d struck seven. Dexter stared as Selene lowered the rifle. “How many?”
“Seven.”
Her face lit up. “Really?”
“Really.”
She smiled, and Dexter found himself smiling too.
Then Lyra stepped forward. Ten shots. Eight hits.
They played ring toss, and Lyra won. They played a ball-throwing game, and Mira won. They tried a ridiculous fishing game designed for children, and Selene somehow won.
Dexter stared at the small stuffed dragon she’d received. “How?”
Selene hugged it. “Talent.”
Dexter looked toward Mira. “She’s becoming arrogant.”
Mira nodded. “Your influence.”
“Why is everything my fault?”
All three women looked at him, and Dexter sighed. “Right.”
Later, they rode the giant observation wheel. Unlike the roller coaster, it moved slowly.

When they finally returned to the picnic field, evening had begun settling over the festival. Lanterns illuminated the area, strings of magical lights appeared among the trees, the artificial waterfall glowed blue and gold, children ran with luminous toys, and music softened.

Dexter spread the mats again. Mira chose to sit on one, and he carefully transferred her from the wheelchair and positioned her legs comfortably. Selene sat nearby, and Lyra dropped onto the mat with an exhausted sigh.
Dexter looked at her. “Tired?”
She nodded.
“Good.”
Her eyes narrowed.
“Maybe you’ll stop trying to empty every food stall.”
She threw a pillow at him, and Dexter caught it.
Mira leaned back. “Today was...” She paused, and Dexter looked toward her. “Terrible?”
Mira glanced at him, then toward the glowing festival. “Acceptable.”
Dexter smiled. “That’s practically a glowing review from you.”
She rolled her eyes.
Selene hugged the small dragon she’d won. “I liked it.”
Dexter looked at her. “Even the roller coaster?”
She hesitated. “Especially the roller coaster.”
Dexter grinned. “I knew it.”
“But I’m still scared of heights.”
“That’s okay.”
Selene smiled. “I know.”
Lyra’s voice entered their minds. ‘Paintball again next time.’
Dexter stared. “No.”
Mira smiled. “Definitely.”
Selene nodded. “I agree.”
Dexter looked betrayed. “Three against one again?”
Mira leaned back comfortably. “Marriage.”
Dexter sighed. “Mistake.”
Mira’s eyes narrowed. “What mistake?”
Dexter immediately corrected himself. “A wonderful mistake.”
Selene laughed, Lyra smiled, and Mira nodded. “Better.”
Dexter looked at them, his wives.

Hours earlier, he’d fought two Peak Ultra Realm experts and he’d nearly died. A man whose strength Dexter couldn’t properly comprehend had almost taken Lyra away. There were enemies waiting beyond this garden. Secrets, Aurelyx. The Eternal Winter Ice , the Nine Great Families, Violette’s inheritance, the Ashfords and hidden danger Dexter hadn’t accounted for yet.
But here? For tonight? None of it mattered.
Mira was laughing and Selene could see colors while Lyra could faintly hear the festival music beneath the muffled world surrounding her.
‘Tiny victories.’
Dexter leaned backward on his hands and smiled.
“Worth it.”

“Don’t give up something you wanted because you’re worried about everyone else.” Her expression softened as Dexter continued.
Mira rolled her eyes while Lyra immediately shook her head and Selene laughed.
Dexter looked offended and he snapped.
Dexter’s lips cruled to a sneer.
“Fine.” Dexter looked toward her, and she nodded.
The paintball arena was much larger than it appeared from outside.

It had been designed as a miniature ruined town with artificial stone buildings throughout the field, wooden fences creating narrow passages, and large barrels, abandoned carts, broken walls, providing cover.
A shallow artificial stream divided one section, elevated platforms overlooked several lanes, and colorful paint splatters covered almost every surface.
The attendant looked at Mira’s wheelchair, then smiled.
Ten minutes later, Mira’s wheelchair had been temporarily fitted with larger outdoor wheels and protective side panels.
Mira frowned as she looked down.
You guys can play, I will watch.”
Dexter stared at her wheelchair, which now resembled a miniature armored vehicle and said in awe.
Her lips curled up as she smiled.
“Good.” The thought of quitting temporarily left her mind.
The attendant explained that the arena had formations preventing participants from using abilities beyond ordinary physical movement, and Mira smiled.
Dexter stared, and Mira stared back.
They changed into protective gear, Dexter in black, Mira in red, Selene in blue, and Lyra in purple and each received a paintball marker.
Dexter thought for a while and immediately spoke before any of them could.
Mira placed one arm on her hip as she frowned.
“Because if you and I are on the same team, you’ll shoot me anyway.”
Mira chuckled but didn’t disagree with him.
Lyra pointed at herself and Mira, and the attendant nodded.
“Red and Purple against Black and Blue.”
Dexter looked toward Selene as he clenched his fist.
Selene hovered her mouth as she giggled.
Across from them, Mira whispered to Lyra—well, Mira whispered while Lyra communicated mentally.
They separated, and Dexter helped Selene toward their starting area.
“You’re not supposed to use hero abilities.”
“The formation only supress one of your talent, you should be able to use the second one.”
Selene shook her head with a smile as Dexter grinned in return.
Dexter immediately dove behind a wall while Selene calmly stepped behind a barrel.
A paintball exploded against the wall where Dexter’s head had been.
He froze as red paint dripped downward.
Her laughter came from somewhere ahead.
Dexter ducked as three more shots splattered around him.
“She isn’t even trying to hit Selene!”
Selene smiled from behind the barrel.
Another barrage arrived, and Dexter rolled as a paintball narrowly missed his shoulder.
His wound twinged, and he ignored it.
Dexter peeked around the wall but there was nothing.
The formation only supress one talent.
The others have two which meant they could use their second talent!
While he couldn’t use Enhanced Hearing, which was annoying.
He moved carefully with Selene following.
Selene pointed, and Dexter looked toward a ruined building.
Selene raised her marker as Dexter sprinted.
A purple paintball struck the ground.
He reached the wall, and then something red struck him directly between the shoulder blades.
Dexter stopped as Mira’s laughter erupted.
He slowly turned to find Mira sitting behind a wooden barricade twenty meters away, her marker resting comfortably against the adaptive support attached to her chair as she waved.
Dexter looked down at the red paint and glared at her.
Lyra suddenly appeared above him on a platform, her marker pointed directly at his head.
Dexter jumped sideways as purple paint exploded against the wall, then ran as Lyra chased him with shots.
Dexter dove behind a fake cart where Selene was laughing.
A blue paintball flew past Dexter and struck Mira’s barrier.
She couldn’t finish, and Dexter burst out laughing.
Blue paint struck Mira’s protective side panel.
Dexter stopped laughing as he recognized that expression.
“I wasn’t the one who shot you!”
He ran while Selene laughed so hard she nearly lost her orientation.
No strategy survived longer than thirty seconds.
The second round became even worse.
Dexter stood at one end of the arena while Mira, Selene, and Lyra stood opposite him.
Dexter looked down at himself, paint covering nearly every part of his protective gear.
A blue paintball exploded beside his head.
Dexter peeked to find Mira holding center, Selene covering the right lane, and Lyra missing.
He moved fast as he sprinted through the ruins.
Selene fired, and he slid behind cover.
Then purple paint exploded against his backside.
Dexter froze as the entire arena became silent.
He slowly turned to find Lyra standing behind him, her eyes widened because she hadn’t meant to hit him there.
Mira saw the paint and burst into laughter.
She laughed harder, and Dexter’s face became dark.
Selene covered her mouth, then started laughing.
Lyra’s entire face turned red, and Dexter pointed at her.
By the fourth round, even the attendants were laughing.
Several festival visitors had gathered outside the arena to watch, and Dexter had somehow become the villain.
Every time he was hit, people cheered.
“I don’t even know who you are!”
After paintball, they tried the shooting gallery.
Mira’s years as a Hero showed immediately.
Even seated in her wheelchair, she calmly aimed the light rifle and hit the targets.
Dexter stared as Mira handed the rifle back.
Mira smiled as Dexter looked at the missed target.
Selene stepped forward, and Dexter hesitated.
She held the rifle, and the targets produced small sounds whenever they moved.
By the end, she’d struck seven.
Dexter stared as Selene lowered the rifle.
She smiled, and Dexter found himself smiling too.
They played ring toss, and Lyra won.
They played a ball-throwing game, and Mira won.
They tried a ridiculous fishing game designed for children, and Selene somehow won.
Dexter stared at the small stuffed dragon she’d received.
All three women looked at him, and Dexter sighed.
Later, they rode the giant observation wheel.
Unlike the roller coaster, it moved slowly.
When they finally returned to the picnic field, evening had begun settling over the festival.
Lanterns illuminated the area, strings of magical lights appeared among the trees, the artificial waterfall glowed blue and gold, children ran with luminous toys, and music softened.
Mira chose to sit on one, and he carefully transferred her from the wheelchair and positioned her legs comfortably.
Selene sat nearby, and Lyra dropped onto the mat with an exhausted sigh.
“Maybe you’ll stop trying to empty every food stall.”
She threw a pillow at him, and Dexter caught it.
“Today was...” She paused, and Dexter looked toward her.
Mira glanced at him, then toward the glowing festival.
“That’s practically a glowing review from you.”
Selene hugged the small dragon she’d won.
Selene laughed, Lyra smiled, and Mira nodded.
Dexter looked at them, his wives.
Hours earlier, he’d fought two Peak Ultra Realm experts and he’d nearly died.
A man whose strength Dexter couldn’t properly comprehend had almost taken Lyra away.
There were enemies waiting beyond this garden.
The Eternal Winter Ice , the Nine Great Families, Violette’s inheritance, the Ashfords and hidden danger Dexter hadn’t accounted for yet.
Mira was laughing and Selene could see colors while Lyra could faintly hear the festival music beneath the muffled world surrounding her.
Dexter leaned backward on his hands and smiled.

chapters.title: Chapter 279 | Thank You For Today
paragraphs: Dexter would have stayed on that mat until midnight if the three women beside him had allowed it. Unfortunately, Lyra yawned.

She tried to hide it behind her hand, then immediately yawned again. Selene had gone quiet beside her, her fingers moving slowly over the little stuffed dragon and her large teddy bear, and even Mira’s answers had grown shorter, although she still managed to glare whenever Dexter looked too pleased with himself.
He glanced at the skies and spoke. "All right. Let’s go home."
Lyra lifted her head. ’Already?’
"Yeah. You girls must be tired"
Lyra shook her head. "I’m not really tired."
Dexter chuckled. "I saw you yawning just now."
’I was resting my mouth.’
"After everything you ate, it deserves a holiday."
She reached for the pillow again, and Dexter caught it before she could throw it, laughing as he stood.
Around them, families were folding blankets and gathering empty dishes. Soft music still drifted across the field.
Dexter looked at it once more before bending to collect their things.
He packed the remaining snacks and food, checked made sure nothing had been left beneath the mat, then he crouched beside Mira.
"Ready?"
She nodded and lifted her right arm toward him as he carefully lifted her and returned her to the wheelchair.
Once she was comfortable, he turned toward Old Lady Lucy.
She sat nearby with an empty cup in her hand, looking so ordinary that anyone passing would have mistaken her for a grandmother enjoying the evening breeze.
Dexter knew better.
For a moment, he remembered the white-haired elder scared if her.
His smile faded into something quieter as he approached her. "Grandma Lucy."
She looked up. "Leaving?"
"The girls are tired."
She sighed as she spoke. "Yeah, today was a bit hectic."
Dexter laughed under his breath, then brought a covered dish out of his spatial storage.
He had set aside a generous plate of the Grade Five meal before packing away the cooler, its lid sealed tightly to keep both the warmth and its rich aroma inside.
He offered it to her with both hands.
Lucy’s eyebrows rose. "What’s this?"
"My way of saying thank you."
She studied his face instead of the container, and Dexter held her gaze. He didn’t mention the forest and she knew what he meant.

Something softened around the old woman’s eyes. She nodded and accepted the gift, resting it carefully beside her. "All right. Little chef. Take care of yourself. Your wives are almost falling asleep."
Dexter glanced back to find Lyra immediately straightening and muttered. ’I wasn’t sleeping.’
Tessa came over while Dexter was gathering the last container. "You’re abandoning us?"
Dexter rolled his eyes at her. "We literally live next to each other.
She remained silent and Dexter gave her a suspicious look. "Did you want something?"
Tessa smiled brightly. "Were there any leftovers?"
Lyra’s head turned at once, and Dexter looked between them before shaking his head. "I’m surrounded."
He passed Tessa a small parcel of the remaining sharing food.
She accepted it happily and then waved to the girls while her father reminded them to drive safely.
"Good night, everyone," Dexter said.
Selene raised her hand, Mira nodded toward Lucy with her usual sharp expression gentler for a moment, and Lyra waved to them enthusiastically.
They followed the path toward the parking area, leaving the music and laughter behind them.

At the vehicle, Dexter opened the doors before returning to Mira. He lifted her into her seat, settled her legs properly, and fastened the supporting harness without allowing the straps to press against her neck.
She watched him check the buckle twice. "It hasn’t changed since this morning."
"There’s no harm checking again."
Mira rolled her eyes, but her right hand briefly touched his wrist before he stepped away. Dexter looked down, and she had already withdrawn it.
He smiled but didn’t say anything.
The journey home was quiet.
Festival lights slid across the windows, then gave way to the warm glow of streetlamps.

In the rearview mirror, Dexter saw Lyra watching the garden disappear behind them while Selene held her large teddy bear and small dragon against her stomach, her head turned toward the shifting patches of light outside.
"Can you see them?" he asked gently.
Selene nodded. "Only the colors."
A golden streetlamp passed over the roof, and her lips curved. "But I can tell when we go underneath one."
Dexter kept his eyes on the road, and his smile stayed with him all the way home.
When they reached the bungalow, he parked near the entrance and unfolded Mira’s wheelchair first.
Lyra stepped out carrying her teddy bear too, followed by Selene.
Dexter opened Mira’s door and waited while she placed her right arm around him, then lifted her carefully, keeping her close as he lowered her into the chair.
Inside, Dexter switched on the lights. Their little living room appeared exactly as they had left it, the clean air carrying the faint scent of the tea he had brewed that morning.
Lyra looked around, then released a long, pleased breath.
’We’re home.’

Dexter paused with his hand still on the door. She had said it casually, already walking toward the hallway but he stood there for another second before closing the door and checking the protection talisman.
’Home.’
He liked how she easiky said the word, as though she had completely accepted him and that this was their true home.
"We should go bathe," Selene said, touching the ends of her hair and there were a few leaves on it.
Lyra suddenly laughed as she pointed at Dexter. ’Your hair!’
Both Selene and Mira chuckled as they looked at Dexter ruffled hair with various leaves on it too.
Dexter huffed and pointed toward the hallway. "Bed. All of you."
Selene laughed softly, then stopped near their bedroom door. "Dexter."
He looked up from the bags.
"Thank you. For today."
Lyra nodded beside her, the playfulness fading into a warm smile. ’I really enjoyed it.’
Dexter’s chest tightened pleasantly and a certain warmth increased even more, radiating through his entire body as he replied. "Anytime."
"Good night," Selene replied.
’Good night, Dexter.’
"Good night..."

chapters.title: Chapter 280 | Mira’s Kiss...
paragraphs: Lyra made a face at him before disappearing into the bedroom. Selene glanced at him a bit of reluctance on her face before she followed after her and Dexter turned to Mira. "You should bath first."
Mira nodded, and he wheeled her toward the bathroom.
The familiar routine should have settled him. He placed clean nightclothes on the dry shelf, spread a towel within reach, and tested the water with his wrist.
Mira watched him from beside the tub, her necklace resting against the dress.
Dexter reached toward the clasp, then paused. "May I?"
Her eyes lifted to his as she raised an eyebrow. "You’ve been helping me bathe for months."
"I meant the necklace."
She was slightly embarrassed but she lowered her chin slightly, giving him room.

His fingers brushed the warm skin at the back of her neck as he unfastened it, and Mira went unusually still. He set the necklace carefully beside her clothes, then helped her out of the dress and lowered her into the bath.
For a while, neither spoke as Dexter washed the festival dust from her arms and shoulders, then worked shampoo gently through her red hair.
Usually, Mira had at least three complaints ready before he finished the first rinse.
Tonight, she simply closed her eyes and enjoyed the warmth.
When she turned slightly toward him, he found himself looking at her face longer than necessary.
"What?" she asked.
"Nothing."
"Liar."
"You looked happy today."
Mira looked down at the water. "I won most of the games."
"That must have been it."
She flicked a little water at his wrist with her right hand, making Dexter chuckled, but she didn’t say anything else.
After a moment, her gaze suddenly went to his shoulder and ti Dexter surprise, she asked.
"Does it still hurt?"
His hand stopped and the sound of water dripping became suddenly loud.
Dexter sighed and he admittted. "Just a little," he admitted.

Mira’s jaw tightened. Dexter had alredy taken her pain and not just hers alone, he had taken Selene and Lyra’s pain too. Now he somehow managed to get himself injured, it made Mira furious and extremely distressed. "You getting injured really irks me. If it were up to me, I’d lock you up at home with me."
Dexter looked at her and saw she was serious.
He nodded slowly, and Mira looked at the sleeve covering his bandages. "Will you tell me what happened?"
"I wasn’t planning on hiding it from your girls forever. But tommorow, I will tell you three what had happen."
She studied him for several seconds, then her right hand closed lightly around his wrist.
"Alright. I know you’re trying to protect us but we’ve grown stronger compared to months ago. Don’t look down on us."
Dexter covered her fingers with his free hand. "All right."
She released him first and looked away. "There had better not be a next time."
That drew a small laugh from him. "I’ll do my best."

He finished bathing her without rushing. When she was ready, he helped her out, dried her carefully, and settled her in the wheelchair. She pushed her right arm into the sleeve of her nightdress herself while he helped with the other, then watched him fasten the buttons.
Mira glanced down at his hands.
Dexter looked up, and they held each other’s gaze for a moment before both nearly smiled.
He combed the damp ends of her hair, placed the towel around her shoulders, and checked that her feet rested comfortably on the supports.
"There."
He gathered the damp towels and set them aside. Then smiled as he spoke.
"Good night, Mira."
He had barely turned when she spoke. "Wait."
Dexter looked back. Mira had moved the wheelchair a little closer, her right hand resting on the armrest, and she seemed suddenly interested in the floor between them.
"Something wrong?"
"No." She took a breath, then lifted her face. "Thank you for today.
The words were quiet and unguarded, and Dexter’s expression softened. "Mira, you don’t have to—"
Crimson light suddenly appeared beside her chair.
He stopped.

Her spectral arms formed, but instead of reaching for a towel or the wheelchair handles, they lowered toward her legs. The mana shifted, stretching into a finer shape as it followed the line of her thighs and knees.
The glowing forms seemed to sink into the outline of her legs, leaving a thin crimson sheen over the skin. Her feet lifted from the footrests and settled on the floor.
"Mira?"
Her fingers tightened around the armrest. "Don’t distract me."

She leaned forward, and Dexter moved immediately, hands ready to catch her. But she was already rising, the spectral limbs supporting and guiding her own as her knees slowly straightened and she stood up!
On her two feet.
Dexter forgot everything as his eyes dropped to the mana holding her steady.
Her legs hadn’t suddenly healed, he could see the effort in her face and the slight tremor at her knees she was actually proficient enough to merge the spectral arm with her legs!
He couldn’t imagine how much pain and practice she went through for this.
"You’ve been practicing," he whispered.
"Dexter..."
He looked up and Mira leaned forward, her right hand catching his sleeve for balance, and before his mind could catch up with the movement, her lips touched his cheek.
Soft, warm and electric.
Dexter went completely still as heat spread from that small point of contact, moving across his face until even his ears felt hot.
He could feel her breath near his skin, and for one bewildered second, he couldn’t remember what he was supposed to do with his hands.
Mira’s face was almost as red as her hair. She stayed close just long enough to whisper beside his ear. "If you tell anyone about this, I will kill you."
Then she drew back.
Dexter stared at her as his mouth opened, but nothing came out.
Mira looked briefly satisfied with that result.
Then the light around her knees flickered, and he caught her elbow as she lowered herself carefully into the wheelchair.

chapters.title: Chapter 281: 281 | Lyra’s Kiss...
paragraphs: It was the only useful word Dexter could manage as he watched Mira wheel herself out of the bathroom with her spectral arms.
He didn’t quite remember walking to his room and it took sometime before he finally came to.
‘I certainly didn’t expect this...’
He ended ended up sitting on the edge of his bed and every time he tried to think about the remarkable control Mira had shown over her spectral arms, his mind returned to the warmth of her lips.
She had stood up to kiss him. That thought was proving much more difficult to handle than any cultivation mystery.
Nearly half an hour passed before a gentle knock sounded at his door. Dexter lowered his hand from his cheek. “Come in.”

Lyra stepped inside. She had changed into a simple purple colored dress and nightdress, her freshly washed hair lying loose around her shoulders, still damp at the ends, and she carried the clean scent of soap into the room with her.
Her eyes found his face immediately. ‘What are you thinking about?’
Dexter smiled. “Nothing much.”
She narrowed her eyes slightly as she pouted slightly.
Dexter cleared his throat. “Come in properly. You don’t have to stand at the door.”

She closed it behind her and approached the bed. For a moment, her fingers brushed over the blanket as though deciding where to sit, and then she settled beside him, close enough that the mattress dipped gently beneath them both.
Dexter turned toward her. “Is anything wrong?”
Lyra eyes became a bit watery, then pouted. ‘Is it bad I came to your room?’
“Of course not.” He smiled. “I was only worried something had happened.”
‘Nothing happened.’ Her expression eased up, and she looked down at her hands before looking at him again. ‘Just wanted to say thank you for today.’
Dexter’s smile faded into something gentler. Lyra tucked a damp strand of hair behind her ear.

‘I had fun. Even though... I missed what happened.’ Her gaze moved to his shoulder. Dexter resisted the urge to immediately assure her that everything was fine. She had been there. She had cleaned the wounds herself. Instead, he waited.
She sighed as she stared at the ceiling.
‘It’s been years since I had a day like that, even before I was injured.’
Dexter looked at her hands resting on the blanket. “Then we’ll have to do it again.”
Her eyes brightened. ‘That would be nice.’
Then her lips curled upwards. ‘And without you complaining whenever you lose.’
“I was outnumbered!”
‘Same thing.’

Dexter laughed, and Lyra’s smile widened at the sound. For a while, they sat together without speaking. She didn’t reach for her phone or look toward the door. Her shoulder nearly touched his, and she seemed content simply to remain there.
Then she turned toward him more fully. ‘Dexter.’
“Hmm?”
Her fingers gathered a small fold of the blanket. ‘Teach me how to kiss again.’
He blinked, a bit stunned as Lyra held his gaze, though a blush was already spreading across her cheeks. The quiet room seemed to grow much smaller.
“You want another lesson?” he asked softly.
She nodded. ‘I don’t think I learned everything last time.’
There was a shy hint of mischief in her eyes.

Dexter recognized it now—that little attempt to sound innocent while asking for exactly what she wanted. What he suspected last time was true, she wasn’t learning to kiss just because, she wanted to kiss him.
Ar the realization, Dexter’s heartbeat quickened.

He turned toward her, and she slowly released the blanket. The uncertainty that had followed their earlier encounter with Aurelyx didn’t take hold this time. He knew from the familiar rhythm of her heartbeat, it was Lyra.
He lifted his hand slowly, brushing a damp strand of hair away from her cheek. “Are you ready?”
Her gaze moved to his mouth, then returned to his eyes. ‘Yes.’
Dexter leaned closer, and Lyra met him halfway.

Their lips touched gently at first, the electric contact made them both pause. Her mouth was warm, and the small breath she released brushed his lips before she closed her eyes and he kissed her again, softly, letting the moment settle between them.

Lyra’s hand found his sleeve. She held it for a few seconds, then loosened her grip and shifted closer. Her shoulder touched his chest, and Dexter’s hand moved to the side of her face, his thumb resting lightly against her cheek.
She leaned into his palm. That small, trusting movement affected him more than he expected.
He drew back just enough to look at her. Lyra opened her eyes, which was a bit dazzling. ‘Why did you stop?’
The question was so immediate that he almost laughed. “I was checking on my student.”
‘Your student is alright, continue.’
His smile touched hers when he leaned in again. This time, she didn’t hesitate as her lips cover Dexter’s upper lip.
Dexter arrested her lower lip, kissing and caressing them carefully with his own lips as their breath became one.
She tilted her head to follow his movement, and the kiss grew steadier and Dexter almost forgot everything.
There was only Lyra sitting close to him, choosing to close the remaining distance.
Her fingers suddenly slid from his sleeve to his shoulder, then into his hair as her fingers tangled against his hair, drawing his lips even tighter to hers.
“Mnn~”
A quiet sound escaped her lips against his mouth, barely more than a breath, and Dexter trembled before he could stop himself.
Lyra felt it. Her fingers stilled for a moment, then softened in his hair.

He held her gently at the shoulder, giving her room to pull back whenever she wished. She stayed, kissing him with growing confidence, occasionally losing the rhythm and finding it again and neither seemed eager to end it in the slightest.
More than a minute slipped by in those close, unhurried kisses before they finally drew apart, both breathing harder than before.
Dexter remained near her for a moment, his forehead almost touching hers. Lyra’s fingers were still in his hair.

He didn’t quite remember walking to his room and it took sometime before he finally came to.
He ended ended up sitting on the edge of his bed and every time he tried to think about the remarkable control Mira had shown over her spectral arms, his mind returned to the warmth of her lips.
She had stood up to kiss him.
That thought was proving much more difficult to handle than any cultivation mystery.
Nearly half an hour passed before a gentle knock sounded at his door.
Dexter lowered his hand from his cheek.

She had changed into a simple purple colored dress and nightdress, her freshly washed hair lying loose around her shoulders, still damp at the ends, and she carried the clean scent of soap into the room with her.

You don’t have to stand at the door.”

I missed what happened.’ Her gaze moved to his shoulder.

chapters.title: Chapter 282: 282 | Give Me Your Hand...
paragraphs: More than a minute slipped by as the warmth of their lips entangled each other, before they finally drew apart, both breathing harder than before.
Dexter remained near her for a moment, his forehead almost touching hers as he stared at ger closed eyes.
Lyra’s fingers were still in his hair.

Lyra’s eyes opened slowly and their eyes locked for a few seconds before she shyly looked at his face, then at her hand, and then seemed to realize just how close she had moved. The blush that followed reached all the way to her ears.
Dexter smiled, equally warm-faced. “Was that—”
Lyra stood up so quickly that the mattress bounced beneath him.
‘I-I should go sleep.’
He blinked. “You don’t have to—”
‘Good night!’
She was at the door before he could finish. Her hand fumbled with the handle once, which only made her cheeks redden further. Dexter wisely swallowed his laugh.
“Good night, Lyra.”
She glanced back at him for a brief moment and smiled. Then she slipped out and closed the door.
Dexter sat in silence.
He looked down at the slight crease she had left in the blanket and let out a long breath.
“Cultivation,” he told the empty room.
That was what he needed to do to calm his rampaging thoughts.
He crossed his legs and closed his eyes.
The first attempt failed almost immediately. He could still feel Lyra’s fingers in his hair.

Dexter opened one eye, frowned at the door, then started again. Gradually, the familiar pattern of the Limitless Grand Cosmos Scripture steadied his breathing. Mana gathered around him, entering his body in a slow, even stream.
The lingering strain in his shoulder eased as he guided energy through the repaired pathways.
The house settled around him and he heard a ater stopped running in the bathroom. The cupboard closed and then soft footsteps crossed the hallway and faded behind the girls’ bedroom door.
Dexter listened until he was sure everything was well, then let himself sink fully into cultivation.
Almost two hours passed.
[Ding!]
The sound rang clearly through his mind.
[Today’s investments have been evaluated.]
Dexter’s eyes opened.
He had almost forgotten about the system.
Golden text began forming before him.
Then suddenly, the room grew cold as tiny mist seeped in from underneath his door.
A faint chill brushed his arms and slipped beneath the warmth surrounding the bed. Dexter looked toward the door before the handle moved. He already knew that heartbeat.
The door creaked open and Selene entered, silver hair falling loosely over the shoulders of her nightdress.
She didn’t linger at the threshold as she had on the first night. Her bare feet followed the familiar route across the room, avoiding the corner of the table without hesitation.
Dexter quietly dismissed the waiting notification.

And just like that, Selene reached the bed and sat beside him, smoothing the fabric over her knees. She was carrying the small dragon she had won at the festival. After a moment’s consideration, she placed it beside his pillow.
Dexter’s mouth curved, and Selene tilted her face toward him. “I came to cultivate.”
He nodded, as he activated his heavenly flame, warmth already spreading from his body toward her. “I know.”
Her shoulders eased as the chill around her began to soften.
Selene’s fingers brushed the edge of the duvet.
Dexter glanced at the space beside him before shifting closer to the wall. “Then come here. You’re sitting a bit close to the edge.”
Selene moved toward his voice, and their shoulders brushed. Dexter reached behind her and adjusted a pillow against the headboard. “Lean back.”
Selene did so slowly. The pillow supported her lower back, and a quiet breath escaped her as the strain in her shoulders eased.
“Better?” he asked.
She nodded.
Dexter settled beside her, their legs folded beneath them and their knees resting lightly against each other.
It was a particularly large bed, and there was only so much space he could give her without pressing himself into the wall.
Not that Selene appeared particularly concerned about the lack of distance. She adjusted the hem of her nightdress over her knees, placed her hands in her lap, and closed her eyes.
Dexter watched her for a moment before doing the same.

The Limitless Grand Cosmos Scripture began circulating. Mana gathered around the bed, drawn toward them by their activated Star Nodes, and Dexter’s breathing gradually slowed as the familiar technique guided the energy through his meridians.
Beside him, Selene’s circulation followed the same rhythm.
The Seventh-Tier technique was remarkably forgiving about posture. Once its circulation had been properly established, they could maintain it while sitting, standing, or lying down.

Even sleep wouldn’t entirely interrupt the steady absorption of mana. Yet both of them still cultivated cross-legged most of the time cause it helped with concentration. It was a habit built all their lives.

Warmth gradually spread from Dexter’s body. He kept his Heavenly Flame carefully restrained, allowing its heat to reach her without filling the room with enough heat to disturb the others or ignite the room.
Selene’s shoulder relaxed against his, and the contact and for a long while, neither spoke.
The house was quiet, and outside, the occasional passing vehicle disturbed the silence before fading into the distance.
Dexter concentrated on Selene’s breathing. It had become steadier, but every few minutes, a faint shiver still passed through her.
The Eternal Ice was extremely stubborn. The warmth surrounding her helped, but some of that heat was lost before it reached the places that needed it most.
Nearly an hour passed before Dexter opened his eyes. Selene was still cultivating beside him, her silver hair slipped forward over one shoulder and her hands folded tightly in her lap.
“Selene.”
Her head turned slightly. “Hmm?”
“Give me your hand.”
She opened her eyes. Dexter held his palm upward between them. “It’s easier to guide the warmth into your body if we make direct contact. You won’t have to rely only on the heat around us.”
“Oh.”
There was no hesitation like Dexter had expected, Selene lifted her hand and placed it in his!

chapters.title: Chapter 283 | Sleep With me...
paragraphs: Dexter paused as their hands touched.
Her fingers were cold with a chill that seemed to come from deep inside her, settling into her skin no matter how warmly she dressed. He gently closed his hand around hers.
"Tell me if it gets uncomfortable."
She nodded.
Dexter adjusted his position until their shoulders rested together more firmly, then guided a thin, controlled current of his Heavenly Flame through their joined hands.
Selene’s fingers tightened, and Dexter immediately reduced the flow. "Too much?"
"No." The answer came quickly. She took a slow breath. "It’s nice."

He looked at her face before increasing it a little. The warmth traveled through her wrist and up her arm, and wherever it passed, the cold pressing against her meridians began to retreat. Selene released a long, comfortable sigh.
Her head rested back against the pillow, and the tension around her mouth gradually disappeared.
Dexter smiled. "That much?"
"Mm."
Her answer was barely a sound. He continued guiding the flame, keeping it gentle as it passed through her damaged pathways.
He couldn’t simply force more heat into her and hope for the best. Her meridians were healing, and carelessness could undo the progress they had made.
A few minutes later, Selene shifted her hand inside his. Dexter loosened his grip, thinking she wanted to adjust her wrist. Instead, her fingers slipped between his.
He looked down at their hands resting together on the blanket.
Selene’s eyes remained closed, but the faint color rising along her neck suggested she was perfectly aware of what she had done.
Dexter said nothing. He simply held her hand more comfortably and resumed cultivating.

Roughly another hour passed and the warmth flowing through Selene had become steady enough that Dexter no longer needed to watch every small movement of his mana, and her breathing was even. Occasionally, her head tilted toward him before she straightened again.
The third time it happened, Dexter opened his eyes and he realized she was fighting sleep. To be honest so was he.

The day had finally caught up with him—fighting the two men and surviving the elder’s attack, running around the festival, and then returning home had left him more tired than he wanted to admit. Cultivation had helped his body recover, but it hadn’t replaced rest.
Dexter moved his shoulder slightly, and Selene immediately lifted her head. "What’s wrong?"
"It’s nothing." He smiled. "I’m just tired."
She sat a little straighter. "Oh. I should go—"
"That isn’t what I meant."
Her fingers loosened inside his, but Dexter refused to let go.
"I’m going to lie down," he explained. "You should too. You need the rest."
"I’m awake."
Dexter looked at her.
Selene turned her face away. "Not completely."
He chuckled. "You don’t have to sit cross-legged to cultivate. The Scripture will keep circulating while you rest."
"Why don’t on make yourself comfortable."

She didn’t answer immediately, and Dexter noticed the way her free hand pressed against the blanket. Sitting beside him was one thing. Cultivating together was familiar now. Lying down beneath the same duvet...
Her face slowly warmed.
Dexter followed her silence to its obvious conclusion, and his own expression became slightly awkward. "You can stay on that side," he said, nodding toward the empty pillow. "There’s enough room."
Selene tilted her head. There wasn’t very much room. They both knew it.
Dexter cleared his throat. "Enough for sleeping."
"That doesn’t make it sound better."
He blinked, then laughed quietly. Selene’s mouth curved, although she quickly pressed her lips together.
Dexter unfolded his legs, keeping their hands joined while using his free hand to pull back the duvet.

His knees felt stiff after sitting for so long. He stretched them beneath the blanket, adjusted his pillow, and carefully lowered himself onto the mattress. The movement pulled gently against Selene’s hand.
She remained sitting beside him.
Dexter looked up at her. "You can let go if you want.
Her fingers tightened instead. For several seconds, she said nothing. Then she slowly uncrossed her legs.

Dexter lifted the duvet out of her way while she turned and settled onto the mattress beside him. She moved, feeling for the pillow before resting her head, letting her silver hair spread over the fabric.

At first, her body was very stiff as she layed down, leaving a narrow strip of mattress between them. Their joined hands rested in that space. Dexter drew the duvet over her, making sure it covered her feet before pulling it gently up to her shoulders.
"Comfortable?"
Selene nodded.
Dexter settled back against his pillow and continued the circulation of the Scripture, while emanating heat from his heavenly flame, keeping a gentle stream of warmth flowing into her.

Selene turned her face toward him. In the dim room, she could make out little more than a darker shape against the pillow, but she knew where his face was. She knew the sound of his breathing and the rhythm of his heart.
"You’re sure this is all right?" she asked softly.
Dexter turned toward her. "Selene, it’s alright."
She remained quiet, then her thumb moved lightly against the side of his hand. "Good night, Dexter."
He smiled. "Good night, Selene."
Her cheeks warmed beneath the duvet, and neither released the other’s hand.
Dexter woke before his alarm.
At first, he didn’t open his eyes. Something soft brushed the underside of his chin, and a comfortable weight rested across his chest. He breathed in slowly—soap, a faint sweetness, Selene.
His eyes opened.
For several seconds, he simply stared at the ceiling. Then he lowered his gaze.
At some point during the night, the small distance between them had disappeared completely.
Selene was snuggled against him, her cheek resting on his chest with one arm wrapped around his waist.
Her other hand still held his beneath the duvet, although their fingers had loosened during sleep.
She had drawn one knee close beside his leg and curled toward his warmth so thoroughly that there was barely any space left between them.

Dexter went still as her silver hair lay across his shirt, a few strands tickling his neck whenever she breathed. He looked at the empty pillow beside her, then back at the woman sleeping against him.

chapters.title: Chapter 284 | Stay A Few More Minutes l
paragraphs: ’So much for staying on her side.’
A smile slowly appeared on his face. He had woken with Selene leaning against him before, but this was different.
They weren’t sitting cross legged this time, they were lying comfortably beneath the same blanket, and she had found her way into his arms as naturally as though she belonged there.
Dexter’s smile softened.
The Scripture was still circulating, and his Heavenly Flame remained gentle, its warmth passing into her through the places their bodies touched.
Selene’s skin was no longer pale and there was a hint of warmth and redness were on her skin now.
More importantly, she was sleeping peacefully and the Eternal Ice suppressed inside her.
Dexter looked toward the clock. It was almost time to get up and it was at this time he cooks too but because of the festival yesterday, there was kind of a holiday today.
As he was thinking about it, Selene suddenly shifted. Her arm tightened around his waist, and her face turned more fully against his chest as a small, contented sigh escaped her mouth.
Dexter looked back at the clock.
’A few minutes.’

He reached carefully toward the bedside table and switched off the alarm before it could ring. Then he settled back down. His free hand hovered over Selene’s shoulder, and after a moment, he gently pulled the duvet higher around her.
She seemed to feel the movement even in sleep. Her fingers searched beneath the blanket until they found his hand properly again.
Dexter let her take it.
Selene woke to warmth.
For a while, that was all she understood. Warmth beneath her cheek, around her shoulders and a steady but powerful heartbeat close to her ear.

She had absolutely no desire to move as her body felt unusually light, free of the constant prickling sensation and discomfort that usually greeted her in the morning. Even the cold deep inside her seemed distant.
She drew a slow breath and moved closer.
Then something beneath her cheek shifted and Selene’s eyes instantly snapped open.
She froze as her echolocation spread through the room almost instinctively, returning the familiar shape of Dexter’s bed, the headboard, the bedside table—and Dexter. Directly beneath her cheek.
Her arm was around him, her body was pressed against his. She was practically hugging him in her sleep.
Heat rushed into her face. Slowly, very slowly, she lifted her head.
"Good morning.
Dexter’s voice was warm with amusement.
Selene stopped breathing for a moment. "You’re awake?"
"For a little while."
’A little while.’ That answer made everything worse. She immediately began pulling back. "I’m sorry. I didn’t mean to—"
Dexter loosened his arm to give her room. "You haven’t done anything wrong."
Selene sat halfway up, clutching the duvet against herself even though her nightdress was perfectly in place. "I was..."
"Hugging me."
Her face burned. "Dexter."
"What? I’m helping you explain."
"You’re not helping."

He laughed softly, and Selene turned away, wishing the floor would open beneath the bed and take her with it. Last night, she had agreed to lie beside him. ’Beside’ him. Not wrap herself around him like a climbing vine.
"You could have woken me."
Dexter’s smile faded a little. "You were sleeping so well, I didn’t want to wake you."
Selene’s grip on the duvet loosened. For a moment, she didn’t know what to say
Dexter watched her for a moment. "How do you feel?"
The question pulled her attention inward. She checked her breathing, the pressure inside her meridians, the familiar cold beneath within her, and her eyebrows lifted slightly.
"Better."
Dexter smiled. "That’s good."
Selene nodded. It was more than good. She couldn’t remember the last time she had slept so peacefully. It’s as thought every sleep she had here got even better then the last.
Her gaze lowered toward where he still held her hand.
Selene brushed her thumb over his knuckles. "Thank you."
Dexter looked at their hands, then back at her. "You don’t have to thank me every time."
"Then stop giving me a reason to."
He fell silent. Selene seemed to realize what she had said a second later, and her cheeks warmed again, but this time she didn’t take the words back.
Dexter’s mouth slowly curved. "All right," he said. "I’ll try to become less considerate."
She squeezed his hand and glared at him. "I didn’t say that."
The answer came so quickly that they both paused. Then Dexter laughed, and Selene lowered her head with a small smile
For a little while, they remained that way.
Then Selene glanced toward the clock. "I should go. You wake up around this time to start breakfast."
Selene nodded, though her fingers didn’t immediately release his hand.
Dexter looked at her more carefully, and Selene turned her face toward him. "You could stay a few minutes. There’s holiday so I can sleep in an hour or two."
Dexter glanced at the clock again, then he shifted back against the pillow and lifted the edge of the duvet. "Come here."
Dexter said so casually as though there was nothing there.
Selene hesitated as she stared at him for a while only long while.
Dexters expression was casual as though he was asking for nothing serious.
Them slowly, she lay down beside him again, resting her head near his shoulder as her hand settled against his chest. Dexter drew the blanket over them and exuded heat from his body.
"Is this better?"
She nodded. "Yes."
This time, when she moved closer, she was fully awake. And when her arm slipped around his waist again, neither of them pretended it had happened by accident.
Selene’s breathing gradually slowed against his chest.

Dexter looked down to find her eyes closed, her cheek resting comfortably against him. One hand remained curled in his shirt while the other lay beneath the duvet, still loosely holding his. She had fallen asleep again, or was very close to it.

He couldn’t blame her. The warmth flowing between them had settled into a steady rhythm, and for once, the Eternal Winter Ice wasn’t forcing her body to remain tense. Dexter should have been thinking about breakfast. Instead, he watched a loose strand of silver hair move with each breath she took.
His chest tightened and a strange urge began to build within him as he stared at her incredibly beautiful face and smooth healthy silvery hair.
’Beautiful...’
Before he could argue with himself, Dexter lowered his head and pressed a gentle kiss into her hair.

chapters.title: Chapter 285 | Affection Scale
paragraphs: The moment Dexter’s lips kissed her head, Selene body went completely still and so did he. His lips lingered for barely a second before he lifted his head.
For a moment, neither moved. But then, Selene’s shoulders slowly relaxed.
Instead of pulling away like Dexter had expected, her fingers tightened as she played there.
Dexter eyes widened slightly. ’She’s awake.’
The realization made Dexter a bit embarrassed as warmth in his face spread to his ears. He waited, giving her time to say something, but she didn’t.
Instead, her embrace tightened again, and that small movement was enough to make him smile.
His free hand rose to her hair, brushing it gently away from her face to reveal her forehead. Then he leaned down again.
This time, his lips touched her skin.
Selene drew a sharp breath as warmth followed the kiss, stronger than either of them expected.

Selene’s fist holding his cloth tightened even more as the kiss from Dexter’s body surged with intense heat even more hotter than his body as it spread through her body and made her everything tingle.
The eternal winter ice actually trembled as though it had met its nemesis.
Dexter swallowed as he felt Selene squirmed in his embrace making the urge multiply.
Dexter lowered his gaze, and she lifted her face slightly, her eyes still closed, the movement bringing her brow within easy reach.
He gently kissed the space between her eyebrows.
This time, Selene groaned as the heat spread through her forehead, her skin, her tissue, her bones, all the way to her lower body as it tingled like an electric jolt, vibrating through her body.
"You’re bullying me..." Selene said softly as she pressed into his chest.
Dexter lowered his gaze as he looked at her, slowly stroking her hair. "Should I continue?" He asked gently.
Selene remained silent and he waited. Her fingers slowly loosened their desperate hold on his shirt, but she didn’t move away.
Then slowly, she nodded.
Dexter’s expression softened, and he leaned toward her, increasing to kiss even lower this time.
’Bang!’
Something shattered outside the room.
Selene jolted upright while Dexter’s head snapped toward the door, his hearing spreading through the house. It was at the living room and from the hesrtbeat, it was Lyra.
Before he could say anything, Selene was already pushing the duvet aside. "I—I’m going to the bathroom."
"Selene—"

She slipped out of bed, her face flushed and her silver hair slightly tangled, nearly forgetting the small stuffed dragon beside his pillow. She reached back, grabbed it, and hurried toward the door. "I’ll see you at breakfast."
Then she was gone.

Dexter stared after her as the door closed and he slowly leaned back against the headboard, then looked down at the wrinkled patch of his shirt where Selene had been holding him. His mouth curved before he could stop it, and he pressed a hand over his face.
’Calm down.’
That instruction accomplished absolutely nothing.
Nothing helped from overthinking what could have been without the disturbance.
The only thing that took his mind away was the system.
Dexter closed his eyes and called up the system. The notifications he had ignored were still waiting.
Golden lines unfolded before him.
[RELATIONSHIP UPDATE]
[Mira Calloway]
? Affection: 58%
? Current Stage: Budding Love
[Lyra Vance]
? Affection: 65%
? Current Stage: Love
[Selene Frost]
? Affection: 61%
? Current Stage: Love
Dexter stopped breathing for a moment. He read the numbers again, then the words beside them. Love. Budding Love.
His hand slowly lowered from his face, and for a long while, he simply sat there.

He remembered Mira glaring at him on their first night, Lyra watching him with that distant, unreadable expression, Selene flinching whenever he tried to help her. He remembered wondering how the four of them were supposed to survive in the same house.
Now—
"Sixty-five," he murmured. Lyra.
His gaze shifted. "Sixty-one." Selene.
And Mira, who had forced her spectral arms into supporting her legs because she wanted to stand in front of him.
Dexter exhaled slowly. He had suspected but seeing the changes laid out so plainly made something warm and unfamiliar spread through his chest.
A smaller notification appeared.
[Would you like to review the affection scale?]
Dexter accepted, and the panel expanded.
[AFFECTION SCALE]
? Affection measures a person’s emotional attachment to Dexter. It grows through care, trust, shared experiences, and freely made choices.
[0% — Indifference]
No emotional attachment. His presence or absence means little to her.
[1-10% — Interest]
She begins noticing him and becomes curious about him.
[11-20% — Familiarity]
She feels comfortable around him and begins enjoying his company.
She starts relying on him and believes he cares about her well-being.
[31-40% — Fondness]
She cares about his happiness, worries about his safety, and looks forward to seeing him.
[41-50% — Growing Attachment]
His presence becomes important to her. She misses him when he is away and begins developing romantic feelings.
[51-60% — Budding Love]
She seeks closeness and wants to hold a special place in his heart. Her feelings may still confuse or embarrass her.
She recognizes that she loves him, even if she has not said it aloud. She wants to be with him by her own choice.
[71-80% — Deep Love]
She trusts him with her fears and vulnerabilities. She begins imagining a future with him.
[81-90% — Devotion]
Her love becomes a lasting commitment. She willingly supports him through hardship and trusts him to do the same for her.
[91-99% — Profound Love]
She knows his strengths and flaws and continues choosing him. Their bond rests on deep understanding, honesty, and shared commitment.
[100% — Complete Love]
She loves him wholeheartedly and fully commits to their future together. There is no uncertainty about her desire to remain with him.
[SYSTEM NOTE]
? High affection does not mean blind obedience. She retains her own opinions, boundaries, and choices.
? Affection can decrease through neglect, broken trust, or betrayal—even after reaching 100%.
? Each person expresses affection differently. Someone who hides her feelings may love just as deeply as someone who shows them openly.
Dexter’s gaze lingered on the final line. Then he glanced toward the girls room.
A quiet laugh escaped him. "Yes," he murmured. "Some hide it very well."

His attention returned to their names. The girls loved him. Or they were beginning to. He didn’t feel triumphant, he felt happy. And a little frightened by how much their happiness had come to matter to him.
He dismissed the scale only after reading their names one more time, then opened the rewards.

chapters.title: Chapter 286 | Rewards!!!
paragraphs: [Investment Evaluation Complete]
[15 Primary Reward Entries Available]
[Exceptional reward consolidation has occurred.]
Dexter raised an eyebrow. "Consolidation?"
The first panel opened.
[PRIMARY REWARD ONE]
[Recognized Investment]
? Restoring joy, hope, and the desire to live through a shared day of meaningful experiences.
[Reward]
? Ninefold Heaven-Returning Resurrection Pill
? Tier: 9
? Quantity: 1
[Effect]
? Resurrects one deceased individual whose cultivation at death was at the Legend Realm or below.
? Recreates the recipient’s flesh and restores their cultivation to its level before death.
? Restoration is directed toward the designated individual and does not create a duplicate.
[SYSTEM NOTE]
? This exceptional reward occupies five standard reward slots.
? The consolidated reward has already been accounted for. The remaining displayed reward entries are unaffected.
Dexter stared. Then he leaned closer to the golden panel, as though being physically nearer would make the words easier to believe.
Tier 9 pill?
His expression gradually turned to shock and disbelief. "What?"
The word came out as a whisper. He read the description again ans again.

A pill that could resurrect someone. Not heal them before their final breath nor preserve a damaged body long enough for a healer to arrive. It could resurrect them, recreate their flesh and even restore their cultivation. Even if that person had reached the Legend Realm.
Dexter slowly sat upright. The little bedroom suddenly felt much too ordinary for the thing waiting inside his system storage.
His bed was rumpled and one pillow still held the impression of Selene’s head. And somewhere within his reach was a pill that could turn the entire world upside down.
The Ashford family? If news of this pill escaped, the Ashford family would be lucky if the experts rushing toward Stargate City bothered to step around their estates.

Anyone trying to claim ownership would be crushed. Nations would move, ancient powers that had remained hidden for generations would emerge. Someone, somewhere, had lost a master, a parent, an ancestor, a ruler. Someone would be willing to destroy cities for a second chance.
Dexter’s mouth went dry. He had spent years believing certain losses were permanent. For one brief moment, a different thought passed through his mind.
His mother.
He knew almost nothing about her beyond what others had allowed him to hear.
His fingers curled against the duvet, and then he forced himself to breathe. Not now. He didn’t know enough, about the pill, about her death, about what would happen if he acted carelessly.
He needed something of hers if he wanted to resurrect her but he has bithjbv that was hers. The only thing he n ew about her was her tombstone.
His gaze moved toward the option to withdraw the reward. "No.
He dismissed it immediately. The pill would remain inside the system storage. Even the slightest aura can cause problems for him.
The system continued.
[PRIMARY REWARD TWO]
[Recognized Investment]
? Devoting personal time to the well-being and happiness of all three wives.
[Reward]
? Natural Lifespan Extension: 50 Years
? Compressed Cultivation: 10 Years
[Distribution]
? Lifespan extension may be integrated independently.
? Compressed cultivation may be retained until the host selects a suitable integration time.
Dexter’s eyes widened again as he looked toward the first reward’s minimized panel, then back at the second. "Did you finally decide I’ve suffered enough?"
There was no response.
Dexter accepted the lifespan extension, and a gentle warmth settled deep inside him. It was different from mana, there was no violent pressure, no sudden swelling of his meridians.
The lingering tiredness behind his eyes simply eased, and his breathing became clearer. He felt as though something worn inside him had quietly been renewed.
The ten years of cultivation remained stored. He was not going to risk an uncontrolled breakthrough inside a small bungalow. That could wait until he had prepared properly.
[PRIMARY REWARD THREE]
[Recognized Investment]
? Risking your life to recover Lyra from the faction’s retrieval party.
[Reward]
? Blackstone Guardian Puppet
Tier 4
[Combat Realm]
? Transcendent Realm — Initial Stage
[Core Functions]
? Personal defense
? Property protection
? Target interception
? Aura concealment
[Binding]
? Recognizes the host as its sole command authority.
? Can identify designated protected individuals.
? Does not require food, sleep, or ordinary medical treatment.
[LIMITATION]
? Core energy is finite and must be replenished with Nexus monster core of Transcedent level for sustained combat.
? Damage exceeding its self-repair capacity requires external restoration.
Dexter’s eyes narrowed with interest.
A figure appeared within the system’s preview—a tall man in dark armor with a plain, almost unfinished face and a thin silver line running down the center of its chest.
There was no decoration, no grand title carved across its shoulders. It looked like something made for one purpose: protection.
His expression slowly changed, and a smile appeared before sharpening. If that bearded old man returned—
Dexter’s fingers flexed. He would be much better prepared.

Yesterday, he had been forced to endure the terrifying difference between their strength. His techniques, his bloodline, his weapon—he had thrown everything forward and still barely kept himself alive.
Now he had something that could stand on the same battlefield as a Transcendent.
He didn’t know the elder’s exact stage. That mattered. A puppet at the Initial Stage was not an excuse to become careless.

But it was enough to make him breathe more easily. And if the old man intended to casually point another finger at him, he might discover that the boy he bullied yesterday had acquired an unpleasant surprise.
Dexter bound the puppet to himself within the system storage, then marked Mira, Lyra, and Selene as protected individuals. Only after that did he move on.
[PRIMARY REWARD FOUR]
[Recognized Investment]
? Helping your wives imagine a future in which they are wanted, valued, and included.
[Reward]
? Fourfold Hearth Array
? Formation Tier: 5
[Effects]
? Stabilizes ambient mana within a designated residence.
? Allows up to four compatible cultivators to regulate their intake independently.
? Reduces interference between conflicting elemental constitutions.
? Creates a shared warning signal when an enrolled household member experiences a sudden life-threatening disturbance within the array’s range.
[SYSTEM NOTE]
? The formation does not share thoughts or compel emotional attachment.

chapters.title: Chapter 287 | Jasmine Reward
paragraphs: Dexter read that description carefully, then nodded. This was useful.
Fire, ice, and shadow were hardly the easiest combination to accommodate in a small house.

Selene’s condition sometimes affected the entire room. Mira’s temper could raise the temperature just as quickly. Lyra’s shadow energy occasionally gathered in places where it shouldn’t. A formation that allowed each of them to cultivate comfortably without disturbing the others was almost tailor-made for their situation.
His gaze lingered on the warning signal.
Yesterday, finding Lyra’s missing heartbeat had nearly stopped his own. He couldn’t place the whole city inside a household formation, but at home, at least, he could make them safer.
A small square array plate appeared in the preview, its four corners marked with empty circles. Dexter smiled at it. Their house was gradually becoming something much harder to break into.
[PRIMARY REWARD FIVE]
[Recognized Investment]
? Maintaining controlled Heavenly Flame support throughout the night to ease Selene’s Eternal Winter Ice.
[Reward]
? Thunder Manipulation Talent: Advanced by One Rank
Dexter blinked. "Thunder?"

He had spent the night using flame. The system offered no explanation. He considered complaining, then remembered that a system capable of handing him a resurrection pill probably wasn’t interested in his opinion on reward categories.

The upgrade settled into him quietly. A faint spark moved across his knuckles, and he watched it crawl between two fingers without burning his skin. Before, controlling such a small discharge would have required deliberate concentration. Now it felt natural.
Dexter closed his hand. Combined with his saber techniques, this would be troublesome for anyone who made the mistake of treating him as an ordinary Superhuman.
[PRIMARY REWARD SIX]
[Recognized Investment]
? Teaching Lyra How to kiss.
[Reward]
? Kamasutra of Harmonious Union
? Manual Tier: 4
Dexter froze. His expression went through several rapid changes, and then he looked toward the closed bedroom door.
"System."
The panel remained unchanged.
He lowered his voice. "You should be a match maker. "
A short description appeared.
[A manual concerning mutual intimacy, emotional attentiveness, and paired energy harmony.]
[Progress requires willing participation from both individuals.]
Dexter stared at it, then immediately sent the manual into the deepest corner of his storage.
His ears warmed.m with embarrassment. "That one can wait."
[PRIMARY REWARD SEVEN]
[Recognized Investment]
? Providing the care, resources, and encouragement that enabled Mira to stand through her own development of spectral support.
[Reward]
? Meridian Loom Bracelet
? Relic Type: 4
? Quantity: 1 Pair
[Effects]
? Improves fine control of external mana constructs.
? Reduces mana usage by 40%
[SYSTEM NOTE]
? This relic assists mana-supported movement.
? It does not repair paralysis or replace the need for continued recovery.
Dexter’s smile returned immediately. Mira.
He remembered mana gathering around her legs and the concentration on her face.
The way she had risen in front of him. He had been so stunned by the kiss afterward that he hadn’t properly considered how difficult standing must have been for her.
Dexter studied the bracelet. They were thin enough to wear beneath sleeves, with no bulky metalwork that would get in her way.
He could already imagine her reaction a suspicious glare, a complaint about him spending money, and then perhaps that brief look she got whenever something gave her back a little more freedom.
He would give them to her today, well, that was a ithout mentioning the kiss. He valued his life.
The next three panels opened together.
[PRIMARY REWARD EIGHT]
[Recognized Investment]
? Supporting Mira’s chosen festival activity: the roller coaster.
[Reward]
? Skybalance Cushion
? Relic Type: 3
[Effects]
? Adapts to wheelchairs and ordinary seats.
? Reduces harmful jolts and uneven pressure.
? Stabilizes the user during abrupt movement.
Dexter laughed quietly. Mira would pretend it was unnecessary, then she would undoubtedly use it.
[PRIMARY REWARD NINE]
[Recognized Investment]
? Sharing Lyra’s chosen festival activity: the haunted house.
[Reward]
? Dawn Moth Lantern
? Relic Type: 3
[Effects]
? Reveals any changes to one’s consciousness.
Dexter’s smile faded into thoughtfulness. Finally he could know if it was Lyra or Aurelyx for sure.
[PRIMARY REWARD TEN]
[Recognized Investment]
? Ensuring Selene could enjoy her chosen festival activity: Paintball
[Reward]
? Echo Thread Earrings
? Relic Type: 4
[Effects]
? Refines the wearer’s interpretation of reflected sound.
? Reduces interference from overlapping noise.
? Helps distinguish moving objects in crowded environments.
Dexter immediately thought of the festival—hundreds of voices, music, footsteps, the waterfall.
Even with Echolocation, Selene must have needed constant effort to sort through it all.
These earrings wouldn’t restore her sight, but they would make the world less exhausting to navigate.
The final notification appeared beneath them.
[ADDITIONAL LINKED-TARGET REWARD]
[Investment Target]
? Jasmine Constance
[Recognized Response]
? Pride in the host’s publicly witnessed conduct.
[Reward]
? Clearheart Soothing Pill
? Grade: 4
? Quantity: 1
Dexter’s smile slowly disappeared. "Jasmine?"
He stared at the name. "How did I make her proud?"
The system did not explain.
His gaze remained on the panel long after he had finished reading it. Jasmine.

There had been a time when her name alone could change the course of his entire day. Back at the Ashford estate, kindness had been something he learned to accept cautiously. People who showed him too much of it always paid for the mistake. But she had still found ways around it.
For years, the system’s requirement had remained almost entirely unfulfilled, almost.
Dexter’s expression became complicated. He hadn’t thought about her in a while.
He had been busy surviving, cooking, rebuilding walls, and learning how three very different women liked their tea.
Now the past had appeared between his rewards without warning. How should he feel?
By the time Dexter stood up, a few hours had passed.
It was Sunday.
The realization came when Dexter glanced at the date on his phone while tying his apron. Outside, the neighborhood was quieter than usual. A few gates stood open, but there was no weekday rush.
Yesterday had left the whole street tired. Dexter understood the feeling.
He entered the living room first and found the source of the earlier crash—a broken cup sitting in a neat pile on a tray.
Mira was by the window, and Lyra sat on the couch looking far too innocent.
Dexter glanced at the fragments, then at Mira. "Cultivation accident?"
Lyra covered her mouth and replied.
