chapters.title: Chapter 288 | Public Display Of Affection!
paragraphs: Dexter shook his head and decided not to investigate.
He installed the Skybalance Cushion on Mira’s chair before she could ask too many questions, explaining only that it would make sitting more comfortable.
Mira’s suspicious expression changed the moment she settled against it. Her shoulders eased, and then she noticed him watching.
"It’s acceptable."
"Of course."
He also fastened one of the Meridian Loom bracelets around her right wrist and left. The moment her mana touched the relic, her eyes sharpened.
"What is this?"
"Something that might make last night’s technique easier."
Mira’s face turned red.
Dexter immediately raised both hands. "I meant the standing. What were you even thinking?’
Mira’s face turned even redder but she immediately glared at him.
Dexter lips curled upwards as he muttered. "Pervert."
"You!"
Dexter chuckled as he dodged her spectral arm and headed tko the kitchen to cook.
He chose a warm, gentle breakfast rather than anything heavy.
The girls had eaten enough festival food to keep an ordinary family supplied for days. The rice simmered while he prepared a nourishing broth, steamed buns, and a small plate of sliced fruit.
He set aside an extra portion before Lyra could appear and ask whether there was more.
By the time everyone sat down, the house smelled of fresh food and warm tea. Selene arrived last.
She had washed her face and combed her hair, but the moment Dexter looked at her, a faint blush returned. He wisely said nothing about the morning.
Instead, he placed the Echo Thread Earrings beside her cup. "These should help when there are too many sounds around you."
She touched the small box. "For me?"
Dexter nodded.
Selene lifted one earring between her fingers. Her expression softened. "Thank you."
Across the table, Mira looked from the earrings to Dexter, then to Selene’s face, then back to Dexter.
He picked up his spoon. "Let’s eat.
Lyra needed no further encouragement.
Breakfast was peaceful for almost ten minutes.
That was longer than Dexter had expected.
Mira tested the control of her spectral arms while eating, occasionally pausing to look at the bracelets. Selene wore her new earrings and seemed fascinated by the difference they made.
While Lyra entirely concentrated on the food.
By her third bun, Dexter began feeling proud. By her fifth, he was glad he had prepared extra.

When she finally finished, she set her bowl down and stood. Dexter reached for the kettle as Lyra stepped beside his chair. Before he could ask whether she wanted more tea, she leaned down and kissed his cheek.
Dexter’s hand froze around the kettle.
’Thank you for the food.’ Her voice was warm inside his mind.
Then, with her pink cheeks and a determined expression, Lyra walked into the sitting room. She settled on the couch, folded her legs, and closed her eyes—as though nothing unusual had happened.
Dexter slowly lowered the kettle.
Mira was staring. Selene had stopped with her cup halfway to her lips.
The silence stretched, and then Mira’s mouth curved. "You’ve corrupted her already, haven’t you?"
Dexter rolled his eyes. "I fed her breakfast."
"So that is what you’re calling it."
"Mira."
Selene lowered her cup carefully. Her face had turned a little pink too. Dexter looked between them and knew the conversation could become dangerous very quickly.
"Stop it. We need to discuss something serious."
The change in his voice was enough. Mira’s amusement faded slightly, and Selene straightened.

Dexter glanced toward the sitting room where Lyra had already begun cultivating, the familiar movement of mana gathering around her while the Dawn Moth Lantern sat unlit on a nearby shelf. He waited until her breathing settled, then lowered his voice.
"About yesterday."
Mira’s expression turned cold. "I thought you would finally get around to it."
"I should have explained properly last night.
"Yes."
He accepted that without arguing, and then he told them.

Dexter began with the two men—their strength, their interest in Lyra, and the secluded place they had taken her. He explained how he had followed her heartbeat and what happened when he confronted them.
Mira listened without interrupting. That, by itself, told him how angry she was becoming. Selene’s hand tightened around her cup.
When he reached the part about Aurelyx taking control, both women went still.
"She wanted to leave with them," Dexter said quietly. "Lyra didn’t know what was happening."
Mira’s eyes moved toward the sitting room where Lyra remained peaceful on the couch. Dexter continued, describing the stronger elder emerging from the void.
Selene set her cup down before the porcelain could crack in her grip. Frost gathered around its base. "Grandma Lucy?"
"Yeah. She helped stopped them."
Mira’s lips pulled into a cold smile. "The old generation bullying the weak." A faint crimson light gathered around her fingers. "If I were in my prime, I would have made him eat his beard."
Despite himself, Dexter looked at her. She sounded entirely serious.
Selene’s expression was no gentler. "I would have made him grovel." The temperature dropped another degree. "He’ll come back. People like that don’t forget being forced to retreat."
Mira nodded once. "Then we’ll wait."

Dexter stared between them. For a brief moment, he saw something beyond the women recovering in his house. The Crimson Valkyrie. The Eternal Ice Princess. They had once entered dangerous dungeons and faced things most people only saw in news reports.
And right now, they were furious because someone had hurt him.
Warmth spread through his chest. "Try not to look so pleased," Mira said sharply.
Dexter’a smile widened even more and Selene shook her head, but her expression softened slightly.
Then he became serious again. "There’s something else. I don’t want Lyra told about Aurelyx yet."
Mira’s gaze sharpened. "Dexter."
"Listen first."

She fell silent, and he explained the connection between Lyra’s negative emotions and the Shadow Corruption the danger of telling her that someone else could take control of her body without first having something useful to offer her.
Selene looked troubled. "She deserves to know what is happening to her."
"I know." Dexter didn’t look away. "I’m not saying we should hide it forever. I’m saying I need time to prepare."
Mira studied him. "Prepare what?"
"A way to separate them."

chapters.title: Chapter 289 | The Egg
paragraphs: After breakfast, the house settled into a quiet Sunday rhythm.
Selene went to her room to examine her earrings more and Lyra continued cultivating on the couch. Mira returned to her place by the window.
The Primordial Beast Egg rested in a padded basket beside her chair. She looked at it for a moment before lifting it with her spectral arms. The movements were noticeably smoother now.
Dexter watched from the dining room doorway as she settled the egg securely in her lap. The bracelets were already helping.
Mira caught him looking. "What?"
"Nothing."
Dexter smiled and carried the dishes into the kitchen.

He washed slowly, his thoughts moving between the system rewards and the conversation they had just finished. The resurrection pill remained sealed away. The puppet needed a discreet place to stand guard. The Hearth Array would require careful installation. And the ten years of cultivation—
A sharp gasp came from the living room.
Dexter dropped the cloth. "Mira?"
He was through the doorway almost before the plate settled in the sink.
Mira sat rigidly in her wheelchair, her eyes fixed on her lap. Lyra’s eyes opened on the couch at the same moment.
"What happened?" Dexter asked.
Mira didn’t answer. She simply lifted one finger.
Dexter followed it.
A thin line ran across the surface of the egg.
He stopped. The line was no longer than his little finger. But it had not been there before.
For a moment, all three stared.
Then—’Crack.’
A second line appeared.
Lyra was on her feet. She crossed the room so quickly that Dexter barely registered the movement. ’’It’s hatching.’’
Her voice sounded inside his mind, stunned and hopeful.
"Wait," Dexter whispered.
He crouched beside Mira’s chair.
The egg moved. Only slightly. Then two more cracks spread across its shell, branching outward from the first like pale lightning. Four cracks.
Dexter’s heart began pounding. "Selene, come here!"
Footsteps sounded immediately. "What’s wrong?"
"Nothing. Come quickly."
She appeared in the doorway, concern still on her face. Then her echolocation passed over the egg.
Selene stopped. Her lips parted. "Is it...?"
Mira nodded. "It cracked."

Selene approached more carefully now. Through her faint vision, the egg was a pale shape in Mira’s lap. Through reflected sound, she could make out the uneven lines breaking its once-smooth surface. Her hand rose toward it, then stopped.
"Can I touch it?"
Dexter nodded before remembering to answer. "Gently."
Her fingertips brushed the shell.
Something tapped back.
Selene jerked her hand away. Lyra’s eyes widened. Mira leaned forward.
Dexter nearly laughed from sheer surprise. "It moved."
’Of course it moved,’ Lyra said, although her own mental voice trembled. ’There’s something inside.’
"Yes, thank you, Lyra. Very useful observation."
She ignored him completely.
They gathered closer. After months of feeding the egg mana, waiting through its silence, and wondering whether they were doing anything at all, something was finally answering them.
Mira’s spectral arms shifted protectively around it. Dexter immediately held out his hands. "Let’s put it somewhere stable."
Mira looked reluctant to surrender it. He glanced at her lap. "If it comes out with wings, claws, or a terrible attitude, I’d rather it wasn’t sitting directly on you."
Dexter brought the padded basket to the low table and laid a folded towel inside. Mira carefully transferred the egg into it. The shell rocked once, then everything went still.
They waited. A minute passed. Then another.
Lyra leaned closer. ’Maybe it’s tired.’
Dexter listened. Inside the shell, beneath the quiet shifting of mana, a heartbeat fluttered.
His expression softened. "It’s still moving."
Mira looked at him. "You can hear it?"
He nodded. For some reason, that made her grip the armrest more tightly.
Selene sat beside the table, her face turned toward the egg. "Should we give it more mana?"
"Only a little," Dexter said. "Let’s not overwhelm it."
After a few minutes, the egg went silent.
Selene finally exhaled.
"It’s sleeping again."
Lyra stared at her.
Then she stared at the egg.
Her expression became deeply offended.
’It woke us up just to go back to sleep?’
"You were already awake," Dexter said.
’That isn’t the point.’
Mira clicked her tongue, though her hand remained careful beneath the shell.
"Little troublemaker."
Dexter fetched the padded basket they had prepared and placed it on the low table. Mira allowed him to transfer the egg, but only after adjusting the folded cloth beneath it herself.
For a while, all four of them continued watching.
Nothing happened.
Eventually, Selene straightened.
"We shouldn’t force it."
Dexter nodded.
"If it needs more time, we’ll give it more time."
Lyra reluctantly released his sleeve.
Mira looked away first, pretending she had not spent the previous several minutes waiting with the same excitement as everyone else.
"I wasn’t expecting much anyway."
Dexter glanced at her.
"Of course."
Her eyes narrowed.
"Hmph..."
His phone rang before she could decide whether to believe him.
Dexter took it from his pocket and glanced at the screen.
Cole Stanley.
He answered while walking a few steps away from the table.
"Cole."
"Dexter! Am I disturbing you?"
"Only a very important household meeting."
"Oh? Should I call later?"
Dexter looked at the egg.
"No. It’s no problem."
There was a brief silence, and then Cole laughed.
"I won’t ask."
"How have you been?"
"Alive, employed, and beginning to think that assembling six heroes in the same place is more difficult than fighting a monster outbreak."
"That bad?"
"You have no idea."
After a little more conversation, Cole’s tone became more serious.
"We should arrange those training sessions we discussed. The meal was good, but knowing each other’s names won’t stop us from getting in each other’s way during a fight."
Dexter nodded.
He had been thinking the same thing.
A squad needed more than several powerful people standing together. They needed to practice.
"Where?"
"The Titan Training Center. I can reserve a tactical arena there. We’ll begin with formation drills, then run a few simulated battles."
Dexter’s eyes flickered.
The same facility he had visited with Violette.
For a moment, he remembered the reinforced arena, the force of her attacks, and how much had changed since that visit.
"I’ll be free on Monday."
"Tomorrow?"
"Yes. In the afternoon."
"Two o’clock?"
"That works."
"Good. I’ll confirm the booking and send you the details."
After exchanging a few more words, they ended the call.

"If it comes out with wings, claws, or a terrible attitude, I’d rather it wasn’t sitting directly on you."
Dexter brought the padded basket to the low table and laid a folded towel inside.
Mira carefully transferred the egg into it.
The shell rocked once, then everything went still.
Inside the shell, beneath the quiet shifting of mana, a heartbeat fluttered.
For some reason, that made her grip the armrest more tightly.
Selene sat beside the table, her face turned toward the egg.
After a few minutes, the egg went silent.
Then she stared at the egg.
’It woke us up just to go back to sleep?’
Mira clicked her tongue, though her hand remained careful beneath the shell.
Dexter fetched the padded basket they had prepared and placed it on the low table.
Mira allowed him to transfer the egg, but only after adjusting the folded cloth beneath it herself.
For a while, all four of them continued watching.
"If it needs more time, we’ll give it more time."
Mira looked away first, pretending she had not spent the previous several minutes waiting with the same excitement as everyone else.
His phone rang before she could decide whether to believe him.
Dexter took it from his pocket and glanced at the screen.
He answered while walking a few steps away from the table.
There was a brief silence, and then Cole laughed.
"Alive, employed, and beginning to think that assembling six heroes in the same place is more difficult than fighting a monster outbreak."
After a little more conversation, Cole’s tone became more serious.
"We should arrange those training sessions we discussed.
The meal was good, but knowing each other’s names won’t stop us from getting in each other’s way during a fight."
He had been thinking the same thing.
A squad needed more than several powerful people standing together.
I can reserve a tactical arena there.
We’ll begin with formation drills, then run a few simulated battles."
The same facility he had visited with Violette.
For a moment, he remembered the reinforced arena, the force of her attacks, and how much had changed since that visit.
I’ll confirm the booking and send you the details."
After exchanging a few more words, they ended the call.

chapters.title: Chapter 290 | Jasmine’s Visit
paragraphs: When Dexter lowered his phone, Mira’s face was turned toward him.
She said nothing.
Somehow, that made him feel more guilty than a question would have.
Her fingers rested against the arm of her wheelchair, a little too still.
Dexter put his phone away.
"There’s already a protection formation covering the whole house," he said gently. "I’ll check it again before I leave. You’ll be safe here."
Mira’s expression barely changed.
Dexter glanced at Selene and Lyra. Neither was smiling.
"It was Cole," he explained. "My team member. We’re going to practise at a regulated training facility with other registered heroes."
"So trouble requires an invitation now?"
Dexter opened his mouth.
Then closed it.
Given his recent experiences, that was a difficult argument to win.
Lyra’s lips curved. Even Selene looked faintly amused, though her fingers remained wrapped tightly around her cup.
Dexter sighed and moved closer to Mira.
"I’ll be careful."
"You always say that."
There was no accusation in her voice.
That troubled him more.
He crouched beside her wheelchair and rested his hand over hers. Her fingers stiffened beneath his touch before slowly relaxing.
For a moment, she seemed about to pull away.
Instead, she turned her hand beneath his.
"You came back hurt," she said quietly.
Dexter’s smile faded.
"I know," he said.
Her fingers tightened around his.
"Then try to remember it before you get hurt again."
Dexter lowered his head for a moment.
"I will."
She did not tell him she believed him.
But she held his hand a little longer before letting go.
"There’s something else," he said as he stood.
He raised his hand.
Space rippled beside him.
A tall figure appeared between the sofa and the doorway.
Lyra immediately stepped back.
Mira’s spectral arm rose.
A thin layer of frost spread beneath Selene’s cup, and Dexter felt the temperature in the room drop.
"It’s all right," he said quickly. "It belongs to me."
The figure stood motionless.

Its body resembled dark stone shaped into the form of a man, though its joints were too precise and its surface too smooth to belong to any ordinary statue. Faint lines ran beneath its exterior, converging at a dimly glowing mark in its chest.
Its expressionless face tilted upward.
Its eyes opened.
For one brief instant, an oppressive aura filled the room.
Lyra’s breath caught.
Dexter suppressed it immediately, but the silence that followed was different from the one before.
Mira’s hand tightened against her wheelchair.
Selene straightened sharply.
"This is a guardian puppet," Dexter said. "Initial Stage Transcendent."
No one spoke.
Then Mira slowly turned toward him.
"A what?"
"A Transcendent-level guardian puppet."
Normally, that would have earned him an irritated response.
This time, she seemed too stunned to give him one.
Selene cautiously extended her perception toward the motionless figure.
The energy contained within it was immense. Even restrained, it pressed against her senses with a weight that made her withdraw almost immediately.
A Transcendent.
Someone at that level could decide the fate of powerful organizations. Families spent generations trying to nurture a single expert who might one day reach such heights.
Dexter had produced one in their sitting room.
Lyra looked from the puppet to him.
"Does it have a name?"
Dexter blinked.
"Not yet."
She considered the figure again.
"Can it cook?"
He stared at her.
"Would you replace me that quickly?"
Her eyes widened.
"No."
Then, after a moment, she added, "It could help you cook more."
Selene let out a quiet laugh.
Dexter shook his head, but Lyra had already moved closer to him. Her fingers caught lightly at his sleeve.
"And then you could rest sometimes," she added.
His teasing reply died before he could say it.
Lyra was looking at the puppet now, studying its broad shoulders with great seriousness, as though she had just found a sensible solution to something that had been troubling her.
Dexter covered her fingers briefly with his hand.
Mira looked at him.
"So you still won’t tell us who’s backing you?"
Dexter smirked and shrugged.
"Why must someone be supporting me? Can’t I support myself?"
"If you don’t want to tell us, then don’t." Her voice softened slightly. "Just don’t lie."
"I’m not—"
He stopped.
There were things he could say. Pieces of the truth he could offer.
None of them would answer the question she was really asking.
Mira waited.
Dexter looked down at the hand he had held a moment earlier.
"I’m not trying to shut you out," he said.
Something shifted in her expression.
"Then you should know," she replied, "that it sometimes feels that way."
The words were quiet enough that he almost wished she had said them angrily.
Anger, he could tease her out of.
This left him standing there with nothing clever to say.
"I know there are things I haven’t explained," he admitted. "And I know asking you to trust me doesn’t make that easier, but please do."
Mira lowered her spectral arm.
Dexter glanced at all three of them.
"But this will stay here whenever I’m away. Whatever else you’re unsure of, you can be sure that I’ve made arrangements to protect you."
He turned toward the puppet.
"Protect the household."
The mark in its chest brightened.
"Prioritize Mira, Selene, and Lyra."
"Do not pursue an enemy beyond the property if doing so would leave them exposed."
The puppet inclined its head.
"Understood."
Its voice was low and strangely even.
Mira listened to it, then turned back toward Dexter.
"And who stays with you?"
He looked at her.
For a moment, the room was very quiet.
Before he could answer, a knock sounded outside.
Lyra released his sleeve.
Dexter glanced toward the entrance, then instructed the puppet to withdraw its presence and take up a position near the corridor.
As he passed Mira, his fingers brushed her shoulder.
"We’ll finish talking," he said quietly.
She gave a small nod.
Afternoon sunlight lay across the front yard.
Beyond the gate stood a woman holding a paper bag against her chest.
Dexter approached without thinking much of it. His mind was still inside the house, still caught on Mira’s last question.
Then the woman lifted her face.
His hand stopped above the latch.
For several seconds, he could only stare.
She smiled.
It was smaller than the smile he remembered. Uncertain at the edges.
But he knew it.
He had remembered that smile through days when there had been very little else worth remembering.
"Hello, Dexter."
Something tightened painfully in his throat.
"Jasmine?"
She nodded, and her fingers creased the paper bag.
He had imagined seeing her again.
More times than he would ever admit.

In some of those imaginings, he had been successful enough that she would no longer have to worry about him. In others, he had simply been someone who could stand in front of her without feeling ashamed of his worn clothes and empty pockets.
Now she was here.
And he could not think of a single thing to say.
Jasmine had rehearsed several ways to greet him.
On the journey over, she had decided she would be casual. She would ask how he had been, smile, perhaps tease him for becoming famous without telling her.
She had even practised a sentence under her breath.
Every word disappeared when she saw him.
He looked healthier... happier.
There was colour in his face. His shoulders had broadened, and he stood upright without that old, unconscious habit of making himself smaller when someone approached.
She remembered how often he used to step aside before anyone asked him to, how quickly he would apologise, even when the fault was someone else’s.
She had hated that.
Now she searched his face and found something she had wanted for him for so long that, for a moment, her eyes stung.
He looked happy.
The thought warmed her and then, unexpectedly, it hurt.
"Are you going to leave me outside?" she asked softly.
Dexter blinked.
"No. Of course not."
He fumbled with the latch.
The small, awkward movement nearly undid her.
There he was.
For all the changes, there was still something of the boy who had stood on a rooftop with a folded blue sweater in his hands, staring at her as though she had given him something far more precious.
Jasmine stepped through the gate.
For a moment, they stood too close to continue pretending this was an ordinary visit, and too far apart to greet each other as they once might have.
Dexter noticed how tightly she was gripping the bag.
Jasmine noticed that he had forgotten to close the gate.
They both looked away.
"H-how did you find me?" he asked.
"Rachel."
"Rachel?"
"We’re working at the same branch now. She was showing me around, and someone mentioned you. There was something about an incident at Harvest Homes."
His expression shifted.
Jasmine searched his face.
"When I heard your name, I thought there had to be another Dexter."
"Unfortunately, the world only has one of me."
A small laugh escaped her.
His mouth curved in response.
For a few seconds, she could breathe properly again.
She had missed this—the way he could find something foolish to say even when neither of them knew what to do.
Then her gaze moved past him to the house.
There were voices inside.
A woman laughed softly.
Jasmine’s smile faltered before she managed to steady it.
"I hope I haven’t come at a bad time."
"No."
He answered quickly.
Then, more gently, "You haven’t."
She nodded, though she was no longer certain what a good time would have looked like.
Dexter finally closed the gate.
"Come in."
Mira heard his voice before he returned.
She had been listening without meaning to.
At first, there had been silence.
Then a name.
Jasmine.
Dexter had said it so quietly that she might have missed it if the room had not gone still.
Now he was speaking again, and something in his voice made her fingers curl against her palm.
She knew many versions of his voice but this one was unfamiliar. He sounded flustered.
Mira slowly withdrew her hand from the armrest as a moment earlier, she had been holding his.
Dexter entered with Jasmine beside him.
Lyra turned from the corridor, where she had been examining the puppet. Selene lifted her face, her attention settling on the unfamiliar footsteps.
Dexter stopped just inside the room.
The pause was brief.
Mira felt every second of it.
He glanced at his wives, then at Jasmine, suddenly conscious of how much of his life neither side knew.
"This is Jasmine Constance," he said. "We knew each other at the Ashford estate."
The introduction sounded inadequate as soon as he spoke it.
Jasmine had been kind to him when kindness was something he had learned not to expect.
But Mira was sitting only a few steps away, waiting for him to finish speaking. Selene had set down her cup. Lyra was watching him with open curiosity.
He swallowed.
"Jasmine, these are my wives. Mira, Selene, and Lyra."
My wives.
He said it naturally.
That was what hurt.
There was no hesitation in the words themselves. Whatever had unsettled him at the gate, this part of his life was certain.
Jasmine looked at the three women.
She had known he was married.
Rachel had told her. Dexter had told her himself.
She had repeated the fact to herself before coming here, convinced that knowing would be enough but...
Her fingers tightened around the bag.
She had brought something for him.
Now she could hear the paper crumpling in the silence.
"Hello,"

chapters.title: Chapter 291 | I Thought We Might Be Together
paragraphs: "These are my... wives."
Jasmine swallowed the discomfort bubbling deep in her chest and smiled. "It’s nice to meet you."
Mira tilted her head and nodded, Selene muttered "Hello." and Lyra watched the words appear across the lenses of her glasses before giving a small wave.
Then she moved closer to Dexter. She did not take his arm but simply stood beside him.
Jasmine instantly noticed it.
"Please, sit," he said.
Jasmine lowered herself onto the sofa and finally released the paper bag.
There was an awkward silence that was even louder than music in the club and the tension in the air was so thick.
Jasmine cleared her throat and spoke.
"I brought something."
"You didn’t have to."
"I know."
His fingers stilled. Jasmine seemed to realize what she had said at the same moment.
The room remained quiet as she drew out a plain ceramic mug, around which was a knitted sleeve in a warm shade of blue. The knitting was neat except for one slightly uneven row near the bottom.
Dexter stared at it.
"I saw the wool in a shop," Jasmine said. "It reminded me of that sweater. I thought a mug might be more useful now."
He ran his thumb over the uneven stitches. "You still pull the thread too tightly at the corners."
Her lips parted, and then she laughed under her breath. "You remember that?"
"Yeah..."
Dexter smiled, and this time the expression reached his eyes slowly. Mira looked down at her own hand.
Jasmine continued, her voice softening. "The old sweater was too big for you."
"It fit."
"The sleeves covered half your hands."
"It fit," he repeated.

Jasmine stopped arguing. She remembered how fiercely he had insisted on that, how carefully he had folded the sleeves afterward rather than allow her to shorten them. Dexter set the mug on the table carefully.
"Thank you."
"You’re welcome."
Lyra’s gaze moved from the mug to his face, and then she sat down beside him without saying anything.
Dexter went to prepare tea, and Jasmine followed him with her eyes.
"You still count the cups first."
He glanced back. "What?"
"Before putting the water on."
He looked down at the cups arranged beside the kettle, and a faint, almost embarrassed smile appeared. "Old habit."
Jasmine nodded.
At the estate, using too much of anything could become an excuse for punishment, too much water, too much tea, too much time.
Mira’s fingers curled against the edge of her blanket.
Dexter noticed it and immediately changed the subject.
He asked about her work, and she told him about the transfer, the new branch, and how Rachel had somehow introduced her to half the building before lunchtime.
Gradually, the awkwardness eased.
When Dexter brought out a small plate of food, Jasmine took one bite and fell silent. He watched her.
"Well?"
She swallowed, then looked at the plate again. "It’s way better than before."
She took another bite, and her eyes grew bright.
He had once cooked for her using scraps taken from the edges of other people’s meals. He had arranged it carefully, still watched her face while she tasted it.
Suddenly, Jasmine’s gaze fell to the pancake and she smiled. "Do you still eat the crisp pieces," Jasmine said.
Dexter glanced at the browned edge of the small pancake on her plate and shrugged. "Yeah. They do taste better."
"You used to say that about the bread crusts too."
Dexter shrugged and replied. "They also taste better."
"It’s only because everyone else had taken the middle."
The words came out gently, but they hurt anyway.
Selene’s hand stopped around her cup, and for a moment the only sound was the kettle settling in the kitchen. Dexter gave a small shrug.
"I had excellent taste under difficult circumstances."
Jasmine smiled but Mira’s gaze was becoming colder. She had lived with Dexter for months and yet, she didn’t know these things about him.
Mira looked at his hand. ’He’s doing it now.’
She had seen that movement before and thought he was merely thinking.

Across the room, Selene listened to Jasmine speak about a young man who had existed long before Dexter entered their lives. Someone lonely, hungry, and needed kindness as desperately as they later had.
And Jasmine had given it to him. There had been no rare materials or treasures it even then, Jasmine had cared for him when nobody else did.
Selene lowered her face. That morning, Dexter had kissed her forehead, and she had held on to him.

All day, she had carried the warmth of that memory like something precious. Now a small, unwelcome thought crept in: perhaps tenderness came easily to him. Perhaps she had mistaken taken care of for being loved.
Beside Dexter, Lyra wanted to say something but stoppe.
She followed the conversation through her glasses, her hands folded in her lap, and when he shifted to reach for the teapot, she immediately moved to give him room.
Dexter immediately noticed that and his brows furrowed together slightly, but before he could ask, Jasmine spoke.
"You really did it."
Dexter turned toward her. "Did what?"
She looked around the room. "The kitchen. A place of your own."
His gaze followed hers. "Oh."
"You used to talk about it on the roof." A small smile touched her mouth. "A quiet house. Somewhere you can live in peace."
Dexter’s expression softened. "I remember."

Jasmine looked at him for a long moment, then her fingers tightened around her cup. "You always told me you wanted to leave that house." Something in her voice changed. "I thought... when it happened, we would be together. I guess fate has other plans."
The room instantly went dead silent.

Selene’s cup grew cold between her hands, and Lyra looked down before her glasses could finish displaying the sentence. Jasmine seemed to become aware of the room around her all at once, and a flush rose to her face.
"I’m sorry," she said. "That sounded—"
"Jasmine."
Dexter’s voice was gentle. She looked at him.
There were too much history behind a sentence that sounded so simple. After a moment, Jasmine nodded.
"I should let you enjoy the rest of your Sunday. I’ve stayed longer than I intended."
She stood, smoothing her skirt then walked outside the house with Dexter following behind her.
Just as they reached the gate, Jasmine suddenly turned back and gave him a folder.
"I heard you also became an Arcane Chef."

Dexter opened the folder and there were photographs of a small commercial property in another city, rental figures, notes about nearby residential streets, and the contact details of a food supplier. Dexter’s brows drew together.
"I have contacts with the owner," Jasmine explained. "The previous tenant left recently. It isn’t large, but there’s a kitchen space, a front room, and storage at the back."
He studied the photographs. It was modest, clean, a little old-fashioned—the kind of place where someone could begin.
"With your ability, you wouldn’t need a prestigious address immediately," she continued. "Once people tasted your food, they would come."
"Jasmine..."
"I know it would take money. I have some savings. Not enough for everything, but enough to help with the deposit. And I’ve checked the Association vacancies there. A transfer wouldn’t be impossible."
Dexter looked up. "You only just arrived here."
"I know."
Her hands trembled slightly. "I’ve had years to think about what I would do differently if I saw you again."
The place became very quiet.

He asked about her work, and she told him about the transfer, the new branch, and how Rachel had somehow introduced her to half the building before lunchtime.
When Dexter brought out a small plate of food, Jasmine took one bite and fell silent.
She swallowed, then looked at the plate again.
She took another bite, and her eyes grew bright.
He had once cooked for her using scraps taken from the edges of other people’s meals.
He had arranged it carefully, still watched her face while she tasted it.
Suddenly, Jasmine’s gaze fell to the pancake and she smiled.
"Do you still eat the crisp pieces," Jasmine said.
Dexter glanced at the browned edge of the small pancake on her plate and shrugged.
"You used to say that about the bread crusts too."
"It’s only because everyone else had taken the middle."
The words came out gently, but they hurt anyway.
Selene’s hand stopped around her cup, and for a moment the only sound was the kettle settling in the kitchen.
"I had excellent taste under difficult circumstances."
Jasmine smiled but Mira’s gaze was becoming colder.
She had lived with Dexter for months and yet, she didn’t know these things about him.
Mira looked at his hand. ’He’s doing it now.’
She had seen that movement before and thought he was merely thinking.
Across the room, Selene listened to Jasmine speak about a young man who had existed long before Dexter entered their lives.
Someone lonely, hungry, and needed kindness as desperately as they later had.
And Jasmine had given it to him.
There had been no rare materials or treasures it even then, Jasmine had cared for him when nobody else did.
That morning, Dexter had kissed her forehead, and she had held on to him.
All day, she had carried the warmth of that memory like something precious.
Now a small, unwelcome thought crept in: perhaps tenderness came easily to him.
Perhaps she had mistaken taken care of for being loved.
Beside Dexter, Lyra wanted to say something but stoppe.
She followed the conversation through her glasses, her hands folded in her lap, and when he shifted to reach for the teapot, she immediately moved to give him room.
Dexter immediately noticed that and his brows furrowed together slightly, but before he could ask, Jasmine spoke.
"You used to talk about it on the roof." A small smile touched her mouth.
Somewhere you can live in peace."
Jasmine looked at him for a long moment, then her fingers tightened around her cup.
"You always told me you wanted to leave that house." Something in her voice changed.
"I thought... when it happened, we would be together.
I guess fate has other plans."
The room instantly went dead silent.
Selene’s cup grew cold between her hands, and Lyra looked down before her glasses could finish displaying the sentence.
Jasmine seemed to become aware of the room around her all at once, and a flush rose to her face.
There were too much history behind a sentence that sounded so simple.
"I should let you enjoy the rest of your Sunday.
I’ve stayed longer than I intended."
She stood, smoothing her skirt then walked outside the house with Dexter following behind her.
Just as they reached the gate, Jasmine suddenly turned back and gave him a folder.
"I heard you also became an Arcane Chef."
Dexter opened the folder and there were photographs of a small commercial property in another city, rental figures, notes about nearby residential streets, and the contact details of a food supplier.
"I have contacts with the owner," Jasmine explained.
It isn’t large, but there’s a kitchen space, a front room, and storage at the back."
It was modest, clean, a little old-fashioned—the kind of place where someone could begin.
"With your ability, you wouldn’t need a prestigious address immediately," she continued.
"Once people tasted your food, they would come."
Not enough for everything, but enough to help with the deposit.
And I’ve checked the Association vacancies there.
"I’ve had years to think about what I would do differently if I saw you again."

chapters.title: Chapter 292 | If I Was Early, Would You Have Chosen Me?
paragraphs: Inside the house.
The door wasn’t closed properly, and Jasmine’s next words carried through the gap.
"You don’t have to spend the rest of your life within reach of the Ashfords."
Selene turned her face toward the sound. Lyra looked up, and her glasses caught the voices and began displaying their words.
"We could build something elsewhere," Jasmine said. "A business. A proper life."
Dexter lowered his gaze to the photographs—a kitchen, a shop, a way out. Once, he would have accepted before she finished asking. Jasmine saw his silence and leaned forward.
"I know what they did to you. I know the marriage wasn’t your choice."
His expression changed.
"They used you, Dexter."
"Yes."
"They handed you responsibilities and expected you to disappear under them. You were never given a chance to decide what you wanted."
He said nothing. Jasmine swallowed.
"I’m not saying your wives should be abandoned without help. There are arrangements we could make. Carers. Financial support. You could make sure they are comfortable."
Inside the house, Mira’s fingers tightened around the wheel and Selene went still. As Lyra stared at the words on her lenses, her expression changed slightly.
Jasmine’s voice softened.
"But you deserve a life too."
Dexter’s face remained still for a few moments, he looked at the folder without really seeing it.
Then he inhaled and closed it.
"Jasmine... I have a life."
Jasmine’s mouth parted, and he met her eyes. "I was forced into the marriage. But staying with them is my choice."
The words were quiet and there was no one in the room he believed he needed to impress.
Jasmine’s gaze lowered to the closed folder. "You care about them."
"Yes."
"Because they need you?"
Dexter took a breath. "That’s how it began." And he continued.
"At first, I counted everything. The money. The food. The hours. Every problem they brought into my life." A faint, uncomfortable smile touched his mouth. "I wasn’t particularly noble about it."
"But I didn’t know how things began to change."
"How?

Dexter was silent for a moment. He could have spoken about gratitude, about duty becoming affection, but instead several small things came to him: Mira pretending not to watch the door when he returned late, Lyra putting aside the food she wanted most because she thought he had not eaten, Selene sitting beside him in the dark, saying very little, while making it difficult for him to remember what it had felt like to be alone.
"I started wanting to come home," he said.
Jasmine looked up. The answer hurt more than she expected. Dexter rubbed his thumb once against the side of his finger, then deliberately stilled his hand.

Previously, he did things for the system but now, if he sees something Mira would like, he would want to bring it back. When something ridiculous happens, he thinks about telling Lyra. If the weather turns cold, he wondered whether Selene is comfortable." He glanced toward the door. "I think about them even more than I do myself"
Jasmine’s eyes watered as a slow tear rolled down her cheek but she held his gaze.
"I thought you were still waiting."
"For what?"
"For the chance to leave."
Dexter’s expression softened with something painfully close to grief. "I was."
She understood the rest. At some point, he had stopped. And she had not been there when it happened. For a while, neither spoke. Then Jasmine asked the question she had been trying to avoid since.
"If I had come back sooner..." Her voice faltered, "Would you have chosen me?"
A strange lump appeared on Dexter throat and he couldn’t speak.
Jasmine watched his face and saw the struggle he was fighting internally.

In the adjoining room, the girls heard what Jasmine had said and Mira breathing seemed to have been passed by an invisible being, Selene eyes narrowed as she lowered her head, and Lyra’s gaze remained fixed on the words before her.

Dexter could have made it easy. He could have denied the past, claimed that Jasmine had only ever been a friend, turned years of lonely hope into something small enough to dismiss. But she deserved way much better than that. She wasn’t just a random nobody to him, he had thought she was his soul mate once upon a time.
But now...
After a few defines of silence, he swallowed down the lump and spoke.
"Maybe my life would have been different," he said at last.
Jasmine closed her eyes briefly. When she opened them, he was still looking at her.
"But I won’t leave them or make them feel unwanted because of a life that never happened."

Another tear slipped down her cheek, and before Dexter knew it, he almost reached out to wipe it but Jasmine beat him to it as she wiped it away almost impatiently. "I wasn’t trying to make them feel unwanted."
"I know."
"I thought I was offering you freedom."
Dexter’s throat tightened even more and he said with a hoarse voice. "You are."
That made her look at him again. He slid the folder gently back toward her.
Jasmine looked at the photographs visible beneath the clear cover. She had imagined him smiling when he saw them, relief or perhaps even the startled happiness he had shown over a secondhand sweater.
She had not imagined that the dream she carried could arrive too late without becoming worthless. After a moment, she nodded.
"All right."
Dexter’s shoulders lowered slightly. "Jasmine—
"Don’t apologize because you’re happy."
Her lips trembled as she continued.
"Of course I’m happy that you’re happy. That’s the most important thing. I... I just need a little time."
Dexter almost looked down. "All right."
She wiped her cheek again, then gave a small, unsteady laugh. "I should have brought cheaper paper. This feels like a very expensive way to embarrass myself."
"You’ve survived worse."
"So have you."
Their eyes met and for one brief moment, they were back on the rooftop, speaking gentle nonsense to each other.
Then Jasmine ahook her he was and cleared her throat.
"I’m glad you found somewhere you belong," With difficultly, she said.
Dexter remained silent for a while before he spoke. "Thank you."
Jasmine turned away and walked away carrying the folder against her chest. Dexter watched her cross the gate but turned around and did not watch until she disappeared.
He then closed the gate. Some goodbyes needed that much mercy.
When he went inside, Mira was waiting when he came inside, having returned to the sitting room. Dexter stopped.
"Is something wrong?"
"No."
"Then—"
"Come here."
Her voice held none of its usual sharpness. He approached, and before he could ask another question, she reached for him. Her right hand closed around his. Dexter looked down in surprise.

Mira stared at their joined hands. She had faced powerful enemies without hesitation, but for some reason, placing her fingers between his required more courage than she wanted to admit. He turned his hand beneath hers and held it properly.
Neither spoke for several seconds.
When he knew Mira might become uncomfortable, he wanted to release his grip but instead, Mira’s grip tightened for a moment and then she let him go.
Dexter remained beside her a moment longer then he smiled at her before walking toward the kitchen.
Selene stood near the doorway, turning her face toward him as he approached, her pale eyes finding the faint warmth she could distinguish around his shape.
"Selene?"
"It’s all right."
He frowned gently. "What is?"
She hesitated. The words she had prepared seemed too large now that he was standing in front of her. "That she mattered to you."
Dexter became still. Selene lowered her face.

chapters.title: Chapter 293 | Affection Increase
paragraphs: Dexter remained beside Selene a moment longer before walking toward the kitchen.
Selene stood near the doorway, turning her face toward him as he approached, her pale eyes finding the faint warmth she could distinguish around his shape.
"Selene?"
"It’s all right."
He frowned gently. "What is?"
She hesitated. The words she had prepared seemed too large now that he was standing in front of her. "The fact that she really mattered to you."
Dexter became still and Selene lowered her face.
"You don’t have to pretend she didn’t."
He looked at her for a long moment, then reached out and stroked her
"You heard?"
A faint blush spread across her cheeks. "The door didn’t close properly."
Dexter chuckled slightly at the timing of it, but the feeling in his chest was too complicated. Selene didn’t remove her head from his strokes as she whispered.
"You can be sad about it."
Dexter’s expression softened. "I have a lot to be worried about and not much time to be sad."
"I know."
She then quietly asked whether he had eaten enough.
Dexter went to his room. He had barely sat on the edge of the bed when someone appeared at the doorway—Lyra. He smiled.
"Come in."

She crossed the room without her usual mischievous expression. For a moment, he thought she was going to ask about Jasmine. Instead, she sat beside him. The mattress dipped, her shoulder brushed his, and then she leaned over and rested her head against him.
Dexter looked down at her dark hair. "Comfortable?"
She nodded, but she did not speak.
After a while, he relaxed and let his cheek rest lightly against the top of her head. The room was quiet and peaceful.
Eventually, her voice entered his mind. ’Take’
She suddenly gave him her favorite pastries.
Dexter smiled. "Are you sure you want to give it to me?"
Lyra nodded her head. ’Yes.’
Dexter reached for it and took it but it remained stuck in Lyra’s hand before she eventually released it.
’Eat it sparingly.’
"I will."
She settled more comfortably against him, and only then did the system chime.
[AFFECTION INCREASE]
[Mira: Affection +7]
? Previous Affection: 58%
? Current Affection: 65%
? Stage: Love
[Selene: Affection +5]
? Previous Affection: 61%
? Current Affection: 66%
? Stage: Love
[Lyra: Affection +5]
? Previous Affection: 65%
? Current Affection: 70%
? Stage: Love
Dexter looked at the notifications, then at the woman resting against him. A quiet warmth spread through his chest. He dismissed the display.
Lyra shifted. ’What are you smiling about?’
He brushed a loose strand of hair away from her face. "Nothing much. Just looking forward to eating it."
She studied him suspiciously, then her lips curved. ’Me too.’
Across the city, Jasmine sat on a bench outside the Hero Association with the folder on her lap.

She had not gone directly back to home. For a while, she had walked without deciding where to go, and then she had found herself outside the branch building and sat down because her legs felt strangely tired.
She opened the folder once, looked at the photograph of the little shop, and closed it.
She did not hate Dexter. That would have been easier.
She did not even hate his wives as she understood those things better now.
She had arrived holding a piece of his past and assumed that meant there was a place waiting for her in his future.
"Miss Constance?"
Jasmine looked up. A middle-aged man in a dark suit stood several paces away, his posture familiar even before she recognized the small crest on his cuff. Ashford.
Her expression closed. "Yes?"
"My name is Hale. I handle several of the family’s external affairs."
"What do you want?"
Her voice turned frosty as she glared at him. If not for them, the Ashford, Dexter would have been with her, they would have belonged together.
He glanced toward the empty space at the other end of the bench. "May I?"
"I’d rather you told me why you’re here."
The man accepted that without visible offense. "It concerns Dexter."
Jasmine’s fingers tightened around the folder. "What about him?"
"The family has become aware of his recent progress. His registration as a hero. His developing business."
"How fortunate for them."
Hale inclined his head. "I understand your reaction."
"I doubt that."
He did not argue. Instead, he lowered his voice. "There are people within the household who believe the situation was handled poorly.
Jasmine looked at him coldly. "Handled poorly?"
"The family would like an opportunity to speak with him."
"Then call him."
"We suspect he would refuse."
"Perhaps you should consider why."
For the first time, Hale paused. Then he said, "That is precisely why I approached you."
Jasmine almost stood. He continued before she could.
"You knew him before the present difficulties. He may trust you enough to consider a conversation."
"You mean you want me to persuade him to return."
"To help bring him home."
Her gaze sharpened. "He already has a home."
Hale studied her face, then smoothly adjusted. "A reconciliation, then. Whatever form he is willing to consider."
Jasmine said nothing. The man drew a card from his pocket.
"The family would also be willing to recognize those who help repair this misunderstanding. You could benefit from their protection. Your aunt and her children could."
A chill ran through her. "How do you know about my family?"
"Miss Constance, you worked for the Ashfords. There are records."
The answer was mild but that made it worse. Hale continued.
"Your former position could be restored on considerably better terms. A permanent appointment in the household office, if you wished it."
"Over my dead body. I have a job and I worked hard for it and I’m satisfied by it."
His expression became solemn. "No offense was intended."
She did not believe that. Yet she did not walk away, because another thought had taken hold beneath her anger.
Dexter had chosen his life—she had heard him—but choosing his wives did not mean he should spend the rest of that life waiting for the Ashfords to interfere.
If the family could be persuaded to leave him alone...
Hale watched her consider it as he gave her time.
Finally, Jasmine spoke. "If you want to repair anything, you can begin by respecting his decision."
"Of course."
"There’s no condition attached to a meeting."
"Of course."
She looked down at the card without taking it. "
"Just a request to speak," Hale said. "Nothing more."
Jasmine exhaled slowly. It sounded harmless when put that way.
"He’s busy today," she said at last. "Tomorrow maybe. But you should ask first. I’ll speak to him before anything is arranged."
Hale nodded. "Tomorrow then."

chapters.title: Chapter 294 | Mira’s Irritation
paragraphs: Hale placed the card on the empty end of the bench. "Thank you for your time, Miss Constance."
Then he left.
Jasmine watched him walk toward a waiting car. The unease remained.
She picked up her phone and opened Dexter’s contact, her thumb hovering over the screen and hesitated
Then she decided to call later, explain properly, make it clear that she had promised nothing.
Jasmine locked the screen.
At the curb, Hale entered the car and shut the door. The driver did not pull away immediately.
"Did she agree?"
"Not to what we want."
"Then?"
"She confirmed when he’ll be home."
The driver glanced at him through the mirror. "And the formation?"
Hale adjusted his cuff. "There will be no attempt to break it." He looked through the window toward the young woman still sitting outside the Association. "We’ll give him a reason to open the gate."
The car pulled into traffic.

On Jasmine’s lap, the folder shifted beneath her hand. A corner of the shop photograph slipped free. She tucked it back inside carefully. She still wanted to help him. That was what she told herself as she stood.
Tomorrow, she would make certain he understood.

Mira was back at her usual spot by the window. The egg rested in its padded basket on the small table beside her, its four thin cracks unchanged, and she had one hand resting on the basket’s edge. Her eyes were closed.
Dexter knew she was not cultivating. Her breathing was too deliberate.
He stood beside her for a moment before speaking. "Ready for your massage?"
Mira opened her eyes. "Have you finished entertaining your guest?"
Dexter said casually. "Yes."
"Then I suppose you have time."

He looked back at her, but Mira looked out the window. For a moment he considered saying something. Instead, he took her to the room and went to fetch the massage oil, a basin of warm water, and several clean towels.

When he returned, he placed everything within reach and lowered the back of her chair slightly. A folded cushion supported her shoulders, and he adjusted the blanket over her knees before sitting on the low stool in front of her. "Tell me if anything feels uncomfortable."
"You say that every time."
"But you never listen."
She gave him a cool look, and Dexter smiled faintly as he warmed a small amount of the Grade-4 Spiritual Massage Oil between his palms. The familiar herbal scent spread through the room.

He began with her right hand. Her fingers had become much stronger since recovering, no longer lying passively in his grip. When he pressed his thumb gently into her palm, she unconsciously curled them around his.
He paused. Mira immediately relaxed her hand.
Dexter lowered his eyes and worked slowly along her fingers, then her wrist, following the circulation paths described by the 108 Body Massage Sutra.

A thin thread of mana accompanied each movement, controlled enough to avoid disturbing the energy she had gathered during cultivation. The tension around her mouth gradually eased, though she still refused to look at him.
Dexter glanced at the bracelets on her wrist. "How does it feel?"
"Useful."
"That’s almost enthusiastic."
"It helps me hold the spectral arms steady without wasting as much mana."
"That was the intention."
"It also makes you more annoying."
"I don’t think that’s one of its functions."
"It seems to happen whenever you give me something."
His mouth curved. For a few minutes, they settled into the familiar rhythm of his hands moving and her pretending not to enjoy it.

Then Dexter looked toward her legs, and the memory of the previous night returned. Mira standing in front of him. Her spectral arms merging with her legs. The brief, impossible sight of her meeting him without the wheelchair between them. And then the warmth of her lips against his cheek.
His fingers slowed. "Mira."
She opened one eye.
"How long have you been practicing that?"
"Practicing what?"
"Using the spectral arms inside your body."
Her gaze shifted away from him, and that was enough to make his smile disappear. "How long?"
"Since I got them."
Dexter’s hands stopped. For a moment, he simply stared at her. "Since you got them?"
"Yes."
"You’ve been trying to merge a materialized energy construct with your own meridians since the first day?"
Mira’s brows drew together. "You make it sound as though I shoved a spear through my leg."
"That might have been easier to understand."
Her eyes narrowed.

Dexter gently released her hand. "Mira, your meridians were still recovering. Your legs still aren’t responding properly. If you had pushed too much energy through the wrong point, or if the construct had destabilized while it was inside your body..."

He stopped. The possibilities had become unpleasantly clear. Torn meridians. Damage to tissue that was only beginning to recover. An energy backlash she might not have been able to stop. His jaw tightened. "It could have killed you."
Mira looked at him without answering, and that silence made him more frustrated. "And you didn’t think to tell me?"
"I knew what I was doing."
"It could have gone wrong."
Her expression hardened. "I have been controlling mana longer than you."
"And I’ve seen enough people do reckless things to recognize one."
"Careful, Dexter."
"No. You should have been careful."

The room fell quiet. Mira stared at him, and Dexter stared back, his worry sitting too close to anger for him to hide it. Finally, she said, "Did you ask our permission before you brought Jasmine into the house?"
He blinked. "What?"
"You heard me."
"What does Jasmine have to do with this?"
Mira lifted her chin. "Apparently, we’re supposed to consult each other before doing things."
Dexter stared at her for several seconds, then dragged a hand down his face. "She came to the gate."
"And you invited her inside."
"She’s someone I know."
"Yes," Mira rolled her eyes as she said. "We noticed."
Something in her voice made him stop. The irritation in his expression faded a little. "Mira..."
"Don’t use that tone."
"What tone?"
"The one you use when you’ve decided I’m being unreasonable."
"I haven’t decided that."
"You’re considering it."
He sighed. "I’m trying to understand how we went from you risking a cultivation backlash to Jasmine."
Mira’s fingers tightened against the blanket, and she looked toward the window. For several breaths, neither spoke.
Then she said, much more quietly, "You kept looking at her and ignored us completely."

chapters.title: Chapter 295 | Lyra...
paragraphs: Dexter immediately went still at her words.
He sighed and then spoke. "I didn’t mean for her to come. I was surprised."
"I know."
Mira’s voice remained level, but her right hand was gripping the blanket hard enough to crease it.
Dexter looked down at that hand, then reached for it again. She resisted for half a second before letting him take it.
"I’m sorry if I was inconsiderate." he said.
Mira did not look at him.
"And I understand that it was uncomfortable."
"Uncomfortable," she repeated.
He rubbed his thumb gently across her knuckles. "I’m not very good at this."
"That much is obvious."
A faint smile touched his mouth, then disappeared. "But you scaring me and Jasmine arriving are two different things."

Mira finally looked at him. There it was again—the worry. It had been in his voice from the beginning, but she had been too busy defending herself to hear it properly. Dexter leaned forward. "Last night, I was happy you could stand. I still am. But if you had fallen, or if the energy had damaged something..." His grip tightened slightly. "I would rather help you take longer than watch you destroy the chance of recovering because you were practicing alone."
Mira’s expression shifted, and she looked at their hands. "I didn’t force it on the first day."
He waited.
"I started with small sections. Outside the skin. Then along the muscles. I withdrew it whenever the flow became unstable."
"Did it hurt?"
She was silent.
Dexter’s eyes narrowed. "Mira."
"Sometimes."
He closed his eyes briefly, and her fingers moved in his hand.
"I stopped when it hurt."
"Immediately?"
She looked annoyed. "Usually."
"Mira."
"All right. Immediately from now on."
He opened his eyes. "That isn’t enough."
"What else do you want?"
"Tell me before you practice. Let me help you monitor the energy flow. If something goes wrong, I want to be there.
Mira studied him. "You’re not forbidding it?"
"Would you listen to me?"
"I wouldn’t."
"I had suspected."
A little of the stiffness left her shoulders, and Dexter lifted her hand and resumed working gently around her wrist. After a while, she muttered, "I wanted to know whether I could do it myself."
He glanced up, and she was watching the egg. "Stand," she clarified unnecessarily.
His expression softened. "I know."
"And last night..." She stopped, and a faint color crept into her face.
Dexter waited.
Mira immediately glared at him. "Don’t look so pleased."
"I haven’t said anything."
"You’re thinking loudly."

He lowered his head, hiding a smile. A moment later, her heel rested carefully in his palm as he began working along her calf. He kept the pressure gentle, the Shockwave Glove on its lowest useful setting, its faint hum barely audible beneath their breathing.
Mira watched his hands. The muscles were still weak, and he knew better than to confuse the support of a spectral construct with genuine recovery.
But there was warmth now where there had once been persistent cold. Better circulation. Less stiffness around the ankle. Small changes, and he treated them seriously.

Dexter had just finished wiping the remaining oil from Mira’s skin when someone touched his shoulder. He turned to find Lyra standing beside him, her gaze moving to the bottle in his hand, then back to his face.
’My turn.’
Dexter raised an eyebrow. "I didn’t know there was a queue."
She nodded. ’I’ve been waiting.’
Mira snorted. Lyra ignored her and caught Dexter’s sleeve, and there was something almost determined about the gesture.
Lyra tightened her hold.
’Come.’
Dexter understood. She did not want to discuss Jasmine—at least, not now. "All right."
He helped Mira settle comfortably, checked that the egg’s basket was secure, then followed Lyra.
She chose the sofa in his room, where the light was softer and there was enough space for her to stretch out. Dexter placed a clean towel over the cushion. "Shoulders first?"
Lyra nodded and sat with her back toward him. He gathered her hair carefully over one shoulder,
He began at the base of her neck, pressing carefully into the muscles along her shoulders.
The massage technique guided the movement of his mana, and he kept it light, allowing the energy to follow rather than force its way through her circulation.
Lyra’s shoulders gradually lowered. She had been holding more tension than he expected. "Here?"
She nodded.
"Too much pressure?"
A shake of her head.

He worked patiently until the tightness beneath his fingers began to soften. Outside, a cart rattled past the house, and Lyra did not react. Dexter looked at the side of her face, at the glasses resting neatly beside her on the table. He tapped her shoulder lightly before speaking again, making sure she was looking at him. "Tell me if you want me to stop."
Her answer came immediately. ’I don’t.’
"That was very quick."
’I’m certain.’

He smiled. She lay down on her side next, resting her head on the folded towel while he worked along her arm. Her fingers opened and closed lazily when he pressed the center of her palm, and Dexter watched with amusement. "Are you testing whether it still works?"
’I’m checking your work.’
"And?"
’Acceptable.’
He paused. "You’ve been spending too much time with Mira."
Lyra’s shoulders shook with silent laughter, and from the sitting room, Mira called, "I heard that."
Dexter looked toward the door, and Lyra immediately covered her mouth, looking delighted.
For a while, that was how the massage continued. When he reached her calves, he noticed that she kept flexing her feet. "Still tired from yesterday?"
’The haunted house had too much running.’
"You were chasing me."
’You were running.’

Her eyes curved. He shook his head and continued. Compared with Mira, Lyra responded more openly to the relief. Her breathing slowed, her hand slid beneath her cheek, and every now and then a quiet thought reached him.
’But then, a little lower. There. Don’t stop yet.’
He followed each request, watching for fatigue and discomfort.
Eventually, she became so relaxed that her eyes closed, and Dexter lowered the intensity of the glove and finished with her hands again. "You’ll fall asleep if I continue."

chapters.title: Chapter 296 | Selene’s Massage
paragraphs: "Lunch will be late."
Both of her eyes opened as she pouted.
She sat up reluctantly, and Dexter handed her a towel for her hands, then began packing the oil away.
He was tightening the lid when Lyra caught his wrist. "What is it?"
She moved closer.
Before he could guess her intention, she leaned forward and kissed him.
A quick, warm touch her lips settling against his with enough confidence to make him forget the bottle in his hand. Then she drew back.
Dexter blinked and Lyra’s cheeks turned pink, but the smile on her face was unmistakably pleased. ’Thank you.’
He looked at her mouth, then her eyes. "For the massage?"
She nodded.
"That’s a very generous payment."
She tilted her head. ’Do you want me to take it back?’
"How would you—"
She kissed him again, even quicker this time and then she slipped off the sofa before he could recover, and at the doorway she turned and gave him a small wave.
Dexter remained seated with the bottle of massage oil in one hand, and a moment later her voice returned to his mind.
’Don’t forget lunch.’
He laughed under his breath. "How could I possibly?"

He found Selene in the backyard. She sat on the wooden bench near the wall, her hands folded loosely in her lap, a little sunlight touching her silver hair. The day was warm enough for most people, but she still wore a light shawl around her shoulders.
Dexter slowed when he saw her face. Her eyes were open, and she seemed to be watching something above the fence. "What can you see?"
Selene turned toward his voice, and a faint smile appeared. "Green."
He looked at the branches extending over the wall. "The leaves?"
"I think so." The smile grew a little. "They move when the wind blows."

Dexter stood beside her for a moment, looking at something he would usually have passed without noticing. A few leaves. Sunlight between them. Then he sat on the other end of the bench. "Do you need a massage?"
Selene’s fingers tightened together, and her face warmed. She nodded.
Dexter smiled. "You could have asked."
"I knew you were helping the others.
Dexter remained silent and then said.
"Come in." Theb headed inside.
And she laid in her bed.
Selene loosened the shawl from her shoulders and folded it beside her. Dexter warmed the oil before touching her—even through the thin layer of warmth left by the sun, her skin was cool.

He began with her hands. A trace of Abyssal Heavenly Flame accompanied his mana, restrained so carefully that it felt like warmth from a cup rather than the heat of fire. Selene let out a slow breath. "Better?"
"Yes."

He worked along her wrist, then her forearm. The cold inside her resisted—it always did—but the flame held it back, allowing the massage technique to work without the surrounding energy immediately tightening again. Selene’s head lowered.
For several minutes, she said nothing. Dexter thought she might be drifting toward sleep. Then she asked, "How did you meet her?"
His hands slowed. "Jasmine?"
Selene nodded. A leaf scraped softly across the paving stones, and Dexter watched it for a moment before answering.
"We collided in a corridor."
Selene lifted her face slightly. "That was all?"
"I was carrying clean linen. She had a stack of documents. Neither of us was watching properly."
"What happened?"
"Everything went on the floor."
A faint smile touched Selene’s mouth. "Did you get into trouble?"
"I thought I would." His thumb moved slowly along the side of her hand. "I started apologizing before I even knew who I’d hit."
Selene’s smile faded, and Dexter continued in a lighter voice. "She apologized too. Then we both tried to pick up the same papers and made it worse."
"What did she say?"
He hesitated. Selene turned her face toward him, and Dexter looked unexpectedly embarrassed. "She told me I had nice eyes."
Selene was quiet for a moment. Then she asked, "And what did you do?"
"Stared at her like an idiot."
A soft laugh escaped her, and he smiled at the sound. "After that, we kept seeing each other. Small conversations at first. Then she found the place where I went when I wanted to be alone."
"The roof.
He nodded, then remembered and answered aloud. "Yes."
Selene’s fingers rested loosely in his. "She brought you the sweater there?"
"On my birthday." The words came more quietly, and Dexter looked toward the fence. "Nobody usually remembered."
Selene’s expression changed, and he felt her fingers move against his palm. "She did," he continued. "I don’t even know how she found out."
For a while, only the wind moved around them. Selene understood a little more now.
Jasmine had given him something when he had almost nothing. That could not be reduced to jealousy and made to disappear.
"I’m glad someone remembered," Selene said.
Dexter looked at her, and she lowered her head. "I wish more people had."
His throat tightened unexpectedly. He resumed the massage to distract himself.

Selene shifted forward slightly when he moved behind her to work on her shoulders, and the muscles there were tense. He pressed carefully, allowing the warmth to spread before increasing the pressure. She breathed out.
"Is that too much?"
"No." A pause. "Dexter?"
"Yes?"
"Were you always like this?"
"Handsome?"
She turned her head so quickly that he laughed. "Like what?"
"Taking care of people."
He considered. "I don’t know. I liked cooking. It was easier to make something useful than to know what to say."
Selene thought about that, then said, "You say useful things too."
"Occasionally."
His hands slowed against her shoulders, and she continued, almost too softly for anyone else to hear. "When you told me I didn’t have to spend the night cold."
Dexter looked down at her. Selene’s ears had turned pink, and he remembered her in his bed that morning, clinging to him after the first startled moment had passed. "I meant it."
"I know."

chapters.title: Chapter 297 | 50,000,000 Dollars
paragraphs: When the massage ended, Selene sat quietly and he helped her where her clothes again.
Her hand caught the edge of his sleeve, and he looked down.
"Thank you."
Dexter smiled. "Anytime."
Dexter stood up and then left the room to the kitchen.
By the time Dexter entered the kitchen, lunch was overdue. Lyra appeared in the doorway almost at once. He looked at her. "Were you waiting there?"
She shook her head. ’Not... really.’
"So you’ve been waiting."

Dexter chuckled as he opened the cupboards and examined what remained. There were still enough ingredients for several meals, though the neatly stacked containers in the cold-storage compartment were beginning to look less abundant.
He took out rice, vegetables, a portion of beast meat, and the herbs he needed to balance the meal’s mana. Lyra watched him arrange everything.
"Go sit down."
’I can help.’
Dexter was stunned as he gazed into Lyra’s eyes.
No matter how hungry she was, she hadn’t once offered tk help and now, it was a but strange that she was offering to do so.
’What?’ Lyra looked innocently at him with a quizzical look on her face.
Dexter slightly shook his head. "It’s nothing."
Then he handed her a bowl of vegetables. "Wash those."

She accepted the task with seriousness. Dexter sliced the meat thinly and set a pan over the flame. A little oil shimmered across the surface, and the first ingredients struck the heat with a sharp hiss. A rich fragrance filled the kitchen.
Lyra’s attention immediately shifted from the vegetables. "Keep washing."
She pouted but looked back down like a startled cat, making Dexter shake his head. He prepared the meal in stages, controlling the heat with small adjustments of his flame.
The meat browned without becoming tough. The broth thickened gradually, carrying the sweetness of the vegetables and the deeper flavor of the herbs.
He kept the mana gentle enough for the women’s recovering bodies to absorb comfortably.
By the time he carried the dishes out, all three were waiting. Mira looked at the clock and then back at Lyra with a raised eyebrow.
Lyra proudly raised her hands which were a little green from the vegetable washing as she said in their minds. ’I was helping.’
Dexter nodded his head. "Yeah. She helped quite a bit.
That pleased her far more than it should have.
They began eating, and for a few moments the conversation stopped entirely.
Selene took another spoonful before she had fully swallowed the first. Mira noticed and smirked. Selene pretended not to notice that.
Lyra looked at Dexter with shining eyes.
’This is better than yesterday.’
"You said that yesterday."
’Yesterday was also true.’

Dexter laughed. As they ate, he found himself looking around the room. He wanted to get a new house before getting new furnitures to replace the old ones but from the look of things, getting a new house might be impossible.
So it’s just better to get the new furnitures. Dexter then set his cup down.
"There’s something I should tell you."
Mira frowned and immediately looked up. "If it’s another woman, at least give us time to finish eating."
Dexter stared at her. Lyra nearly choked and even Selene’s lips curled to a frown.
Dexter immediately glared at Mira. "Mira...It’s about the house."
Mira’s expression settled. "What about it?"
"I tried to find somewhere larger." The women became still. "Somewhere with more room," he continued.
Selene quitely looked towards Dexter. "What happened?"
Dexter paused, thinking of Harvest Homes, of the money that was basically scammed from him.
He chose his words carefully. "People are intimidated by the Ashfords. Once they know who I am, they become less interested in selling."
Selene’s brows drew together. "They’re afraid of offending them?"
"Yes."
"By selling you a house?"
Dexter’s smile held no humor. "Apparently, allowing us to live comfortably might be interpreted as taking sides."
Mira’s eyes turned cold. For a moment, he thought she would ask for names. Instead, she looked around the room. "A different place would be nice," she said. "But we don’t need one immediately."
Dexter studied her. "The three of you living in a room isn’t that ideal. I wanted to give each one of you your individual space.
Selene shook her head and replied. "It’s no bother."
Lyra spoke. ’It’s alright."
Mira replied.
"I can be patient."
Dexter raised an eyebrow, and she glared at him. "Occasionally."
Lyra nodded in agreement. ’I like it here.’
Dexter looked at her, and she gestured toward the kitchen, then the sitting room, then—with obvious importance—the place where the snacks were stored. He smiled.
Selene placed her spoon down. "The neighborhood is growing on us." Her voice was gentle.
Mira leaned back. "We can move when you find somewhere worth moving to. There’s no need to accept a bad arrangement because we’re impatient."
Dexter looked from one to the other, and a little of the pressure in his chest eased. "All right."
Lyra extended her bowl. ’Can we discuss the next house after another serving?’
He laughed and reached for the pot.

The account balance on Dexter’s phone remained almost offensive. Fifty million dollars. He stared at the number while standing alone in the kitchen after lunch, and beneath it sat the restriction notice.
He had already tried enough times to know that staring harder would not change the situation.
The rebate from giving Kreg money had transformed his balance, and the bank had responded by turning that balance into something decorative.
Dexter tapped the notice again. The same instruction appeared. He would need to resolve the restriction through the bank.
"Of course," he muttered.
He closed the application. Tomorrow.
He would visit the bank and deal with it properly. There was the training session at 2.
Dexter rubbed the back of his neck. Then another unfinished matter came to mind. Two kills.
That was all that remained before the rebate multiplier advanced to 1000 times. His expression changed.
If he had killed those two elders at the festival instead of merely defeating them, the requirement might already have been completed.
He remembered the force of their attacks, the way they had treated Lyra as though she belonged to them, and then the stronger old man stepping out of the void.
Dexter’s jaw tightened. After a moment, he put the phone away. There would be opportunities to fight. The world had been generous with enemies lately.
For now, the women in the next room needed a safer place to cultivate. That was something he could do today.
