chapters.title: Chapter 298 | Setting Up The Array
paragraphs: Dexter brought out the Fourfold Hearth Array during the afternoon. Mira watched the formation plate appear in his hand, and her expression became weary. "What is that?"
"Something useful."
"So you don’t want to tell me..."
He placed the plate on the table. Four faint points of light marked its corners, and between them thin lines formed a pattern that seemed to shift whenever he changed the angle.
Selene tilted her head. " Its a Formation."
Dexter nodded. "It will help reduce interference between our energies."
Lyra moved closer. ’Inside the whole house?’
"That’s the intention."
Mira examined the pattern. "What tier?"
Dexter pondered but then spoke offhandedly.
"Just tier 5."
She looked at him stunned. And after a long silence, she said, "Your mysterious lack of a backer is very generous."
Dexter sighed. "I knew you would say that."
He cleared the center of the sitting room and examined the existing protection formation before placing anything.
The two arrays served different purposes, and he had no intention of weakening the house’s defenses merely to make cultivation more comfortable.
For the next hour, the room became a shared project.
Mira studied the placement of the formation points. Selene listened to the changes in the flow of mana as Dexter adjusted them.
Lyra helped move cushions, carried small items, and repeatedly stopped Dexter from putting furniture where it would interfere with Mira’s chair.
He looked at her after the third correction. "Have you all been discussing my furniture arrangements?"
She nodded. ’They’re bad.’
Mira lips curled upward. Dexter chose not to respond.

He positioned one formation point near the sitting room, another along the corridor, and the remaining two where they could balance the circulation through the bedrooms and backyard. When he returned to the central plate, the four lights had begun pulsing at different intervals. He frowned.
Mira extended a spectral finger toward one of the lines. "That connection is drawing too much from the front of the house."
Dexter examined it. She was right. He adjusted the angle, and the pulse steadied.
"Better," Selene said. "The cold isn’t collecting near the corridor anymore."
He made another small correction, then placed his palm above the central plate and fed a measured stream of mana into it.
Light spread beneath the floor, and for a moment faint lines appeared across the room, reaching toward the four points he had positioned. Then they sank out of sight.
The change was subtle.
A pressure Dexter had become accustomed to without noticing it seemed to ease. Selene inhaled slowly. Mira closed her eyes. Lyra’s expression brightened.
’It’s easier.’

Dexter nodded. His flame no longer pressed so heavily against the colder energy in the house, and Selene’s ice did not spread as readily into the circulation paths the others were using. Each could gather mana without constantly disturbing the others.
Mira opened her eyes. "It works."
Dexter smiled. "Try not to sound surprised."
"I’m surprised you installed it without breaking the floor."
"Must you go against me?"
"Must you argue with me?"
He shook his head, but the satisfaction remained.

They spent the rest of the afternoon testing the formation in short sessions. No dramatic breakthrough occurred, and no one suddenly recovered a lost ability. Yet Selene’s breathing became easier during cultivation. Mira no longer had to pause whenever a colder current crossed her position. Lyra rested beside the egg with a look of contentment that made Dexter quietly pleased.
The egg did not hatch which are Lyra a bit sad.
Evening settled slowly over the neighborhood. Dexter prepared a lighter dinner and made sure everyone ate before returning to cultivation.

Mira complained that he was watching her too closely, and he replied that he was waiting to see whether she intended to put a spectral arm somewhere dangerous. She threatened to put one through his forehead and he glared at her to try it.
Later, while he was washing the last dishes, someone knocked at the gate.
Tessa stood outside carrying a large insulated container, with another resting at her feet. Dexter looked at the containers, then at her. "Are you delivering furniture?"
"Your plates."
"All of them?"
"All one hundred." She smiled brightly.
Dexter picked up the second container and stepped aside. Tessa followed him into the courtyard.
"Perfect. I’ll bring the food early tomorrow."
Tessa leaned slightly to peer past him toward the house. "Busy day?"
"Yes."
"With cooking?"
"Among other things."
Her eyes narrowed with exaggerated suspicion. "What are you busy with?"
Dexter looked at her and knocked her head. "What are you thinking?"
Tessa pouted and glared at him. "I didn’t even say anything!"
Dexter rolled his eyes and then he handed her a small covered portion of the evening meal. She looked down at it. "For me?"
"For your father too."
Her expression became thoughtful. "How much of it has to reach him?"
"All of his portion."
"You’re very strict."
"He knows where I live."
She accepted the container with both hands, then smiled up at him. "If you keep feeding me like this, I’ll start finding reasons to come every night.
"I’ll give you dishes to wash."
"That would ruin the atmosphere."
"What atmosphere?"
"This atmosphere..."
Dexter laughed. "The atmosphere of feeding a stray cat."
Tessa looked offended. "I’m a very pretty stray cat."
"Goodnight, Tessa."
She lingered just long enough to make him repeat it, then waved and walked toward the gate. "Early tomorrow," she reminded him. "Father will be there before the shop opens."
"Alright, I will be there."
Dexter watched her leave, then carried the clean plates into the kitchen. One hundred portions. He looked at the clock and began arranging the ingredients he would need before dawn.
Selene came to his room later that night. Dexter looked up as the temperature near the doorway dropped slightly. She stood with one hand resting on the frame.
"You can come in," he said.
"I know."

But she remained there for another breath before crossing the room. Dexter moved aside on the bed, and she sat beside him, leaving a careful distance between their shoulders. He looked at the gap, then at her. Selene kept her face forward.
"Comfortable?"
"Yes."
He did not believe her. Still, he only offered his hand. She took it.

They settled against the headboard and began cultivating. The new formation helped immediately. The surrounding mana remained steadier, allowing Dexter to direct his attention toward the exchange between his flame and the cold inside Selene. Her fingers gradually loosened in his, then after some time tightened again for an entirely different reason.
She had shifted closer without noticing. Their shoulders touched. Dexter kept his eyes closed. He had noticed. He chose not to mention it.

The hours passed quietly. Now and then, a faint silver mist gathered around Selene’s wrist before dispersing beneath the warmth flowing from his hand. Her breathing remained slow. The house around them settled into sleep.
When Dexter finally opened his eyes, the clock showed one. He turned toward her, and Selene’s head had tilted slightly toward his shoulder. "Selene."
Her eyes opened. "Mm?"
"Lie down."
She straightened at once, and Dexter watched color rise slowly into her face. "We can continue like this," she said.
"We can. But my back is beginning to arch."
"The technique doesn’t require a fixed posture. Which means there’s no reason for us to sit here pretending we’re comfortable."
She lowered her gaze, and he understood what she was remembering.
That morning. His lips against her forehead. The way she had held his shirt and her hurried escape after the crash outside.

chapters.title: Chapter 299 | The Morning
paragraphs: "I’m just asking you to rest."
Selene remained quiet. He loosened his hold enough that she could withdraw her hand if she wanted.
Slowly, her fingers closed around his. "All right."

He moved the pillows and lay down first. Selene followed more slowly. For a few moments, she remained carefully on her side of the bed, with their joined hands stretched between them. Dexter pulled the duvet over her shoulder.
He smiled into the darkness. "You can tell me if you need anything."
Selene nodded her head but neither of them spoke.
Dexter didn’t try to kiss her this time nor did not tease her. After a while, that quiet restraint allowed the last of her nervousness to fade.
"Goodnight," she whispered.
"Goodnight, Selene."
Her breathing slowly deepened. Dexter remained awake a little longer, watching the faint light at the edge of the curtains. Then he closed his eyes.
For several seconds, Dexter eyes snapped open as his biological clock woke him.

Selene was tucked closely against him, her hand was resting on his chest, a loose strand of silver hair lying across his wrist. The room was dark. The house formation maintained a gentle balance around them, and the heat beneath the duvet was mild enough that she slept soundly.

Dexter looked at the clock, then at Selene. He needed to get up. Unfortunately, she had become remarkably effective at making that seem unreasonable. He eased his arm from beneath her shoulders a little at a time. Selene stirred and her fingers caught his shirt.
Dexter froze as she moved closer. He looked toward the ceiling. "Of course," he whispered.
After another patient attempt, he managed to place a pillow where his arm had been.

Selene frowned faintly in her sleep. He drew the duvet more securely around her and left a little warmth in the bedding before standing. At the doorway, he glanced back. She had settled again but eas hugging his pillow.
Dexter quietly closed the door.
The kitchen felt cool when he entered. He washed his hands, tied on an apron, and began. He moved with practiced efficiency, keeping the work quiet enough not to wake the house.
The one hundred meals for the bakery would be Grade One. He was careful about that.

Soon, several pots worked together across the stove. Steam rose as the aroma of seasoned meat and warming grain filled the kitchen. Dexter moved between them, tasting, adjusting, and guiding small threads of flame beneath the pans. The sky outside gradually changed from black to deep blue.
He portioned the first finished dishes while the next batch cooked. Only when the larger batch was nearly complete did he begin the regular Grade-Five meal for his wives.
The new house formation made the work easier.

By the time the first birds began singing love songs, the one hundred meals were packed and the girls’ breakfast remained warm in the kitchen. He cleaned the work surfaces, checked the time, and went to wake Mira.
She opened her eyes before he reached the bed. "Hm..." She groaned as her eyes focused on him.
Dexter stopped and smiled. "Good morning."
She glanced at the time and then back at him as she frowned. "5 more minutes.
Dexter smiled. "Wake up." "Sorry I came early."
Mira’s eyes snapped open as her eyes flashed deviously and she smirked. "Oh... I haven’t noticed."
Dexter blinked his eyes in confusion at her response but then his pupils constricted as he glared at her. "What are you thinking?"
"You obvious know what I’m thinking, why bother asking? Moreover, is it wrong?"
Dexter rolled his eyes and then chuckled. "Why don’t you try me and see?"
Mira looked at him up and then down and spat out. "Pervert."
Dexter helped her sit up, supporting her carefully while she adjusted to being awake.
"For you? Anytime..."
She gave him a flat look. Dexter laughed and carried her to the bathroom before she could say anything else. The water was already warm. He checked it again anyway.
Their morning routine had become familiar, but he never allowed familiarity to make him careless. Mira was quieter than usual.
When he moved her hair away from her neck, she said, "I didn’t practice."
He looked at her. "Last night?"
She nodded. "Not without telling you."
Dexter’s expression softened. "Thank you."
"Don’t make it sound as though I’ve performed some great act of obedience."
"I’m thanking you for taking care of yourself."
She looked away. "You’re irritating."

He smiled and continued helping her wash. There was no rush in his hands, even though the morning had already become busy. When he had finished, he helped her into clean clothes and settled her hair over her shoulders. Mira examined his face.
"What?"
"You look tired."
"I’ve been awake for a while."
"You should rest a while here then."

Dexter laughed softly. She did not. He gave in long enough to sit beside her while she adjusted the blanket across her knees. A minute. Then another. Mira appeared satisfied. Only then did she allow him to bring the wheelchair closer.
By the time they reached the sitting room, Lyra had emerged. Her hair was slightly disordered, and she followed the smell from the kitchen with considerable interest.
Selene appeared shortly afterward. She stopped when Dexter spoke.
"You’re awake."
Her face warmed. "You left."
"Yeah. I had to cook."
"I know."
Lyra looked between them. Selene immediately turned toward the kitchen. Dexter wisely said nothing.
"I’m taking the meals to the bakery," he told them. "I’ll be back shortly, and then we’ll eat."
Mira glanced toward the guardian standing near the corridor. "Go, we will survive."
"I appreciate your courage."
Lyra lifted a hand. ’Will be expecting you.’
He smiled. "Wont be long."
The street was still waking when Dexter reached the bakery. The front shutters remained closed. As arranged, he went around to the side entrance, where Mr. Henry was already waiting.
The older man opened the door and looked at the insulated containers.
"You’ve been busy."
"One hundred portions."
"Come in."
Dexter carried them inside and placed them on the prepared counter. The bakery smelled of fresh dough and warm ovens. Mr. Henry inspected the labels. "Grade One?"
Dexter nodded. "All of these. The grade is marked clearly."
"Good."
They checked the count together. Tessa appeared from the back with her hair tied up, looking far less energetic than she had the previous evening. "You actually came this early."
"You told me to."
"Yeah. Just didn’t expect you to be so early." She grumbled.
Dexter looked at her father. "Is she always like this in the morning?"
"Worse."
Tessa gave them both an offended look.

Dexter laughed and finished arranging the containers. He did not linger—breakfast was waiting at home. After confirming that everything was in order, he said goodbye and left through the side entrance.

There was no rush in his hands, even though the morning had already become busy.
When he had finished, he helped her into clean clothes and settled her hair over her shoulders.
"You should rest a while here then."
He gave in long enough to sit beside her while she adjusted the blanket across her knees.
Only then did she allow him to bring the wheelchair closer.
By the time they reached the sitting room, Lyra had emerged.
Her hair was slightly disordered, and she followed the smell from the kitchen with considerable interest.
Selene immediately turned toward the kitchen.
"I’m taking the meals to the bakery," he told them.
"I’ll be back shortly, and then we’ll eat."
Mira glanced toward the guardian standing near the corridor.
Lyra lifted a hand. ’Will be expecting you.’
The street was still waking when Dexter reached the bakery.
As arranged, he went around to the side entrance, where Mr.
The older man opened the door and looked at the insulated containers.
Dexter carried them inside and placed them on the prepared counter.
The bakery smelled of fresh dough and warm ovens.
Tessa appeared from the back with her hair tied up, looking far less energetic than she had the previous evening.
Just didn’t expect you to be so early." She grumbled.
"Is she always like this in the morning?"
Tessa gave them both an offended look.
Dexter laughed and finished arranging the containers.
He did not linger—breakfast was waiting at home.
After confirming that everything was in order, he said goodbye and left through the side entrance.

chapters.title: Chapter 300 | The Bank
paragraphs: Dexter had already turned down the street when the first customer stopped in front of the bakery. Then a second arrived. Then three more.
By the time Mr. Henry raised the front shutter, a small crowd had gathered. Several faces were familiar from the festival. A man near the front immediately leaned forward. "Is it his food?"
Mr. Henry pointed at the labels. "Grade-One meals. Read before you buy."
"That’s fine."
"One portion first," Tessa added quickly when the man began reaching for several.

Behind him, someone complained. Another person called to a neighbor across the street. The news traveled from one doorway to another with remarkable speed. The young man from the festival was selling his meals.
Inside the bakery, Tessa stared at the growing line, then looked at her father. "One hundred might not be enough."
Mr. Henry was already moving the next container closer. "No," he said. "I don’t think it will."
Dexter, meanwhile, was almost home. He had no idea.
When he entered, Lyra was waiting near the kitchen. He stopped. "Have you been standing there the whole time?"
She shook her head. ’I sat down briefly.’
Dexter looked at her.
Mira looked up from her place by the window. "Youre back."
Selene sat at the table with her hands folded around an empty cup. Dexter washed his hands and began serving breakfast. The Grade-Five meal released a rich fragrance as soon as he lifted the lid.
Lyra’s expression changed immediately. Mira tried to remain composed. Selene inhaled softly. Dexter noticed all three reactions and smiled. "Careful. It’s hot."

He placed Mira’s portion where she could reach comfortably, then served Selene and Lyra before sitting down himself. The first few bites were accompanied by complete silence. He considered that a success.
Warmth spread gradually through the room as the food’s mana began to settle inside them. Mira’s shoulders loosened.
Selene’s fingers no longer felt as cold when she adjusted her cup. Lyra looked at her bowl as though she had made a deeply personal discovery.
’You should cook this again.’
"I haven’t even finished this serving."
’I’m planning ahead.’
Dexter smiled. After breakfast, he prepared their tea.
Once the dishes were cleared, he returned to Mira’s spot with the small stool and folded towels. She looked at him. "You already helped me this morning."
"And now we’re doing your stretches."
"Alright."
He supported her leg beneath the knee and ankle, moving slowly through the familiar range. He watched her face as closely as he watched the limb. Mira watched his hands.

Outside, the neighborhood was becoming louder. Somewhere down the street, several people seemed to be arguing about breakfast. Dexter paid them little attention. He flexed her ankle gently, waited, then eased it back.
"Anything?
"A little tight."
"Here?"
She nodded. He adjusted immediately.
The massage followed, warmer and lighter than the previous afternoon’s session.

Sunlight spread across the floor. Lyra settled on the sofa with her tea and the egg nearby. Selene began a quiet circulation of the seventh-tier technique, the new formation keeping her energy from disturbing the others.
Dexter glanced toward the clock. There was still the bank. The team meeting at two. A crowded day waited beyond the gate.
For the moment, however, Mira’s hand rested on his shoulder as he leaned forward to support her foot. Her fingers moved slightly. He looked up.
"What?"
"Nothing."
But she did not remove her hand. Dexter smiled and returned to the massage. After a while, she asked, "Will you be back before dinner?"
He glanced at her again. "I intend to be."
"Good."
"Any particular reason?"
Mira looked toward the window. "The others will be hungry."
From the sofa, Lyra immediately nodded. Selene smiled into her cup. Dexter lowered his head, hiding the expression on his face.
"Then I’d better make sure I come home."
Dexter finished Mira’s stretches before putting the massage oil away. "Don’t practice the merging technique while I’m gone," he reminded her.
Mira looked at him over the rim of her teacup. "You’ve said that three times."
"Yet, you’re the most stubborn person I’ve ever met."
Mira rolled her eyes cutely.
"Go and attend your meeting."
"The meeting isn’t until two. I need to visit the bank first."
Her eyes narrowed slightly. "What happened?"
"An account restriction. Apparently, they need me to verify some information in person."
"Which information?"
"That’s what I’m going to find out."
Mira continued looking at him, and Dexter smiled before she could ask anything else. "It should be straightforward."
"Just don’t return injured."
"I’ll try not to fight the cashier."
"You think you’re joking.
He laughed, but her expression remained serious. A moment later, her right hand caught his wrist. "Call if there’s a problem."
Dexter raised an eyebrow and looked down at her fingers. What would she do if he called?
But then, he nodded. "I will."
Lyra appeared beside him with a small food container, and he raised an eyebrow. "For me?"
She nodded. ’You forgot to pack something.’
"You’re giving me food?"
Her expression immediately became offended, and Dexter accepted the container before she could change her mind. "Thank you."
’Don’t give it or throw it away.’
"I wouldn’t dare."
Selene stood near the corridor, one hand resting lightly against the wall. "Be careful," she said, her voice quiet but following him all the way to the door. Dexter glanced back at the three of them.
"I’ll be home before dinner."
He checked the guardian puppet’s position once more, confirmed that both formations were functioning properly, and left.
As he settled into the driver’s seat, his phone vibrated with a message from Jasmine. She’d like to see him.
Dexter blinked his eyes and read it twice before replying. ’All right. When would you like to meet?’
Then he put the phone away and started the vehicle.

For now, he needed access to his money. Fifty million dollars was waiting behind a restriction notice, and he had a house to improve, cultivation resources to purchase, and three wives whose recovery would only become more expensive as they progressed.
He had no intention of leaving that amount frozen because someone needed another signature.
The bank was tall but its width not as large.
Its entrance is covered in polished glass. Two uniformed guards stood beside the doors while a discreet detection formation examined everyone who entered. Dexter passed through without difficulty.

Inside, rows of customers waited beneath screens displaying ticket numbers, and a few sat with drinks and packaged breakfasts from the adjoining refreshment counter. Others stood near the service desks, speaking in low voices.
Dexter approached the reception station.
A woman in a dark blazer looked up. "Good morning. How may we assist you?"
"My account has been restricted. The application told me to visit a branch."
"Do you have identification?"
He produced it. She scanned the card, checked the screen, and gave him a ticket. "Customer verification. Counter six."
"Thank you."

Dexter found a seat and waited. A man nearby complained about an international transfer, and across the room an elderly woman argued patiently with a clerk about a charge she insisted had already been reversed. For a little while, Dexter allowed himself to believe his would be ordinary too.

His number appeared on the screen seventeen minutes later, and he approached counter six. The banker seated behind it was a young woman with carefully arranged hair and a neat name badge. She smiled professionally as he sat down.
"Good morning, sir."
"Morning."
